title: Space in article view should page down through content, then advance to next article at the end
description:
Desired behavior: while reading an article, pressing Space pages down through the article body. When already at the bottom of the content, the next Space advances to the next article (scrolled to the top). So holding a reading rhythm on one key: page, page, page, next article, page, page...

Current behavior: Space is bound directly to `handleKeyboardNextUnread` (application.tsx:725, `{ key: " ", handler: handleKeyboardNextUnread, description: "Next unread" }`). It always jumps to the next unread entry immediately, with no paging. Paging exists but is on a separate, less reachable binding: Ctrl+F / Ctrl+B -> `handleContentPageDown` / `handleContentPageUp` (application.tsx:685-701), which scrollBy `clientHeight * 0.9` on `contentScrollRef`.

Implementation sketch:
- New handler (e.g. `handleSpacePageOrAdvance`) replacing the Space binding. Reads `contentScrollRef.current`; if `scrollTop + clientHeight < scrollHeight - threshold`, page down; otherwise delegate to the existing next-entry handler.
- Reuse `handleContentPageDown`'s 0.9 * clientHeight overlap so a line or two of context carries over between pages.
- Reset scroll to top when the new article renders (confirm whether the content pane already does this on entry change).
- Bind Shift+Space to page up / previous article as the mirror. The KeyboardCommand type already supports `modifiers: { shift: true }` and `matchesModifiers` requires an exact match, so Space and Shift+Space can coexist as separate entries.

Traps to handle:
- `scrollBy` uses `behavior: "smooth"`. If the bottom check reads live `scrollTop` while a smooth scroll is still animating, rapid Space presses will misread position and skip to the next article early. Track the intended target offset, or use a settled/instant scroll for this path.
- Iframe view (toggled with `i`) renders third-party content, where scroll position is not measurable cross-origin. Decide the fallback: probably keep the old advance-immediately behavior when in iframe mode.
- Space must keep its existing no-op inside inputs; `isInputElement` in hooks/useKeyboardCommands.ts already guards this, but verify Space in a search box or comment field still types a space rather than paging.
- Space currently means 'next UNREAD' specifically, not 'next entry'. Confirm which one the advance step should use, since j/n use `handleKeyboardNext`.

Acceptance criteria:
- Space pages down within a long article without changing entries.
- Space at the bottom of the content advances to the next article, and the new article starts at the top.
- Space on a short article that fits entirely on screen advances immediately (no dead keypress).
- Shift+Space mirrors the behavior upward.
- KeyboardShortcutsDialog is updated to describe the new Space behavior.
- Vitest coverage for: page-down case, at-bottom advance case, short-article immediate advance, and Space inside an input.

Affected files:
- app/javascript/application.tsx (keyboardCommands list, handlers around lines 685-748)
- app/javascript/hooks/useKeyboardCommands.ts (if the matching logic needs changes)
- app/javascript/components/KeyboardShortcutsDialog.tsx
close_reason: Space now pages down through the article body and advances to the next unread entry only at the end; Shift+Space mirrors upward. Ctrl+F/Ctrl+B share the same paging state. Iframe view keeps immediate advance. Vitest coverage added in useContentPaging.test.ts.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit ba6e7d6: new useContentPaging hook drives Space (page down, then next unread) and Shift+Space (page up, then previous entry); Ctrl+F/Ctrl+B now route through the same hook so both paths share pending-scroll state. Smooth-scroll race handled by paging from the pending target instead of live scrollTop. Iframe view falls through to immediate navigation. EntryContent resets the viewport to the top on entry change. 21 new tests in useContentPaging.test.ts plus a Space-inside-input test in useKeyboardCommands.test.ts; full vitest suite 544 passed.

title: Decide tracking policy for public/icons/ favicon cache (currently 63 untracked files)
description:
Request: commit the untracked public/icons/ directory (63 files, ~967 KB: 28 .ico, 28 .png, 5 .jpg, 2 .svg).

IMPORTANT - read before committing. Evidence says these are a regenerable runtime cache, not source assets:

- app/jobs/fetch_favicon_job.rb writes them. Filenames are `"#{feed.id}#{extension}"` (fetch_favicon_job.rb:32-33), so every name is keyed to a local database primary key. On any other database those IDs point at different feeds, making the committed files wrong rather than merely stale.
- The directory is created on demand via `FileUtils.mkdir_p(ICONS_DIR)` (fetch_favicon_job.rb:52-54), so nothing breaks if it is absent from a fresh checkout.
- UpdateFaviconsJob runs daily at 4am (config/initializers/good_job.rb:16) and rewrites these files, so tracking them produces a permanent stream of modified-binary noise in git status and bloats history with churned binaries.
- The directly analogous cache, /public/audio/cache/, is already gitignored (.gitignore:54), as is /public/assets (.gitignore:31). public/icons/ looks like an oversight in the same list.

Two options:

A. Gitignore it (recommended). Add `/public/icons/` to .gitignore. Favicons repopulate automatically on the next UpdateFaviconsJob run, or immediately via FetchFaviconJob per feed. Confirm the production deploy does not depend on the directory being present in the image at boot (it should not, given mkdir_p), and confirm nothing in config/deploy.yml expects a baked-in icons dir rather than a persistent volume.

B. Commit them as requested. Only makes sense if these should ship as seeded/default icons for a fresh install. If so they should probably not live under a job-writable path at all, since UpdateFaviconsJob will overwrite them; move seeds elsewhere and have the job write to a separate cache dir.

Note: if B is chosen, production also needs a persistent volume or the cache is lost on every container restart, which is a separate concern worth checking either way.

Acceptance criteria:
- A decision recorded on this issue.
- Either .gitignore updated (A) or the files committed with the seed/cache split resolved (B).
- `git status` clean with respect to public/icons after the change.
close_reason:
Already done; the ticket was left open by oversight. No new work.

Andy recorded the decision on 2026-08-17 (Option A, gitignore) with all four evidence points independently verified. The change is in the tree: .gitignore:60-64 carries /public/icons/ with a three-line comment explaining that FetchFaviconJob names each file after a local Feed primary key, that the contents are therefore meaningless against any other database, and that the directory is recreated on demand via mkdir_p and refreshed daily by UpdateFaviconsJob.

Acceptance criteria checked against the current tree on 2026-08-30:
- Decision recorded on the issue: yes, in the 2026-08-17 comment.
- .gitignore updated: yes, line 64.
- git status clean with respect to public/icons: yes. `git ls-files public/icons/` returns 0 tracked files and the 63 cache files raise nothing in `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all`.

The open concern noted in the description and worth carrying elsewhere if it matters: production has no persistent volume for this cache, so favicons are refetched after a container restart until the next UpdateFaviconsJob run at 4am. That is a deploy question, not a tracking-policy one, and it is not a regression.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
DECISION: Option A (gitignore). All four evidence points in the description verified independently:

1. fetch_favicon_job.rb:33 names files by local Feed primary key. Production runs a separate postgres DB (deploy.yml accessories.db), so committed files would be actively wrong there, not merely stale.
2. mkdir_p at fetch_favicon_job.rb:52-54 confirmed; nothing breaks on a fresh checkout.
3. UpdateFaviconsJob runs daily at 4am (good_job.rb update_favicons) and rewrites these files.
4. /public/audio/cache/ (.gitignore:54) and /public/assets (.gitignore:31) are the analogous already-ignored caches.

Additional verification the description asked for:
- ICONS_DIR / public/icons appears in exactly one file repo-wide (fetch_favicon_job.rb). No frontend, seed, fixture, or test references it. Serving is driven by Feed#icon_url from the DB, not by a directory listing.
- config/deploy.yml has no expectation of a baked-in icons dir. No volumes: key; asset_path bridges /rails/public/assets only.
- The files were never tracked (git log --all and git ls-files on public/icons are both empty), so no history rewrite was needed.

Option B rejected: these are not seed assets. They are one user's dev-database cache, and UpdateFaviconsJob would overwrite them anyway.

Two production bugs found while verifying, filed separately:
- ttrb-t2eq: Dockerfile:58 is COPY . . and .dockerignore does not exclude /public/icons, so this dev cache is currently baked into production images and serves wrong icons on ID collision. One-line fix, left out of this issue's scope since .dockerignore was not in the stated scope.
- ttrb-4pk6: cache is ephemeral in production and UpdateFaviconsJob keys off favicon_last_checked rather than file existence, so favicons 404 for up to 7 days after each deploy.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 4640ded: added /public/icons/ to .gitignore with an explanatory comment. git status is now clean with respect to public/icons; git check-ignore confirms both the directory and its contents match .gitignore:60. No Ruby or JS changed, so no test run was warranted.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
DECISION (Andy, 2026-08-18): Option A. Gitignore public/icons/ rather than committing the 63 cached favicon files.

Scope is now settled:
- Add /public/icons/ to .gitignore, alongside the existing /public/assets (line 31) and /public/audio/cache/ (line 54) entries.
- Do not commit the files; they regenerate via FetchFaviconJob per feed and via the daily 4am UpdateFaviconsJob.
- Option B (commit as seeded defaults) is rejected; no seed/cache split needed.

Still worth confirming while in here (does not block A):
- Production has no persistent volume declared for public/icons in config/deploy.yml, so the favicon cache is lost on every container restart and silently re-fetched. Check whether that is acceptable or whether a volume should be added. If it turns into real work, split it into its own issue rather than growing this one.

title: Fresh view is inconsistent: /api/v1/entries filters by date only, /api/v1/counters counts unread+recent
description:
The Fresh virtual folder means two different things depending on which endpoint you ask.

Api::V1::CountersController#index computes virtual.fresh as current_user.user_entries.unread.joins(:entry).where('entries.date_entered > ?', 24.hours.ago) - unread AND recent.

Api::V1::EntriesController#index (view=fresh) applies only where('entries.updated > ?', cutoff); there is no unread filter. #headlines does the same. The frontend (app/javascript/application.tsx around line 200) does not add unread=true for the fresh view either, it only passes fresh_max_age/fresh_per_feed.

So the sidebar badge counts unread recent articles while clicking Fresh lists every recent article including ones already read. The two also disagree on which column they filter: date_entered (counters) vs updated (entries).

Found while making the Playwright suite hermetic: e2e/smoke.spec.ts 'mark all read works' asserted view=fresh returned zero entries afterwards, which the API never did. That spec now queries unread=true instead.

Decide which reading is correct and make counters, entries#index and entries#headlines agree.
close_reason: Fresh is now unread + published within the window across counters, entries#index and entries#headlines; single UserEntry.fresh scope plus shared FreshArticleWindow concern. Commit 200950a.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 200950a: Fresh is now unread + entries.updated within the window everywhere. UserEntry.fresh(cutoff) is the single definition; FreshArticleWindow concern resolves the window for both controllers; counters accepts fresh_max_age and the frontend passes the view's age selector so the badge matches the list. Also fixed a pre-existing 500 in entries#headlines (bare .count over a multi-column select produced invalid COUNT(...) SQL) - it had to work before the agreement test could exercise it.

title: ALLOW_DEV_AUTH does not cover Api::V1::SessionsController, so dev auth alone never renders the reader
description:
Api::V1::BaseController#require_auth falls back to User.first when ALLOW_DEV_AUTH=1. Api::V1::SessionsController does not inherit from BaseController and defines its own require_auth with no such fallback, so GET /api/v1/auth/me returns 401 even with the flag set.

The React app calls /api/v1/auth/me on boot to decide between LoginPage and the reader, so a browser with ALLOW_DEV_AUTH=1 and no session cookie sees the login form while every /api/v1 data endpoint would happily answer. The flag looks enabled but does nothing for anyone driving the UI.

Found while making the Playwright suite hermetic; the E2E fixtures now log in for real (POST /api/v1/auth/login as the seeded admin) rather than relying on the fallback.

Either extend the fallback to sessions#show or drop ALLOW_DEV_AUTH, but the two halves should not disagree.
close_reason: Removed ALLOW_DEV_AUTH; SessionsController inherits BaseController so /api/v1 auth is uniform. Tests sign in for real; added the missing sessions controller test.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit c2d6442: dropped ALLOW_DEV_AUTH entirely rather than extending the fallback.

Api::V1::SessionsController now inherits from BaseController and skips require_auth only for #create, so the two halves cannot disagree again; BaseController#require_auth just 401s. The flag is gone from bin/e2e-server, bin/dev and docs/playwright-testing-guide.md.

Chose removal over extension for two reasons: nothing needs it now that the E2E fixtures log in for real, and an env var that authenticates any request as User.first is a footgun one misconfigured deploy away from account takeover (see ttrb-iob, which gated the same bypass behind this flag in January).

Test-side fallout: the six /api/v1 controller tests got their session from the fallback. They now call sign_in(User.first) in setup. test_helper.rb's sign_in posted to /session, which is not a route, and sign_in_as was an empty stub with a comment admitting it did nothing; replaced with one helper that POSTs to /api/v1/auth/login and asserts the response.

Added test/controllers/api/v1/sessions_controller_test.rb (14 tests) - the controller had none. Includes a regression test asserting /api/v1/auth/me and /api/v1/feeds return identical 401 bodies for an anonymous request.

E2E: the 'Protected routes' block asserted ok() on endpoints its own test names said required authentication. Now parameterised over four paths, checking both the signed-in and the logged-out response.

Verified: Minitest 432 runs / 1280 assertions / 0 failures (was 418/1159), Vitest 550 passed, Playwright 219 passed / 5 skipped, rubocop 184 files / 0 offenses, tsc clean.

title: FeedSidebar does not default new users to expanded categories despite the comment saying it does
description:
app/javascript/components/FeedSidebar.tsx initialises expandedCategories from localStorage and falls back to new Set(categories.map(c => c.id)). At mount the categories prop is still empty (the request has not returned), so a browser with no saved state gets an empty set and every folder renders collapsed, hiding all feeds. The comment above it says 'defaulting to all expanded'.

A related defect in the same effect - it wiped the saved set on every load because the stale-id cleanup ran against the empty categories list - was fixed while making the Playwright suite hermetic (guarded with an early return when categories.length === 0). That restored persistence but not the intended first-visit default.

Fix: on the first run with real categories, expand all of them when localStorage had no saved entry (distinguish 'nothing saved' from 'saved an empty set').
close_reason: First visit with no saved state now expands all categories once the categories request returns; saved empty set still honored

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 66132b8: track whether localStorage held a set at mount (hadSavedExpansionRef); expand all categories on the first effect run with real data when it did not. Also guarded the persist effect so the empty pre-load set is never written. 5 tests added in FeedSidebar.test.tsx; 2 of them fail on the pre-fix component (verified by reverting).

title: Add a global unmocked-fetch guard to test/setup.ts
close_reason: globalThis.fetch guard added to test/setup.ts: records, logs, and throws on an unmocked call, and the existing afterEach fails the test on any recorded URL. Verified against a listener on port 3000 that the request no longer leaves the process. Commit cdc4e92.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit cdc4e92: guard in test/setup.ts replaces globalThis.fetch (global.fetch does not typecheck under this tsconfig). Resolves the silence caveat three ways: records the URL, console.errors it, and throws; the existing afterEach then fails the test on any recorded URL, after cleanup() so DOM teardown still runs. Verified with a TCP listener on 127.0.0.1:3000 and a throwaway test that swallows the rejection: guard off, the listener logs 'GET /api/v1/feeds HTTP/1.1 ... HappyDOM/20.11.2' and the test passes green; guard on, zero connections and the test fails with the URL named. Full suite 28 files / 550 tests before and after, tsc --noEmit clean. Also documented under Mocking Patterns in docs/vitest-rtl-testing-guide.md.

title: next_poll_at intervals that are multiples of 5 min always slip a full cron cycle
description:
Discovered while fixing ttrb-q19b (same class of bug, different guard).

UpdateFeedsJob runs on */5 and selects feeds with next_poll_at <= Time.current. Feed#update_polling_stats! sets next_poll_at = Time.current + interval, where Time.current is the moment the poll *completed*, always a few seconds after the cron tick that scheduled it. Any interval that is a multiple of the 5-minute cron period therefore lands just past the matching tick and waits a whole extra cycle.

Concretely: a feed at Feed::MIN_POLL_INTERVAL (5 min) polled at 22:05:07 gets next_poll_at 22:10:07; the 22:10:02 run skips it and it polls at 22:15, an effective 10-minute interval. Feed::DEFAULT_NEW_FEED_INTERVAL (15 min) becomes 20, and any manual update_interval of 5/10/15/30 minutes is similarly inflated by 5.

Options: select with a small lookahead (next_poll_at <= Time.current + 30.seconds), or subtract slack when computing next_poll_at. Either way the fix belongs in one place so the scheduler and the interval math agree.
close_reason: Scheduler looks Feed::POLL_DUE_SLACK (1 min) ahead of the cron tick, so intervals that are multiples of the 5-minute period no longer wait an extra cycle. Commit 55c5757.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 55c5757: scheduler now compares against Time.current + Feed::POLL_DUE_SLACK (1 min) instead of Time.current. Chose the lookahead over subtracting slack in update_polling_stats! so it also covers the legacy last_updated branch and feeds whose next_poll_at was written by the old code. retry_after deliberately left on the real clock. Tests: 3 new regression tests in test/jobs/update_feeds_job_test.rb (adaptive tick, legacy tick, slack bounds); verified they fail with POLL_DUE_SLACK = 0. Full suite 438 runs, 0 failures.

title: AudioPlayerContext#requestTtsAudio ignores server status "error", leaving the panel stuck in loading
description:
app/javascript/contexts/AudioPlayerContext.tsx requestTtsAudio branches on "generating" and "ready" only. When GET /api/v1/entries/:id/audio replies status "error" (a previously failed GenerateArticleAudioJob), no branch matches, so state stays "loading" and the audio panel spins forever with no message.

useTtsPlayer.ts handles the same response correctly (sets state "error" plus the message); the context is the copy that drifted. Pre-existing; found while adding the "unavailable" status in ttrb-h45v, which had to be handled in both places for the same reason.

Also in that file: the queue pre-generate poll (pollForReady) retries forever on any non-ready status, so a terminal error keeps a setTimeout chain alive for the life of the page.
close_reason: requestTtsAudio and both queue pre-generate polls now treat "error"/"unavailable" as terminal (commit 4601c94); tests added. Follow-ups filed: ttrb-2rmb, ttrb-8txz, ttrb-q7o3.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 4601c94: added isTerminalAudioStatus/terminalAudioMessage helpers; requestTtsAudio now handles "error" on both the initial response and the generating poll (poll interval is cleared), and both queue pre-generate polls (pollForAudio, pollForReady) stop on a terminal status instead of retrying forever. New app/javascript/contexts/AudioPlayerContext.test.tsx covers all four paths; verified the 3 error-path tests fail against the pre-fix branch logic. Full suite 554 passed, tsc clean.

title: KeyboardShortcutsDialog documents 'k / p' as Previous entry but p toggles published
description: In app/javascript/components/KeyboardShortcutsDialog.tsx the Navigation section lists 'k / p' => 'Previous entry', but application.tsx binds p to handleKeyboardTogglePublished (key 'p' in the Actions group) and only k is previous entry. The dialog should list 'k' for previous entry and 'p' for toggle published. Found while updating the dialog for ttrb-gi13.
close_reason: Dialog now matches actual bindings: k = previous entry, p = toggle published

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 17024cb: Navigation now lists 'k' alone for Previous entry; added 'p' => Toggle published under Actions, matching application.tsx bindings. Test updated (KeyboardShortcutsDialog.test.tsx), full vitest suite 555 passed.

title: Fix strict-mode locator violation in e2e/keyboard-navigation.spec.ts:162 (help dialog shortcuts)
description:
Pre-existing deterministic failure found while establishing a baseline for ttrb-549p.

e2e/keyboard-navigation.spec.ts:162 asserts:
  await expect(page.getByText(/previous entry/i)).toBeVisible()

The regex now matches two elements in KeyboardShortcutsDialog:
  1) 'Previous entry'
  2) 'Page up, then previous entry'

Playwright strict mode rejects the multi-match, so the test fails on every run. Not a dependency-update regression; it fails on a clean tree at dd7f68a.

Fix: tighten the locator (exact text, or scope it to the shortcut row) rather than loosening the assertion.
close_reason: Tightened locator to dialog-scoped exact text match. Full e2e suite green at 214 passed / 5 skipped.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Provenance correction (from bdexec orchestrator): this is NOT pre-existing. Verified: commit ba6e7d6 (ttrb-gi13) added KeyboardShortcutsDialog.tsx:21 'Page up, then previous entry', which makes e2e/keyboard-navigation.spec.ts:161 getByText(/previous entry/i) match two elements (line 17 'Previous entry' + line 21) and trip Playwright strict mode. ttrb-ff5l had the suite green at 214 passed immediately prior; ttrb-gi13 ran no browser check and introduced this. The ttrb-549p baseline was taken at dd7f68a, already after ba6e7d6, which is why it read as pre-existing there. Raising to P2 regression; the test_e2e CI job from ttrb-3pyl/ttrb-ff5l would catch this on PR.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit d619360: scoped both navigation assertions in e2e/keyboard-navigation.spec.ts to page.getByRole('dialog') and switched to exact text match ('Next entry' / 'Previous entry'). Verified: 'Help Dialog' block 4/4 passed; full e2e suite 214 passed / 5 skipped in 2.3m, matching the ttrb-ff5l baseline.

title: Sweep loose regex getByText locators in e2e specs that risk strict-mode collisions
description:
ttrb-g973 fixed one strict-mode collision (getByText(/previous entry/i) matching two dialog rows). The same latent fragility exists elsewhere: e2e/keyboard-navigation.spec.ts:175-176 uses unscoped getByText(/toggle read/i) and getByText(/toggle starred/i) - passing today, but any new shortcut description containing either phrase trips strict mode. Other loose regex locators noted in command-palette.spec.ts, filters-labels.spec.ts, settings.spec.ts, error-handling.spec.ts.

Fix pattern established in ttrb-g973 (d619360): scope to a role container and use exact text matching, e.g. page.getByRole('dialog').getByText('Toggle read', { exact: true }). Tighten, never loosen.
close_reason: Tightened 9 loose regex getByText locators to role-scoped exact matches per the ttrb-g973 pattern; 2 numeric row probes anchored. Suite held at 146 passed / 5 skipped before and after. Commit 2a336a7.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit 2a336a7: tightened 9 loose regex getByText locators across command-palette, error-handling, filters-labels, keyboard-navigation and settings specs; left 2 row-scoped numeric probes as anchored regexes (/^\d+ articles?$/, /^\d+\/\d+ matched$/) since they match rendered counts, not fixed copy.

Empirically confirmed via a throwaway probe spec (since deleted) that Radix aria-hides outer dialogs when a nested one opens, so page.getByRole('dialog') resolves to exactly the topmost dialog even with SettingsDialog + the tag dialog both mounted. That made role-scoping safe without hasText filters.

Two locators were asserting on strings that do not exist standalone and passed only on substring match: /toggle read/i (real copy 'Toggle read/unread') and /loading/i (also substring-matches 'Loading tags...' / 'Loading filters...'). Real collision risk was /no tags yet/i, rendered by LabelManager, SuggestedTags and TagEditor.

Baseline and post-change both 146 passed / 5 skipped / 0 failed on the five affected spec files. Filed ttrb-aivz for a defect found in passing: error-handling.spec.ts computes hasLoadingIndicator and never asserts it.

title: Fix ReferenceError in FeedSidebar.tsx:989-990 - undefined handleEditFeed / handleRefresh in tag-group branch
description:
app/javascript/components/FeedSidebar.tsx lines 989-990 call handleEditFeed(feed) and handleRefresh(feed). Neither identifier exists in the module.

  onEdit={() => handleEditFeed(feed)}
  onRefresh={() => handleRefresh(feed)}

The parallel FeedItem render sites at lines 1187-1188 and 1494-1495 use the real names: onEditFeed (a prop) and handleRefreshFeed (defined at line 540). The tag-group branch appears to have been copied without renaming.

Impact: clicking Edit or Refresh on a feed nested under a tag group throws a ReferenceError at runtime. esbuild strips types and does not resolve identifiers, so the build succeeds and this only fails in the browser.

Surfaced by tsc as TS2304 'Cannot find name handleEditFeed' and TS2552 'Cannot find name handleRefresh. Did you mean handleRefreshFeed?' - it is in the 55-error pre-existing typecheck backlog, which is why it went unnoticed.

Acceptance criteria:
- Both call sites use the correct identifiers
- A component test covers edit and refresh on a feed rendered inside a tag group
- TS2304/TS2552 no longer reported for FeedSidebar.tsx
close_reason: Fixed in 091d8a4: tag/smart-folder branch now uses onEditFeed and handleRefreshFeed; 3 regression tests added; TS2304/TS2552 cleared for FeedSidebar.tsx

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit 091d8a4: fixed both call sites (onEditFeed prop, handleRefreshFeed local). Added 'feeds nested inside a smart folder' describe block in FeedSidebar.test.tsx with 3 tests; verified they fail with the original identifiers (ReferenceError: handleEditFeed is not defined / handleRefresh is not defined) and pass after. Full vitest suite 547 passed. tsc backlog 55 -> 53; TS2304/TS2552 gone for FeedSidebar.tsx.

Correction to the issue description: the affected branch is the feed-list virtual folder (smart folder) render at FeedSidebar.tsx:912-997, not a tag group. The nested feeds are those matching Uncategorized / Dead Letter Box.

title: Clear the 55-error tsc backlog and gate typecheck in CI
description:
npx tsc --noEmit currently reports 55 errors on main and always has - the typecheck is not wired into any npm script or CI job, so nothing has ever failed on it. Confirmed identical under both 5.9.3 and 7.0.2 (ttrb-h4cd), so this backlog predates the TypeScript upgrade and was not caused by it.

Breakdown by code:
- 34x TS6133  unused locals/imports (mostly stale 'import React' in .test.tsx files under noUnusedLocals)
- 9x  TS2322  type not assignable, concentrated in test/fixtures/data.ts where optional fields meet required ones
- 3x  TS2339  property does not exist (application.tsx and FilterManager.tsx both read .tags / .tags_with_counts off a Tag[])
- 3x  TS2304  cannot find name (2 are the real runtime bug in ttrb-xmln, 1 is 'global' in api.test.ts)
- 2x  TS2367  string/number comparison with no overlap in EditFeedDialog.tsx
- 1x  TS2740, 1x TS2741, 1x TS2552

Notes:
- The two 'global' errors (app/javascript/lib/api.test.ts:16, test/setup.ts:63) just need @types/node or a switch to globalThis.
- The bulk (34 unused-import errors) is close to mechanical, but do not blanket-suppress: TS2339/TS2367/TS2304 are real defects, one of which is a confirmed runtime crash.

Do this as a few focused commits by error class rather than one sweep.

Acceptance criteria:
- npx tsc --noEmit exits 0 with no new @ts-ignore / @ts-expect-error / any added to get there
- A 'typecheck' npm script exists
- CI runs it (the test_js job is the natural home) so the backlog cannot silently regrow
- npm run test:run still 544/544
close_reason: tsc backlog 55 -> 0 across 7 commits; typecheck npm script added and gated in CI test_js. Two real runtime bugs found and fixed with regression tests: tags API read with the pre-consolidation shape (empty sidebar tag list and autocomplete since 8ef88db), and integer filter enums in the word-cloud tag filter rejected by server-side validation since d2b6edb. Suite 550/550.

title: SuggestedTags shows no loading affordance while fetching entry top_words
description:
SuggestedTags fetched api.entries.info(entryId) behind a loading state that was never rendered - the flag was set and cleared but no consumer read it, so the popover shows an empty word list until the request resolves. The dead state was removed in 60e339e (it was one of the noUnusedLocals errors in ttrb-m0ar); the missing affordance itself is unaddressed.

Decide whether the popover should render a spinner or skeleton while top_words loads, and implement it if so. app/javascript/components/SuggestedTags.tsx
close_reason: Loading pill renders in the suggestions slot while entry top_words loads; also clears stale suggestions on entry switch. 5 new component tests.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 6117024: loading pill (Loader2 + role=status, 'loading suggestions') renders in the suggestions' slot while api.entries.info is in flight. Placed as a ternary against the suggestions map rather than beside it, which also drops the previous entry's words on an entry switch (SuggestedTags has no key at EntryContent.tsx:368, so topWords carries over). New app/javascript/components/SuggestedTags.test.tsx, 5 tests. Full suite 560 passed, tsc --noEmit clean.

title: Remove unused jsdom devDependency (tests run on happy-dom)
description:
Discovered during ttrb-fm6q. jsdom is a direct devDependency but nothing loads it:

- vitest.config.ts:8 sets environment: 'happy-dom' (happy-dom@20.11.2)
- no test file carries a @vitest-environment jsdom docblock
- no import of jsdom anywhere in app/ or test/
- vitest declares jsdom in peerDependenciesMeta as optional, so dropping it does not break the vitest install
- Playwright E2E runs against real browsers, not jsdom

The dependency has been carried since ttrb-3i7, which originally specified environment: 'jsdom'; the config was later switched to happy-dom and the dependency was never removed.

Proposed: npm uninstall jsdom, confirm npm run test:run still reports 28 files / 550 tests, commit.

Alternative if the intent is to keep a jsdom escape hatch for components happy-dom renders poorly: leave it and add a comment in vitest.config.ts saying why, so the next dependency sweep does not spend time upgrading a package nothing loads.
close_reason: Removed unused jsdom devDependency (8a7a13d). Suite held at 30 files / 560 tests before and after, npm ci exit 0, typecheck and both builds exit 0, 38 packages pruned.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit 8a7a13d: removed jsdom from devDependencies; npm install pruned 38 packages from the tree.

Premise re-verified before acting (not taken from the issue text):
- vitest.config.ts:8 is environment: 'happy-dom'
- grep -rIn jsdom across the repo excluding node_modules/lockfile hit only package.json:58 (no @vitest-environment docblocks, no imports, no CI or docs refs)
- vitest/package.json declares peerDependencies.jsdom '*' with peerDependenciesMeta.jsdom {optional:true}, so the install does not need it

Verification, before/after on the same commit:
- npm run test:run: 30 files / 560 tests before, 30 files / 560 tests after, exit 0. (Baseline is 30/560, not the 28/550 in the issue text; the suite grew after this issue was filed. Held fixed across the change.)
- npm ci from the updated lockfile: exit 0, 0 vulnerabilities, then test:run 30/560 again on the fresh tree
- npm run typecheck / build / build:css: all exit 0
- package-lock.json diff is 533 deletions, 0 additions, so nothing else moved

Chose removal over the keep-it-as-an-escape-hatch alternative: no test currently opts into jsdom, and a dep nothing loads costs a re-evaluation on every sweep (it already cost one in ttrb-fm6q). Re-adding it is one npm install if a component ever needs it.

Residual: package-lock.json still contains two 'jsdom' strings at lines 3777 and 3811. Those are vitest's own peerDependencies/peerDependenciesMeta metadata, not an installed package; npm ls jsdom reports empty and node_modules/jsdom is gone.

title: Vite 8 warns vitest.config.ts is loaded as CommonJS (configLoader: native)
description:
Discovered during ttrb-0ixu. The vite 7 -> 8 bump (via @vitejs/plugin-react 6) makes every vitest invocation print:

  (!) Your Vite config uses features that are unsupported by `configLoader: 'native'`, which is planned to become the default in a future major version of Vite:
    - ESM syntax in a file loaded as CommonJS (vitest.config.ts:1:1). Use a `.mjs` extension or set "type": "module" in the closest package.json

Forward-compat notice, not a failure: the suite is green (28 files, 550 tests) and the config loads fine today. It becomes a real break when native config loading turns on by default in a future vite major.

Two fixes, and the choice is a judgement call I did not want to make inside a dependency ticket:

1. git mv vitest.config.ts vitest.config.mts. Narrow, pure rename, no content change. Verified nothing outside .beads/issues.jsonl references the filename (no CI workflow, no npm script, no tooling), so the rename is reference-safe.
2. Add "type": "module" to package.json. Broader blast radius, since it changes how node treats every .js in the project. Only two root config files exist today (vitest.config.ts, playwright.config.ts), both .ts, so it is survivable, but it is not the minimal change.

Do not fix it with VITE_CONFIG_NATIVE_IGNORE_WARNING=true; that suppresses the notice without making the config loadable.

Acceptance criteria:
- npm run test:run emits no configLoader warning
- 28 files / 550 tests still pass
close_reason: Renamed vitest.config.ts -> vitest.config.mts and swapped __dirname for import.meta.dirname (dd88d34). Warning gone from npm run test:run; suite held at 30 files / 560 tests before and after. Rename alone was insufficient: vite's compat check only surfaces the __dirname finding once the file is ESM. Confirmed genuinely loadable via vite's loadConfigFromFile with configLoader: 'native', not just silenced. Filed ttrb-o8x5 for the unrelated broken test:coverage script.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit dd88d34: git mv vitest.config.ts vitest.config.mts, plus __dirname -> import.meta.dirname.

Took option 1 (the rename) over "type": "module", for the reason the issue gives: one file versus reclassifying every .js in the project.

The issue's premise is incomplete, though. The rename ALONE does not clear the warning. Vite's native-config compatibility check (node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js, createNativeConfigCompatPlugin) short-circuits on a CJS file: it reports the esm-syntax-in-cjs finding and returns before running analyzeConfigModuleReferences. Once the file is ESM that early return goes away and the second check runs, which flags free references to __dirname/__filename with '`__dirname` (loc). Use `import.meta.dirname` instead'. vitest.config.ts:24 used __dirname for the @ alias, so a pure rename would have swapped one warning for another. Both changes are in the one commit.

Verification, before/after on the same tree:
- Before: npm run test:run printed the configLoader warning; 30 files / 560 tests pass
- After: npm run test:run prints no warning at all; 30 files / 560 tests pass, exit 0
- Baseline is 30/560, not the 28/550 in the acceptance criteria; the suite grew after this issue was filed. Held fixed across the change.
- npm run typecheck: exit 0 (tsconfig include is app/javascript + test, so the root config was never typechecked either before or after)

Proved the config is actually loadable natively rather than merely quiet, since silencing was the failure mode the issue warned about:
- node --input-type=module -e "await import('./vitest.config.mts')" resolves, alias = { '@': '/home/andy/projects/nibbler/app/javascript' }
- vite's own loadConfigFromFile(..., configLoader: 'native') loads it and returns the same alias

Rename is reference-safe, re-verified rather than taken from the issue text: grep for 'vitest.config.ts' across the repo (excluding node_modules/.git/coverage) hits only .beads/issues.jsonl historical text. CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml:118) runs 'npm run test:run', no filename. No npm script names the file. playwright.config.ts is untouched; Playwright does not go through vite's config loader.

Discovered separately: npm run test:coverage is broken and has been for a while ('Cannot find dependency @vitest/coverage-v8'; only 'vitest' is in devDependencies). Pre-existing, unrelated to the rename. Filed ttrb-o8x5.

Not run: npm run test:e2e (needs a live Rails server, outside this issue's criteria and untouched by this change).

title: SimpleCov config hygiene in test_helper.rb: redundant group/filter redefinition and stale resultset noise
description:
Two pieces of pre-existing SimpleCov noise, surfaced while working ttrb-ll4i. Both cosmetic; neither affects coverage numbers.

1. Redundant config. The SimpleCov 'rails' profile already defines skip %r{\Aconfig/}, skip %r{\Adb/}, and the Controllers/Models/Mailers/Jobs groups. test/test_helper.rb redefines four of those five groups and duplicates two filters. Harmless (groups are a name-keyed hash, filters are additive and idempotent) but misleading to read. Could be trimmed to only the non-default bits: /test/, /vendor/, Services.

2. Stale resultset noise. Every run prints '[SimpleCov]: Excluded 32 result(s) older than merge_timeout (600s)' from leftover parallel-worker resultsets. Either clean coverage/.resultset.json between runs or raise merge_timeout.

Verified baseline at the time of filing: 398 runs / 1083 assertions / 0 failures, line coverage 1607/2745 (58.54%).
close_reason: Trimmed test_helper's SimpleCov block to the two non-default bits (skip /vendor/, Services group) and cleared coverage/.resultset.json in the parent before SimpleCov.start, so each report covers only its own run. Commit cff6dac. Filed ttrb-azer for the parallelize(workers: 1) finding.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit cff6dac.

Both items addressed in test/test_helper.rb.

(1) Redundant config. Trimmed to 'skip "/vendor/"' plus 'group "Services"'. Note the description's suggested keep-list was slightly off: skip "/test/" is also redundant. simplecov-1.1.1/lib/simplecov/defaults.rb:24 loads the test_frameworks profile (skip %r{\A(test|features|spec|autotest)/}) for every SimpleCov.start, and profiles/rails.rb:4 loads it a second time. The rails profile also supplies Channels/Helpers/Libraries groups that the old block never mentioned, so the report's group set is unchanged: 9 tabs before and after.

(2) Stale resultset noise. Fixed by deleting coverage/.resultset.json in the parent before SimpleCov.start (so before any worker forks), not by raising merge_timeout. Raising it is the wrong lever - it makes SimpleCov *include* the stale slices for longer.

That matters because the noise is not purely cosmetic. Reproduced on 09aeec1:
  - stale entries aged past 600s: 'bin/rails test test/models/cached_audio_test.rb' printed the 'Excluded 32 result(s)' warning, 150 / 2793 (5.37%).
  - same file, same stale entries re-stamped to now (i.e. inside merge_timeout): no warning, but the report merged all 32 previous worker slices and claimed 1042 / 2793 (37.30%) off 8 tests.
After the fix, both cases report 150 / 2793 (5.37%).

Also verified under real forking with PARALLEL_WORKERS=4: 33 seeded stale entries dropped, resultset ends with exactly this run's 5 entries, no warning, total identical to the single-process run.

Full suite before/after on the same commit: 454 runs, 1365 assertions, 0 failures, 1865 / 2793 (66.77%). The description's 398/1083 and 58.54% baseline is stale - tests landed between filing and now. rubocop clean.

Filed ttrb-azer: the suite has not actually been running in parallel. Four test classes call parallelize(workers: 1), and Rails' parallelize has no per-class scope - it reassigns Minitest.parallel_executor globally, last call wins - so the whole run goes single-process. Forcing PARALLEL_WORKERS=4 makes 4 image/audio cache tests fail, so the serialization is load-bearing until those are made parallel-safe.

title: Dev favicon cache is baked into production images via COPY . . (wrong icons served)
description:
Discovered while working on ttrb-yjqo.

Dockerfile:58 is `COPY . .` and .dockerignore does not exclude /public/icons (it only excludes /public/assets, line 37). Docker builds from the working tree, not from git, so the untracked public/icons/ files on the build host are copied into every production image regardless of .gitignore.

Why this is wrong, not merely wasteful: FetchFaviconJob names each file `"#{feed.id}#{extension}"` (app/jobs/fetch_favicon_job.rb:33). Production runs against a separate postgres database (config/deploy.yml accessories.db), so those primary keys identify different feeds there. Any ID that happens to collide serves the wrong site's favicon; the rest are dead weight.

Fix: add `/public/icons` to .dockerignore, alongside the existing /public/assets entry. One line, no code change.

Acceptance criteria:
- /public/icons excluded in .dockerignore
- Verify a built image has no /rails/public/icons contents
close_reason: Added /public/icons to .dockerignore (commit 6b94404). Verified before/after on the same tree: pre-fix context contained public/icons, post-fix it does not, so COPY . . can no longer bake the dev favicon cache into production images.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit 6b94404: added /public/icons to .dockerignore.

Verified empirically against the same tree with a throwaway build (nginx:alpine, COPY . /ctx) driven by a Dockerfile outside the context, so the repo .dockerignore applies:
- baseline (git show HEAD:.dockerignore as a per-Dockerfile ignore file): 'FAIL: public/icons present in context'
- after the fix: 'OK: public/icons absent from context'

Since the build context no longer contains public/icons, COPY . . cannot create /rails/public/icons, and the final stage only copies /rails from the build stage. 63 files, ~1.1M, were leaking in.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Filed ttrb-h8eu for the same leak class on /public/audio/cache (latent; dir absent on this host). Left out of this fix to keep the change scoped.

title: Favicons 404 for up to 7 days after each deploy: cache is ephemeral but UpdateFaviconsJob ignores file existence
description:
Discovered while working on ttrb-yjqo.

Two facts combine into user-visible breakage:

1. public/icons/ is not persisted in production. config/deploy.yml has no `volumes:` key (only accessories.db has `directories:`), and asset_path bridging covers /rails/public/assets only. Every new container therefore starts with an empty icons directory.

2. UpdateFaviconsJob selects work purely by timestamp (app/jobs/update_favicons_job.rb:19-21):
   `favicon_last_checked IS NULL OR favicon_last_checked < 7.days.ago`
   It never checks whether the file is actually on disk.

So after a deploy, feeds whose favicon_last_checked is recent are skipped, but their files are gone. Feed#icon_url still points at /icons/<id>.<ext>, which now 404s. Broken favicons persist until the 7-day REFRESH_INTERVAL expires.

Fix options:
- Mount a persistent volume for /rails/public/icons in deploy.yml (keeps the cache across deploys), or
- Have UpdateFaviconsJob also enqueue feeds whose icon_url is set but whose file is missing, or
- Clear icon_url/favicon_last_checked at boot so the daily job repopulates.

The volume is the cleaner fix; the existence check is a useful backstop either way.

Acceptance criteria:
- Favicons survive or are repopulated promptly after a deploy
- Decision recorded on which mechanism was used
close_reason: Mounted a named Kamal volume at /rails/public/icons (with a Dockerfile mkdir as uid 1000 so the volume inherits writable ownership) and added a file-existence backstop to UpdateFaviconsJob so missing icons are refetched regardless of favicon_last_checked. Commit f215df3.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit f215df3: both mechanisms shipped.

Decision: named Kamal volume as the primary fix, file-existence check as the backstop.

1. config/deploy.yml gains top-level volumes: ["nibbler_icons:/rails/public/icons"]. Top-level volumes apply to every app role, so web (serves the files) and job (FetchFaviconJob writes them) share the same volume on 192.168.1.208. Verified with 'bin/kamal config': volume_args renders --volume nibbler_icons:/rails/public/icons. Named volume rather than a host bind mount so no host directory has to be pre-created with the right ownership.

2. Dockerfile creates /rails/public/icons after the COPY, under USER 1000:1000. Required because .dockerignore excludes /public/icons, so the path does not exist in the image; without it Docker creates a root-owned mountpoint and uid 1000 cannot write (silently, since FetchFaviconJob does discard_on StandardError). Verified empirically with a throwaway alpine image mirroring the WORKDIR + COPY --chown layout: /rails stays root-owned, /rails/public is rails-owned so the mkdir succeeds, and a fresh named volume mounts as rails:rails, is writable by uid 1000, and persists across containers.

3. UpdateFaviconsJob now enqueues a feed when it is stale OR when icon_url is set and the file is gone. Path is resolved as FetchFaviconJob::ICONS_DIR.join(File.basename(icon_url)), so a stored icon_url cannot walk outside the icons dir. This is what repairs the current production state on the next cron run, since those feeds have recent favicon_last_checked and missing files.

Tests: new test/jobs/update_favicons_job_test.rb, 7 cases covering never-checked, stale, fresh-with-file, fresh-with-missing-file, blank icon_url, custom favicon, and no site_url. Icon filenames are randomized so parallel workers do not contend. Full suite 405 runs / 1097 assertions / 0 failures; rubocop clean over 181 files.

Discovered and filed: ttrb-i8we (images/audio caches have the same ephemerality with no self-healing path), ttrb-8y5w (favicon filename is stable but served with a 1-year Cache-Control).

title: Same COPY . . leak for public/audio/cache (TTS audio) in .dockerignore
description:
Discovered while working on ttrb-t2eq.

.gitignore excludes /public/audio/cache/ but .dockerignore does not, so the same Dockerfile:58 COPY . . mechanism would bake dev TTS audio into production images. Not leaking today only because the directory does not exist on this build host (verified: the context contained an empty public/audio dir).

CachedAudio::CACHE_DIR is Rails.root.join('public','audio','cache') and filenames come from the cached_audios.audio_filename column, so the files are meaningless against the production database. The production image also has no Python interpreter (see the .dockerignore note on /lib/tts/models), so prod never regenerates them; anything copied in is pure bloat and audio files are large.

Fix: add /public/audio/cache to .dockerignore next to the new /public/icons entry. One line.
close_reason: Already resolved by ttrb-i8we (commit 9b92c54). Verified .dockerignore now has /public/audio/cache at line 45 (alongside /public/images/cache:44, /public/icons:43, /public/assets:37), so the COPY . . leak this issue described is closed. .gitignore also covers all three (lines 54, 58, 64). i8we additionally added the Dockerfile mkdir -p under USER 1000:1000 that the dockerignore exclusion makes necessary, plus a named Kamal volume. No separate change needed.

title: public/images/cache and public/audio/cache 404 permanently after each deploy: rows persist, files do not, nothing repairs them
description:
Same root cause as ttrb-4pk6, but with no self-healing path.

config/deploy.yml now mounts a volume for /rails/public/icons only. CachedImage::CACHE_DIR (public/images/cache) and CachedAudio::CACHE_DIR (public/audio/cache) are still ephemeral, so every new container starts empty.

Unlike favicons, nothing ever refetches:
- CachedImage rows survive the deploy and cached_url keeps pointing at /images/cache/<filename>, which now 404s. ImageCacher only creates rows for uncached URLs (app/services/image_cacher.rb:121); it never checks File.exist? on an existing row.
- CleanupCachedImagesJob deletes orphan FILES that have no row (app/jobs/cleanup_cached_images_job.rb:17-37). It never deletes orphan ROWS whose file is gone, which is exactly the post-deploy state.
- CachedAudio has the same shape: rows point at public/audio/cache, no existence check on read.

Net effect: cached article images and generated audio break permanently at the first deploy after they are cached.

Fix options:
- Add volumes for both paths in deploy.yml (mirrors the icons fix; the Dockerfile must mkdir each dir as uid 1000 so a fresh named volume inherits ownership), and/or
- Have the read paths treat a missing file as a cache miss (delete the row / recache) so the data self-heals.
close_reason: Added Kamal volumes for public/images/cache and public/audio/cache (with Dockerfile mkdir as uid 1000), made ImageCacher and TtsGenerator treat a missing file as a cache miss, taught CleanupCachedImagesJob to purge records with no file and clear the entry's cached_content, and registered that job in the GoodJob cron table (it had never been scheduled). Commits 9b92c54 and 673e38b.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commits 8a4cbd1 (infra) and HEAD (self-heal). Both mechanisms shipped, same shape as ttrb-4pk6.

1. config/deploy.yml gains nibbler_images_cache:/rails/public/images/cache and nibbler_audio_cache:/rails/public/audio/cache alongside the existing icons volume. Verified with 'bin/kamal config': volume_args renders all three mounts. Dockerfile mkdir -p creates all three under USER 1000:1000 so a fresh named volume inherits writable ownership; both new paths added to .dockerignore for the same reason icons is (filenames encode local primary keys, and dev TTS wavs are large), which is also what makes the mkdir necessary. Also added /public/images/cache/ to .gitignore, which was missing (only audio/cache and icons were listed), so dev-cached images were committable.

2. ImageCacher#cache_image: was 'return true if CachedImage.exists?(entry:, original_url:)'. Now finds the record, returns a hit only when File.exist?(cached_path), otherwise destroys it and re-downloads.

3. CleanupCachedImagesJob gains purge_entries_with_missing_files: destroys CachedImage rows whose file is gone and nils the entry's cached_content, so the article falls back to its original remote image URLs. Purges the entry's whole cache rather than only the missing rows, because cached_content rewrites every image in one pass and cannot represent a partial cache.

4. That job was never registered in config/initializers/good_job.rb, so neither direction of the reconciliation had ever run in production. Now scheduled daily at 4:30am, after update_favicons. Verified the entry parses (Fugit.parse) and appears in config.good_job.cron.

5. TtsGenerator#generate now requires File.exist?(existing.cached_path) before serving a cache hit. Correction to the issue text: the audio READ path already self-healed - entries_controller#audio line 131 has checked File.exist?(cached.cached_path) and destroyed the stale record since eba2197 (yesterday, from the TTS-availability work). Only the job/service path was missing the check.

Tests: 6 new cases (2 image_cacher, 3 cleanup_cached_images_job, 2 tts_generator, minus 1 existing test corrected). The old 'skips downloading already cached images' test created a row with no file on disk, which now correctly counts as a miss; it writes the file. Full suite 411 runs / 1120 assertions / 0 failures (was 405/1097). Rubocop clean over 181 files.

Not done: old entries whose images were already lost get repaired to remote URLs, not re-cached. Re-enqueuing CacheArticleImagesJob for every affected entry would mean a large download burst, and with the volume in place this is a one-time repair.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Correction: the commit SHAs are 9b92c54 (infra: volumes, Dockerfile mkdir, dockerignore, gitignore) and 673e38b (self-heal: ImageCacher, CleanupCachedImagesJob, cron entry, TtsGenerator, tests). The 8a4cbd1 in the previous comment is wrong.

title: Refetched favicons stay stale in browsers: /icons/<feed_id>.<ext> is served with a 1-year Cache-Control
description:
config/environments/production.rb:19 sets config.public_file_server.headers = { "cache-control" => "public, max-age=31536000" } for everything under public/.

FetchFaviconJob writes the favicon to a stable path derived from the feed primary key (app/jobs/fetch_favicon_job.rb:33, "#{feed.id}#{extension}"). When UpdateFaviconsJob refetches a changed favicon every 7 days, the bytes change but the URL does not, so any browser that fetched it already keeps the old image for up to a year. Same for the new icons volume: content changes, filename does not.

The 1-year header is correct for /assets (fingerprinted by Propshaft) and wrong for these unfingerprinted paths, which also covers /images/cache and /audio/cache.

Fix options:
- Include a content digest in the favicon filename (and update Feed#icon_url on change), or
- Append a cache-busting query param derived from favicon_last_checked, or
- Serve unfingerprinted public subtrees with a shorter max-age instead of the blanket one.
close_reason: Favicon filenames carry a content digest so refetched icons get a new URL; old file deleted on change. Verified /audio/cache and /images/cache were already immutable-by-name, so the 1-year public/ header stays.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit dd5e053: favicon filenames now carry a 16-char SHA256 of the image bytes (FetchFaviconJob#filename_for), and the superseded file is deleted once icon_url moves (#delete_superseded_icon). Chose the content-digest option over a query param or a shorter max-age because it keeps the URL genuinely immutable, so the 1-year header stays correct.

Audited the other unfingerprinted public/ subtrees named in the report: /audio/cache is already content-addressed (CachedAudio.hash_content in the filename) and /images/cache is URL-addressed with a given entry+URL downloaded exactly once, so neither rewrites a file in place. Left the blanket header alone and documented the precondition in config/environments/production.rb instead.

Added test/jobs/fetch_favicon_job_test.rb (6 tests, none existed before). Full suite: 444 runs, 0 failures. Rubocop clean.

title: Fresh badge counts all fresh articles while the list caps at fresh_per_feed
description:
Follow-on from ttrb-y0na. Counters and entries now agree on what Fresh means (unread + entries.updated within the window) and on the window itself, but the Fresh list also applies fresh_per_feed (default 5 in the UI, app/javascript/application.tsx) which caps how many articles per feed are shown. Api::V1::CountersController#index has no equivalent cap, so with many feeds the badge can read far higher than the number of rows the user sees.

Decide whether the badge should honour the per-feed cap (counters would need the same window-function limiting as EntriesController#limit_per_feed) or whether the cap is purely a display convenience and the badge is correct as-is.
close_reason: Badge now honours fresh_per_feed. The cap is part of Fresh's definition, not display sugar; counters size it with a grouped min() instead of the list's window query, and headlines gained the cap so all three endpoints still agree. Commit 20d0699.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit 20d0699: the badge now honours the cap. Decision was that fresh_per_feed is part of what Fresh means, not display sugar - it is a user selector sitting next to the age selector, and ttrb-y0na already established that the badge tracks the selector-defined view.

Counters do not run the list's window query. Keeping the top N per feed keeps min(rows_in_feed, N) from every feed regardless of how rows rank inside it, so UserEntry.count_per_feed_capped groups by feed_id and sums the minimum: exact, one query, no id pluck.

entries#headlines got the cap as well (via .where(id: UserEntry.top_per_feed_ids(...))). Without it, headlines would have become the one endpoint of the three disagreeing about Fresh, which is exactly what y0na closed.

Refactors: the ROW_NUMBER ranking moved out of EntriesController#limit_per_feed into UserEntry.top_per_feed_ids next to the fresh scope; param parsing moved into FreshArticleWindow#fresh_per_feed_limit so all three endpoints read fresh_per_feed identically (absent or non-positive means no cap, matching the list's inf option). Frontend passes freshPerFeed to api.counters.get and reloads counters when it changes.

Tests: 2 new counters cases (exact cap arithmetic on a fixture-free user; counters/entries/headlines agreement under caps of 1 and 2), plus the existing agreement test refactored onto a shared fresh_totals helper. Full suite 446 runs / 1328 assertions / 0 failures. Rubocop clean, tsc clean, vitest 560 passed.

Filed ttrb-5mr4 for the sort-discard defect found in limit_per_feed.

title: useTtsPlayer poll loop ignores status "unavailable", polling forever
description:
app/javascript/hooks/useTtsPlayer.ts requestAudio handles "unavailable" on the initial response but its setInterval poll branches only on "error" and "ready". If GET /api/v1/entries/:id/audio flips to "unavailable" after generation started (toolchain went away), the interval keeps firing for the life of the page and the hook stays in "generating".

AudioPlayerContext.tsx now treats both "error" and "unavailable" as terminal via isTerminalAudioStatus(); useTtsPlayer is the remaining copy. Found while fixing ttrb-rvm4.
close_reason: Poll loop treats unavailable as terminal; regression tests added (a5cee11)

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit a5cee11: poll loop and first-response branches both route through isTerminalAudioStatus/terminalAudioMessage. New app/javascript/hooks/useTtsPlayer.test.ts (5 tests) covers both terminal statuses on the first response and mid-poll; the mid-poll unavailable case fails against the old condition. Full vitest suite 565 passed, tsc --noEmit clean. Filed ttrb-53dc (helper duplication with AudioPlayerContext) and ttrb-p7qx (hook + TtsPlayer component appear unused).

title: AudioPlayerContext pollForReady has no catch; a network error strands the queue item in "generating"
description:
In the pre-generate useEffect in app/javascript/contexts/AudioPlayerContext.tsx, pollForReady is invoked via setTimeout with no try/catch. If api.entries.audio() rejects (network blip, 500), the rejection is unhandled, the setTimeout chain stops, and the queue item stays status "generating" forever with no retry and no error shown.

The outer preGenerate() has a catch, but it only covers the first await, not the detached poll chain. Contrast preGenerateQueueItem's pollForAudio, which is awaited inside the try and so does mark the item errored.

Found while fixing ttrb-rvm4 (terminal-status handling); left alone there to keep the diff scoped.
close_reason: Poll chain now awaited inside the try/catch; network failures mark the item errored. Covered by 3 new vitest cases.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 788a1ff: awaited the poll loop inside preGenerate's try (sleep-then-request-then-recurse, matching pollForAudio), so a rejected api.entries.audio marks the queue item errored instead of stranding it in "generating". Added finally cleanup of preGeneratingRef. Three vitest cases in AudioPlayerContext.test.tsx cover reject / terminal status / ready; the reject case fails on the pre-fix source (verified).

title: AudioPlayerContext has two near-identical queue TTS pre-generation implementations
description:
app/javascript/contexts/AudioPlayerContext.tsx contains preGenerateQueueItem (useCallback, with pollForAudio) and preGenerate (inside the pre-generate useEffect, with pollForReady). Both poll GET /api/v1/entries/:id/audio for a queue item and write status onto the queue entry; both fire for the same item (playQueueItem calls the first for index+1, the effect covers index+1 and index+2), deduped only by the shared preGeneratingRef set.

They have drifted: preGenerateQueueItem stores audioUrl/duration on the item and clears preGeneratingRef in a finally; preGenerate stores neither and never clears the ref, so an item it handles is never retried. Every bug in this area (ttrb-h45v, ttrb-rvm4) has had to be fixed twice.

Decide whether both are needed, and if so extract one poll helper. Not extracted during ttrb-rvm4 per the ask-before-extracting rule.
close_reason: Extracted: one preGenerateQueueItem, one trigger (the lookahead effect). playQueueItem's redundant imperative call removed. Merged the correct half of each version and added 3 vitest cases for audioUrl/duration storage, ready short-circuit, and terminal first response.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit e569503: sameness test says structurally same, so extracted. Both paths answered the same question (get this pending TTS queue item to a terminal queue status, polling as needed) and wrote the same fields onto the same queue entries; only the trigger differed. The drift was pure bug, not intentional divergence - they raced on preGeneratingRef, so whether an item ended up with audioUrl/duration was nondeterministic. Effect is now the only trigger (playQueueItem's imperative call was redundant: setCurrentQueueIndex already reruns the effect for index+1), preGenerateQueueItem the only implementation. Verified: vitest 703/703, tsc --noEmit clean, esbuild clean. Rails/Minitest and Playwright NOT run - PostgreSQL is down in this environment.

title: Dead keyboard i18n section in locales/en.json: nothing references it and it is stale
description:
app/javascript/locales/en.json lines 204-230 define a full 'keyboard' i18n section that nothing in the codebase references - KeyboardShortcutsDialog.tsx hardcodes its English strings. The dead section is also already stale relative to the real bindings in application.tsx (surfaced while fixing ttrb-4z4p, which corrected 'k / p' -> 'k' and added the missing 'p' = Toggle published row).

Two directions, pick one:
- Wire KeyboardShortcutsDialog to i18n and correct the keys. Makes the dialog translatable, but re-creates the drift risk in a second place unless the key list is derived from the bindings.
- Delete the dead section. Smaller, honest about the fact that the dialog is English-only today.

Note the drift class is the real issue: the dialog's rows and application.tsx's bindings are independent literals, which is what produced ttrb-4z4p. Deriving the dialog from a single binding table would close it for good.
close_reason: Deleted the dead top-level 'keyboard' block from app/javascript/locales/en.json (25 unused keys). Chose deletion over wiring KeyboardShortcutsDialog to i18n: en is the only supported language, and wiring would have added a fourth copy of the shortcut list. Filed ttrb-8zvu for the underlying drift class. typecheck clean, vitest 568/568 pass. Commit 4335e7d.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit 4335e7d: deleted the dead top-level 'keyboard' block (25 keys, en.json:204-230). Picked deletion over wiring the dialog to i18n.

Evidence it was dead: grep over the whole repo (excluding node_modules/.git) for the keys and for 'keyboard.' finds only the definitions themselves. app/javascript/lib/i18n/index.ts is the only importer of en.json and it just hands the object to i18next as resources.en.translation; no useTranslation('keyboard...') call exists.

Evidence it was stale vs application.tsx:726-762 - missing p (Toggle published), Shift+F (Toggle focus mode), Ctrl+K (command palette), Space/Shift+Space paging; and carried nextUnread plus category labels views/scrolling/other that the dialog's own grouping (Navigation/Actions/View/Other) does not match.

Why not wire it up: SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES in lib/i18n/index.ts is [en] only, so translation buys nothing today, and the key strings ('j / n', 'Shift+J') would stay hardcoded regardless - a second drift surface for no gain.

Verified: en.json still parses, top-level keys now [app, common, sidebar, entryList, entryContent, feed, settings, dialogs, errors]. npm run typecheck clean. npm run test:run 30 files / 568 tests, 0 failures. Note settings.tabs.keyboard ('Keyboard') is a different key and was left alone.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Filed ttrb-8zvu for the drift class the description flagged (dialog literals vs application.tsx bindings vs CommandPalette's own Ctrl+K useEffect). Not fixed here - deleting the dead i18n section does not touch it.

title: error-handling.spec.ts 'shows loading states during slow requests' computes hasLoadingIndicator but never asserts it
description:
e2e/error-handling.spec.ts:58-64 builds `hasLoadingIndicator` from three probes (getByText('Loading...'), [class*=animate-spin], [class*=loading]) and then never uses it. The only assertion in the test is that a button is visible after the delay, which says nothing about loading state, so the test cannot fail for the behavior its name describes.

Each probe is also wrapped in .catch(() => false), so any locator error (including a Playwright strict-mode multi-match) is silently swallowed into a passing no-op.

Found while sweeping loose regex locators for ttrb-62uw; the locator there was tightened to an exact 'Loading...' match, but the dead assertion is a separate defect and needs a decision about what the test should actually assert.
close_reason: Replaced the dead hasLoadingIndicator computation with real assertions on the entry-list loading placeholder, gated on a controllable route instead of a 2s sleep. Verified the test fails when the loading state is removed.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 7932b3a: rewrote the test around a gated route. Asserts the entry-pane 'Loading...' placeholder is visible while the entries request is parked, then that it is hidden and entries render after release. Mutation-checked: forcing EntryList's isLoading branch to false fails the new assertion. 33/33 in error-handling.spec.ts pass.

title: npm run test:coverage fails: @vitest/coverage-v8 not installed
description:
Discovered during ttrb-07i4. The test:coverage script exists in package.json but the provider package it needs was never added:

  $ npm run test:coverage
  > vitest run --coverage
   MISSING DEPENDENCY  Cannot find dependency '@vitest/coverage-v8'

vitest.config.mts sets coverage.provider 'v8' and coverage.include 'app/javascript/components/**/*.tsx', but @vitest/coverage-v8 is absent from devDependencies (only 'vitest' itself is there). Pre-existing, not caused by the .mts rename; the same failure reproduces on any prior commit.

Fix: npm i -D @vitest/coverage-v8 pinned to the vitest 4.x line, then confirm the report renders. Alternatively drop the test:coverage script and the coverage block from the config if per-file coverage is not wanted for the frontend.

Note the coverage config's include list only covers components/, so contexts/, hooks/ and lib/ would report nothing even once the provider is installed; decide whether that narrowing is intentional while fixing this.

Acceptance criteria:
- npm run test:coverage exits 0 and prints a text coverage table
- CI is unaffected (it runs test:run, not test:coverage)
close_reason: Installed @vitest/coverage-v8; test:coverage exits 0 with a text table. Widened coverage.include to the four directories that have tests.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Created ttrb-iupo: test:ui has the same missing-dependency bug (@vitest/ui absent).

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit d6ee3db: installed @vitest/coverage-v8@^4.1.10 (matches installed vitest 4.1.10) and widened coverage.include to components/, contexts/, hooks/, lib/. npm run test:coverage now exits 0, 31 files / 568 tests pass, text + html reports render.

title: Fresh view silently discards the sort selection whenever fresh_per_feed is set
description:
Api::V1::EntriesController#limit_per_feed (app/controllers/api/v1/entries_controller.rb) rebuilds the relation from scratch: current_user.user_entries.where(id: ids).includes(:entry, :feed).joins(:entry).order("entries.date_entered DESC"). That discards whatever apply_sorting put on the relation earlier in #index.

The Fresh toolbar defaults fresh_per_feed to 5 (app/javascript/application.tsx), so in practice the Fresh list ALWAYS ignores the user's sort config (params[:sort] / order_by=score) - picking a sort in Fresh does nothing.

Noticed while making counters honour the per-feed cap (ttrb-ma6z). That change also gave headlines the cap via .where(id: UserEntry.top_per_feed_ids(...)), which keeps the existing order, so #index and #headlines now order differently under a cap.

Fix: apply the cap the way headlines does - filter the existing relation by the ranked ids instead of rebuilding it - so the sort survives. The ranking inside UserEntry.top_per_feed_ids can stay date_entered DESC (it decides which rows survive, not how they are displayed); note it ranks by import date while Fresh membership is defined by publication date (entries.updated), which may itself be worth revisiting.
close_reason: limit_per_feed now filters the existing relation by the ranked ids instead of rebuilding it, so apply_sorting survives the Fresh per-feed cap; headlines shares the same helper. Commit bdd4cf6, 3 regression tests.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Raised to P2 by the bdexec orchestrator. The underlying defect (limit_per_feed discarding apply_sorting) is pre-existing, but commit 20d0699 (ttrb-ma6z) made #index and #headlines order differently under a cap, which is a new divergence introduced in this run. ttrb-y0na had just finished making those endpoints agree; leaving them split re-opens that class of bug. Taking it next rather than leaving it in the P3 pile.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit bdd4cf6: limit_per_feed now filters the existing relation (user_entries.where(id: UserEntry.top_per_feed_ids(...))) instead of rebuilding from current_user.user_entries with a hardcoded order. headlines calls the same helper, so #index and #headlines can no longer diverge under a cap. Three regression tests added to entries_controller_test: sort survives the cap, index and headlines return identical id order under a cap, and the cap keeps the newest per feed. 449 runs / 0 failures, rubocop clean.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Filed follow-ups discovered here: ttrb-jypp (cap ranks by import date while Fresh membership uses publication date) and ttrb-csn6 (index applies the cap before the tag filter, so Fresh+tag under a cap under-reports).

title: Fresh per-feed cap ranks by import date while Fresh membership uses publication date
description:
UserEntry.top_per_feed_ids (app/models/user_entry.rb) ranks rows with ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY feed_id ORDER BY entries.date_entered DESC), i.e. by import date. The Fresh scope itself selects membership by publication date (entries.updated > cutoff). So which 5 articles of a feed survive the cap is decided on a different clock than the one that decided the feed's articles are fresh at all: a backlog imported today outranks an article published today but imported yesterday.

Noticed while fixing ttrb-5mr4. Not a correctness bug on its own - the cap only decides which rows survive, not how they are displayed - but the two clocks should probably agree. Options: rank by entries.updated DESC to match the freshness definition, or leave it and document why import date is the right tiebreak.
close_reason: Fresh per-feed cap now ranks by entries.updated (publication date), the same clock the fresh scope uses for membership, with import date and id as tiebreaks. Commit 1d2f1f0, 2 regression tests.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 1d2f1f0: top_per_feed_ids now ranks ROW_NUMBER() by entries.updated DESC (publication date, matching the fresh scope's membership test), with entries.date_entered DESC and user_entries.id DESC as deterministic tiebreaks. count_per_feed_capped is rank-independent so the Fresh badge still matches the list. Two new regression tests; three existing cap tests reworked to vary publication date instead of import date. 456 runs / 0 failures, rubocop clean.

title: Fresh + tag filter under a per-feed cap under-reports: index applies the cap before the tag filter
description:
In Api::V1::EntriesController#index the view case block (and its limit_per_feed call) runs before the tag filter further down the method, so the per-feed cap is computed over ALL fresh rows and the tag filter then thins the survivors. Fresh + tag with fresh_per_feed=5 can return zero tagged articles even when a feed has fresh tagged articles ranked 6th or later by import date.

#headlines applies feed_id/category_id before its cap (and has no tag filter), so the two endpoints use different orderings of filter vs cap. Feed and category filters commute with a per-feed cap (feeds partition into one category), so tag is the only filter that actually diverges today.

Fix direction: move the view/cap block after all filters in #index so the cap is always the last thing applied, and keep headlines consistent. Decide first whether the cap means '5 newest fresh per feed' or '5 newest matching per feed' - the latter is what the toolbar implies.

Found while fixing ttrb-5mr4.
close_reason: Moved the view/cap block in entries#index below all filters so the Fresh per-feed cap ranks the final row set (newest N matching per feed). Commit 65c96a3, 2 regression tests.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 65c96a3: moved the view/cap case block in #index below the feed, category and tag filters so the per-feed cap is the last thing applied. Semantics chosen: the cap means 'newest N MATCHING articles per feed' (what the toolbar implies), not 'newest N fresh'. headlines already applied its view block last; added a comment there so it stays. Two regression tests, both verified failing without the controller change. 451 runs / 0 failures, rubocop clean.

title: Consolidate isTerminalAudioStatus/terminalAudioMessage duplicated in AudioPlayerContext.tsx and useTtsPlayer.ts
description:
Both app/javascript/contexts/AudioPlayerContext.tsx and app/javascript/hooks/useTtsPlayer.ts now define identical module-private isTerminalAudioStatus() and terminalAudioMessage() helpers. They classify the same api.entries.audio() status enum (AudioResponse["status"]) and will always change together when the API grows a new status, so this is structural sameness, not incidental.

Suggested home: export both from app/javascript/lib/api.ts next to the AudioResponse type, or a small app/javascript/lib/audioStatus.ts. Kept as a copy while fixing ttrb-2rmb to keep that diff inside the named file; extraction touches AudioPlayerContext.tsx and wants Andy's sign-off per the rule-of-three policy.
close_reason: Duplication removed by deleting useTtsPlayer.ts in ttrb-p7qx (45e82fe); AudioPlayerContext.tsx is now the sole definition

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Moot as of 45e82fe: useTtsPlayer.ts was deleted as dead code (ttrb-p7qx), so its copy of isTerminalAudioStatus/terminalAudioMessage is gone. AudioPlayerContext.tsx now holds the only definition and there is nothing left to consolidate.
