title: e2e page objects and specs reference data-testids the app never renders (entry-list, entry-content, feed-item, data-entry-title)
description:
e2e/pages/feeds.page.ts:37 and :40 build locators from getByTestId("entry-list") and getByTestId("entry-content"), and :109 reads [data-entry-title] under them. grep over app/javascript shows the only data-testid attributes in the app are filter-row, tag-row, color-preset, audio-player, video-player, plus app-root in app/views/home/index.html.erb. None of entry-list, entry-content, feed-item or data-entry-title exist, so those locators match nothing.

Consequence: every spec branch guarded by 'if (await locator.isVisible().catch(() => false))' on one of these silently skips its body and the test passes without exercising anything. error-handling.spec.ts:40 (feed-item), :492 (feed-item) are two examples; feeds.page.ts helpers that use entryList are dead the same way.

Fix is a decision: either add the testids to EntryList/EntryContent/the sidebar rows, or rewrite the page objects around semantic locators (EntryItem already carries role=option). Found while fixing ttrb-aivz.
close_reason: Rewrote feeds/sidebar/entry-list page objects around semantic locators (listbox, article, navigation landmark, role=option, aria-selected) and added the missing app-side handles; fixed the two vacuous feed-item guards in error-handling.spec.ts, which exposed a back/forward test that had never run. Commit efdac74.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Orchestrator note: this is not blocked on a decision. The project CLAUDE.md already sets the policy - 'Use getByRole() as primary locator strategy' and 'Use getByTestId() only when semantic locators insufficient' (Testing Guidelines > E2E Tests). EntryItem already renders role='option', which ttrb-aivz's fix used successfully. So the direction is: rewrite the page objects around semantic locators, and only add a data-testid where no semantic handle exists.

Also worth folding in: the vacuous-guard pattern itself is the deeper bug. 'if (await locator.isVisible().catch(() => false))' converts both a missing element AND a locator error into a silent skip. Prefer an unconditional assertion, or an explicit test.skip() with a stated reason, so a broken locator fails loudly. Same class as ttrb-aivz and ttrb-62uw.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit efdac74. Rewrote the page objects around semantic locators per the orchestrator note, adding app-side handles only where none existed.

App changes (app/javascript/components/):
- EntryList.tsx: entries wrapped in role=listbox aria-label='Entries' (the role=option rows had no owning listbox, an ARIA defect independent of the tests); title bar span -> h2 (Tailwind preflight makes this visually identical); loading placeholder given role=status aria-label='Loading entries' so it is separable from EntryContent's own bare 'Loading...'; EntryItem gained data-entry-title next to the existing data-entry-id/data-unread.
- FeedSidebar.tsx: both roots (collapsed and expanded) are role=navigation aria-label='Feeds'.

Page objects now: listbox/article/navigation roles, role=option rows, aria-selected for selection, [data-slot=scroll-area-viewport] for scrolling.

Two extra locator bugs found by exercising every helper against a live page in a throwaway spec (since deleted):
1. allFeedsButton /all feeds/i matched 'Show all feeds' and freshButton /fresh/i matched 'Refresh all feeds'; both toggles precede the folder list so .first() clicked the wrong control. Anchored to /^All Feeds/, /^Fresh/, /^Starred/. starredButton had been right only by DOM order.
2. SidebarComponent.isCollapsed measured clientWidth against the 150ms width transition and reported 'expanded' right after collapsing. It checks for the 'Expand sidebar' button now.
Also replaced getSelectedEntry(): Promise<Locator|null> with a selectedEntry locator - the old shape read a count before React committed the aria-selected flip and always answered 'nothing selected'.

Removing the guard on 'handles back/forward navigation' exposed a test that had never executed: the click matched nothing, and the first honest run failed on about:blank. Confirmed via probe that selecting a feed does push history state (history.length 2 -> 3, state {type:'feed',feedId:1}), so both specs now assert the entry-list title across the navigation instead of only 'some button is enabled'.

Verification: npm run typecheck clean; npm run test:run 568 passed; full playwright suite 219 passed / 5 skipped / 0 failed (224 total), same shape before and after.

Filed ttrb-a736 for the six remaining isVisible().catch(() => false) guards in error-handling.spec.ts.

title: Six remaining vacuous isVisible().catch(() => false) guards in error-handling.spec.ts skip their own assertions
description:
Follow-up to ttrb-yoil, which removed the two guards that wrapped the phantom [data-testid="feed-item"] locator. Six of the same pattern remain in e2e/error-handling.spec.ts:

  216 starredNav      - page.getByText("Starred")
  232 searchInput     - page.getByPlaceholder(/search|type/i)
  430 button          - page.getByRole("button").first()
  463 subscribeButton - page.getByRole("button", { name: /subscribe|add feed/i })
  467 urlInput        - page.getByLabel(/url/i)
  494 numberInput     - input[type=number]

'if (await locator.isVisible().catch(() => false))' collapses two different outcomes into a silent pass: the element is genuinely absent, and the locator itself errored (strict-mode violation, bad selector). Either way the test body never runs and the example is reported green. Line 430 is the extreme case - it guards page.getByRole('button').first(), which is exactly what the assertion after the block already checks.

The database is seeded deterministically by E2eDataset and every example is signed in via the auto fixtures, so 'the element might not be there' is not a real condition for most of these. Replace each with an unconditional assertion, or with an explicit test.skip() carrying a stated reason.

Note ttrb-yoil found that removing such a guard can expose a genuinely broken test rather than a passing one: 'handles back/forward navigation' had been clicking a locator that matched nothing, and the first honest run failed on about:blank.

Acceptance criteria:
- No 'catch(() => false)' visibility guards remain in e2e/error-handling.spec.ts
- Each affected example asserts something real, or is skipped with a reason
- Full e2e suite stays green
close_reason: Replaced all six catch(() => false) visibility guards in e2e/error-handling.spec.ts with unconditional assertions; no test.skip needed. Full e2e suite green (219 passed). Commit e0acc74.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit e0acc74: replaced all six guards. Full e2e suite green (219 passed, 5 pre-existing skips, 2.4m). Notable finding: the settings example's input[type=number] does not exist anywhere in app/javascript - grep for type="number" returns nothing - so that guard could never have opened. Rewrote it against the accent hue range input (PreferencesPanel.tsx:150, min 0 max 360), driven past its minimum from the keyboard because Locator.fill refuses out-of-range values on a range input (verified: 'Error: Malformed value'). Also found the subscribe locator was pointed at the collapsed sidebar rail's 'Subscribe to feed' button; the expanded sidebar reaches the dialog through the 'Add...' dropdown.

title: npm run test:ui fails: @vitest/ui not installed
description:
Same class of bug as ttrb-o8x5 (missing coverage provider), found while fixing it. package.json defines a test:ui script (vitest --ui) but @vitest/ui is absent from devDependencies:

  $ node -e "require.resolve('@vitest/ui/package.json')" -> MISSING

Running npm run test:ui will fail with a MISSING DEPENDENCY error the same way test:coverage did. Not exercised by CI (ci.yml:118 runs test:run only).

Fix: npm i -D @vitest/ui pinned to the vitest 4.x line, or drop the test:ui script if the browser UI runner is not wanted.

Acceptance criteria:
- npm run test:ui starts the UI server, or the script is removed
close_reason: Installed @vitest/ui@^4.1.10; npm run test:ui starts the UI server and serves the dashboard.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit ce633e5: installed @vitest/ui@^4.1.10 (matches installed vitest 4.1.10). npm run test:ui now starts the UI server (HTTP 200 at /__vitest__/, 30 files / 563 tests pass). npm audit clean, test:run unaffected.

title: entries#headlines has no tag filter while entries#index does
description:
Api::V1::EntriesController#index supports params[:tag] (joins entry -> tags, scoped to current_user) but #headlines does not, so the same query string returns a tag-filtered list from /entries and an unfiltered list from /entries/headlines. ttrb-y0na and ttrb-5mr4 both worked to keep the two endpoints in agreement; this is the remaining divergence.

Low priority because nothing calls headlines today: the route exists (config/routes.rb:46) but app/javascript/lib/api.ts has no headlines client, so only tests hit it. It becomes a live bug the moment the frontend switches the list to headlines.

Fix: add the same tag filter to #headlines, above its view case block (which must stay last so the Fresh per-feed cap ranks the final row set - see ttrb-csn6).

Found while fixing ttrb-csn6.
close_reason: Added the params[:tag] filter to #headlines matching #index, positioned before the view case block so the Fresh per-feed cap ranks tagged rows. 3 regression tests, 102 controller tests green, rubocop clean.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit e7dd1be: tag filter added to #headlines above the view case block, mirroring #index. Three tests added (tag filtering, current-user tag scoping, index/headlines agreement under tag + fresh_per_feed cap); all three fail on the pre-fix controller. Verified the generated SQL joins entries once, not twice.

title: parallelize(workers: 1) in 4 test classes silently serializes the entire suite
description:
ActiveSupport::TestCase.parallelize unconditionally reassigns Minitest.parallel_executor (activesupport-8.1.3.1/lib/active_support/test_case.rb:125), so the LAST call at load time wins for the whole run. There is no per-class opt-out.

Four test classes call parallelize(workers: 1) with comments claiming they disable parallel execution 'for this test class':
  test/models/cached_image_test.rb:5
  test/services/image_cacher_test.rb:6
  test/jobs/cleanup_cached_images_job_test.rb:5
  test/jobs/cache_article_images_job_test.rb:5
All load after test/test_helper.rb's parallelize(workers: :number_of_processors), so the executor ends up size 1. ParallelizeExecutor#many_workers? is then false, the suite runs single-process, and execution_info returns nil so nothing is printed about it either.

Verified 2026-08-18 on 09aeec1: a plain 'bin/rails test' run produced exactly one SimpleCov resultset entry ('Minitest', no subprocess entries) and printed no parallelization line. Forcing PARALLEL_WORKERS=4 makes it parallelize (454 tests, 4 processes) and 4 tests fail:
  ImageCacherTest#test_re-downloads_when_the_cache_record_has_lost_its_file
  CachedAudioTest#test_deletes_cached_file_on_destroy
  CleanupCachedImagesJobTest#test_leaves_an_intact_cache_alone
  CleanupCachedImagesJobTest#test_keeps_files_with_database_records

So the serialization is load-bearing: those tests share on-disk cache paths and are not parallel-safe. The fix is to make them parallel-safe (per-worker cache directories keyed off ENV['TEST_ENV_NUMBER'] or Process.pid, the way test/jobs/fetch_favicon_job_test.rb and test/jobs/update_favicons_job_test.rb already do) and drop the parallelize(workers: 1) calls, rather than leaving the whole suite serial by accident.

Discovered while working ttrb-s5br.
close_reason: Replaced the four parallelize(workers: 1) calls with real parallel safety: image and audio cache directories now come from config.x.image_cache.dir / config.x.audio_cache.dir, resolved at call time, and test_helper's parallelize_setup gives each forked worker its own subdirectory. Suite now runs in parallel and is green at 1/4/8/16/32 workers. Commit 571830f.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit 571830f: moved the image and audio cache directories into config.x.image_cache.dir / config.x.audio_cache.dir (resolved at call time, not constants), added parallelize_setup in test/test_helper.rb to append the worker number per forked process, and dropped the four parallelize(workers: 1) calls. Test env points both at tmp/test_caches so a run can no longer wipe public/images/cache in a dev checkout.

Verified on 83687da (before) and 571830f (after), same machine, same tree:
- before: bin/rails test ran single-process (no parallelization line); PARALLEL_WORKERS=4 gave 6 failures + 1 error (more than the 4 recorded in the description, since which tests lose the race varies per run)
- after: green at PARALLEL_WORKERS=1, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 3 consecutive default runs (32 processes), 454 runs / 1365 assertions each
- mechanism re-confirmed on the fixed tree: adding a scratch test class with parallelize(workers: 1) put the whole 455-test suite back into one process, then removing it restored 32 processes
- brakeman 1 warning (the pre-existing lib/e2e_dataset.rb SQL injection), rubocop clean

CachedAudioTest was also unsafe (its teardown rm_rf'd the shared audio directory) and is covered by the same isolation. Callers read Rails.configuration directly instead of a CachedImage.cache_dir helper because a method call on a model class makes Brakeman classify the path as a model attribute and file File Access warnings at every downstream File/Dir call (6 of them).

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Filed ttrb-48cm: CI's scan_ruby job is red independently of this work, because bin/brakeman exits 3 on the one standing lib/e2e_dataset.rb warning.

title: CI scan_ruby job fails: bin/brakeman exits 3 on the lib/e2e_dataset.rb TRUNCATE warning
description:
The CI 'scan_ruby' job runs 'bin/brakeman --no-pager'. Brakeman exits 3 whenever it reports any warning, and the repo has one standing Medium-confidence SQL Injection warning at lib/e2e_dataset.rb:105 (the TRUNCATE built from ActiveRecord::Base.connection.tables, each name passed through quote_table_name). So the job fails on every push regardless of the change.

Verified 2026-08-18 on 571830f: 'bin/brakeman --no-pager; echo $?' prints exit=3 with exactly that one warning; 'bundle exec rubocop' (185 files) and 'bin/bundler-audit' are both clean, so brakeman is the only red gate. Last recorded CI run (24587751929, 2026-04-17) shows scan_ruby and lint failing; its logs have expired (HTTP 410) so the lint failure could not be re-confirmed and looks to have been fixed since.

Fix is to decide on the warning rather than the exit code: either add a config/brakeman.ignore entry documenting why the interpolated table list is safe (names come from the connection and go through quote_table_name, no user input), or rewrite the truncate to avoid the interpolation. Do not silence it by dropping the exit check.

Discovered while working ttrb-azer.
close_reason: Added config/brakeman.ignore documenting the lib/e2e_dataset.rb TRUNCATE false positive. bin/brakeman --no-pager exits 0; exit-code gate left in place, no CI workflow change needed. Commit 810abd8.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 810abd8: added config/brakeman.ignore with a documented note for the lib/e2e_dataset.rb TRUNCATE warning (fingerprint 9ee6341d...). bin/brakeman --no-pager now exits 0 with 'Security Warnings: 0 / Ignored Warnings: 1'. Brakeman reads config/brakeman.ignore by default, so .github/workflows/ci.yml is unchanged and the exit-code gate stays intact. Rejected the rewrite option: ActiveRecord's connection.truncate_tables builds 'TRUNCATE TABLE <quoted list>' with no RESTART IDENTITY (activerecord-8.1.3.1 postgresql/database_statements.rb:208), which would break the deterministic record ids the E2E fixtures rely on. Also added a pointer comment above E2eDataset.truncate_all! so the ignore is discoverable from the call site. Verified: rubocop 185 files clean, bin/bundler-audit clean, brakeman exit 0.

title: KeyboardShortcutsDialog rows and the real key bindings are independent literals that drift
description:
The shortcut help dialog and the actual bindings are three separate hand-maintained lists, with nothing tying them together:

1. app/javascript/application.tsx:726-762 - the keyboardCommands useMemo passed to useKeyboardCommands. Each entry already carries a 'description' string.
2. app/javascript/components/KeyboardShortcutsDialog.tsx:14-47 - a 'shortcuts' const with its own category grouping, its own key labels ('j / n', 'Shift+J') and its own copies of the same descriptions.
3. app/javascript/components/CommandPalette.tsx:163-178 - useCommandPalette binds Ctrl/Cmd+K in its own useEffect, outside keyboardCommands entirely. The dialog lists it; the command table does not know it exists.

This produced ttrb-4z4p (dialog said 'k / p' for Previous entry and omitted p = Toggle published) and it will produce the next one. The lists are currently in sync except for wording ('Go to All feeds' in the dialog vs 'Go to All' in the bindings), so this is prevention, not an outstanding bug.

Sketch: give KeyboardCommand an optional display label and section, export the command table from a module both application.tsx and the dialog import, and render the dialog by grouping over it. Aliases (j/n, o/Enter, m/u) need to collapse into one row, which is why the display label has to be explicit rather than derived from 'key'. Ctrl+K either moves into the command table or gets an explicit 'declared elsewhere' entry so it is not silently omitted.

Discovered while closing ttrb-8xkd (deleted the dead 'keyboard' i18n section rather than wiring the dialog to i18n, since wiring it would have added a fourth copy of the same list).
close_reason: Shortcuts now come from one catalog (lib/keyboardShortcuts.ts); dialog renders it, application.tsx supplies only handlers via an exhaustive typed map, Ctrl+K documented as bound elsewhere

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 746280d: added app/javascript/lib/keyboardShortcuts.ts as the single source of truth (id, section, display label, description, bindings). KeyboardShortcutsDialog renders shortcutsBySection(); application.tsx calls buildKeyboardCommands() with a handler map typed Record<BoundShortcutId, () => void>, so a catalog entry with no handler is a compile error (verified with a throwaway file: TS2741). Ctrl+K kept its own listener in useCommandPalette (it fires inside text inputs, which useKeyboardCommands does not) but now has a catalog entry with empty bindings + boundElsewhere note. Wording drift resolved to the dialog's strings. 580 vitest tests pass, tsc clean.

title: vitest isolate:false leaks module mocks between files; CI test_js red on main
description:
CI run 32183347632 (push of f7c5603) failed test_js with 2 failures in PreferencesPanel.test.tsx:
- 'purge unread is disabled when purge days is never' -> expect(element).toBeDisabled()
- 'updates preference when toggle is clicked' -> expected vi.fn() called with [{ show_content_preview: 'true' }]
All other jobs green, including test_e2e (219 passed / 5 skipped).

Root cause: vitest.config.mts sets pool:'threads' with isolate:false. Its comment ('tests are already independent') is false - vi.mock module registries leak between test files that share a worker. Which files share a worker depends on worker count, which depends on CPU count, so the failure set differs per machine.

Reproduced locally (32 cores, npm ci from lockfile):
- default workers: 31 files / 580 tests pass (3 consecutive runs)
- --maxWorkers=4: pass
- --maxWorkers=2: pass
- --maxWorkers=1: widespread failures across I18nContext (4), PreferencesContext (3+), SuggestedTags (1)

That is the same defect class as ttrb-azer on the Ruby side: a config claiming isolation that does not hold, masked by the local machine's core count.

Fix: set isolate:true (vitest default). Measure the runtime cost and record it - isolate:false was introduced in 998242e for speed.
close_reason: Fixed in 54e42d6: isolate:true in vitest.config.mts. Verified green at maxWorkers 1, 2, 4 and 8 (maxWorkers=1 previously failed across I18nContext, PreferencesContext and SuggestedTags). No measurable speed cost: 3 runs each on the same tree, 4.09/3.95/4.17s with isolate:false vs 4.08/4.03/4.12s with isolate:true, so the original speed premise was also wrong. tsc clean.

title: Surface the deployed commit SHA in the app (meta tag + settings footer)
close_reason: Implemented in 13f6cd5. AppVersion (lib/app_version.rb) resolves KAMAL_VERSION -> git -> UNKNOWN; meta tag in the application layout; AppVersionFooter in the settings dialog. title: Sidebar badges never refresh from background feed ingestion (loadCounters is mount-only)
description:
Current behavior
The Fresh badge (and the other sidebar counts) only update after a local user action. app/javascript/application.tsx:124 runs loadCounters() in a useEffect keyed on [freshMaxAge, freshPerFeed], and every other call site (lines 259, 325, 338, 367, 382, 397, 470) hangs off a user interaction (toggle read/starred/published, mark all read). loadFeeds() at line 117 is mount-only with no deps. There is no polling interval, no visibilitychange listener, and no server push.

Result: the fresh cron job ingests new entries server-side, but the client has no reason to re-ask, so the badge stays stale until you click into the Fresh list and act on an item. Andys read: "perhaps it is just not responsive to background updates." Confirmed - that is exactly the mechanism.

Expected behavior
Sidebar counts converge on server state regardless of where focus is, without requiring navigation into the list.

Affected files
- app/javascript/application.tsx (loadCounters, loadFeeds, the mount effects)
- app/controllers/api/v1/counters_controller.rb (GET /api/v1/counters, already cheap-ish: 3 grouped counts + fresh cap)

Options to weigh
1. Poll GET /api/v1/counters on an interval (30-60s), paused when document.hidden.
2. Refetch on window focus / visibilitychange (cheapest, covers the common tab-switch case).
3. Push (ActionCable / SSE) from the feed-refresh job - correct but heaviest.
1+2 together is probably the pragmatic answer.

Also decide whether per-feed and per-category unread badges refresh on the same tick; they come from loadFeeds(), which is separately mount-only, so fixing only counters leaves feed rows stale.

Acceptance criteria
- With the app open and idle on any view, a background feed fetch that adds fresh entries updates the Fresh badge within one poll interval.
- Refetch does not run while the tab is hidden.
- Feed and category unread badges update on the same mechanism (or a follow-up bead explicitly defers them).
close_reason: Sidebar badges now converge on server state without user action: useBackgroundRefresh polls loadFeeds + loadCounters every 60s while the tab is visible, tears the timer down while hidden, and refreshes once on visibilitychange->visible. Suspended while the settings dialog is open. Commit 68b81a6; 13 new hook tests, full vitest suite 621 passing.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 68b81a6: added app/javascript/hooks/useBackgroundRefresh.ts (interval poll while visible + refresh on visibilitychange->visible, timer torn down while hidden) and wired it in application.tsx to call loadFeeds() + loadCounters() on the same tick, so virtual folder badges and per-feed/per-category unread badges converge together. Poll suspended while the settings dialog is open (FeedOrganizer mutates the feeds array optimistically via stale closures). 13 hook tests; full vitest suite 621 passed, tsc --noEmit clean, esbuild build clean. Verified frontend only: PostgreSQL is not running on this host, so Minitest and Playwright were not run.

title: Article search: filter box scoped to the current list or all history
description:
Wire up article search end to end. The backend half already exists and is unused: GET /api/v1/search (app/controllers/api/v1/search_controller.rb) runs PostgreSQL full-text search over Entry#tsvector_combined (GIN index entries_tsvector_combined_idx, db/schema.rb:80) and returns paginated results with match snippets. Nothing in app/javascript calls it. There is no api.search in app/javascript/lib/api.ts and no UI.

Shape agreed with Andy:
- Search is a SERVER query, not a client-side filter over loaded rows. Typing (debounced) sends the current view scope along with the query, so results cover the whole list rather than the ~50 rows EntryList happens to hold.
- Scope is the current list by default: whatever feed / category / view / tag the user is looking at carries into the query.
- Read-state depth defaults to the current view (unread stays unread), with an explicit opt-in to search deeper into read and archived history.
- Ctrl+F is NOT available: keyboardShortcuts.ts:123 binds it to page-down-content next to Ctrl+B. Use / to open the search box.

Children cover the backend params, two defects in the existing search implementation, the API client, the input UI and keybinding, the scope controls, and result rendering.
close_reason:
All eight children closed. The feature is complete end to end, and the epic turned out to be sitting on a foundation that had never worked.

Children, in the order they landed:
- ttrb-xhk3 (d15ba15) typed api.search() client
- ttrb-qv7i (12b1752) search box on /, shared keyboard catalog entry
- ttrb-a81x (9f00b60) snippets and term highlighting, XSS-safe React nodes
- ttrb-voe4 (367159e) THE FOUNDATION: tsvector_combined was nil on all 8271 production rows because a before_save read a PostgreSQL result column by the wrong name; every Entry.search returned []. Replaced with a GENERATED ALWAYS ... STORED column so no write path can bypass it.
- ttrb-soaj (8b0773a) one query instead of pluck-and-IN, ordered ts_rank DESC, date_entered DESC, user_entries.id DESC
- ttrb-aawe (5fc50be) full entry-list scoping vocabulary via EntryScoping concern
- ttrb-prmg (456eaf0) two orthogonal scope pills, defaulting to the list as shown
- ttrb-20gl (57892f7) removed the misleading sanitize_sql_like
- ttrb-clec (41e4c21) ts_headline snippets with U+0002/U+0003 delimiters the client renders as React nodes

Worth recording: the first three children were built and tested against an index that contained nothing, and all of them passed their tests, because those tests mock the API or seed the column directly. voe4 was only found later, while investigating an unrelated feed bug. Anything reasoning about this epic should treat the pre-voe4 test results as having proved less than they appeared to.

NOT VERIFIED AGAINST REAL DATA. The development database here has 0 entries; the 8271 rows are production. Everything above is the test suite, which is now 574 Ruby runs / 1682 assertions and 864 vitest across 47 files, all passing. Production still needs `bin/rails db:migrate` to build the generated column, then `bin/rails search:status` to confirm. Until that runs, search in production still returns nothing.

Also open and deliberately not folded in: ttrb-w84a (re-sortable results, un-hide the sort controls), ttrb-i3ay (the whole feature shipped with vitest coverage only, e2e/ has no search spec), ttrb-brv2 (EntriesController#headlines still carries its own copy of the filter block).

title: Extend GET /api/v1/search to accept the entry list scoping params (unread, view, starred, tag)
description:
Current behavior
SearchController#index scopes only by feed_id and category_id (filter_by_feed / filter_by_category). EntriesController#index supports a much wider set: unread, starred, published, feed_id, category_id, tag, and view (fresh / starred / published / archived), where fresh additionally applies the age window and the per-feed cap via FreshArticleWindow and limit_per_feed.

Because of the gap, a search cannot be scoped to the list the user is actually looking at, and cannot express unread-only vs deeper history. Both are required by the agreed design.

Expected behavior
GET /api/v1/search accepts the same scoping params as GET /api/v1/entries and applies them identically, so search results are the intersection of the query and the current list.

Implementation note
The filter block in EntriesController#index is about 60 lines and would become the second copy if pasted into SearchController. Extract it into a shared concern or query object (for example app/controllers/concerns/entry_scoping.rb, or an EntryScope query object) used by both. Per the rule of three this is the second site, so extraction is a judgement call: propose the shape before extracting, and keep the fresh per-feed cap ordering semantics intact (the cap must be applied LAST, after the tag filter, per the comment in EntriesController#index).

Affected files
- app/controllers/api/v1/search_controller.rb
- app/controllers/api/v1/entries_controller.rb
- app/controllers/concerns/ (new shared scoping module, if extracted)

Acceptance criteria
- search?q=X&view=fresh returns only entries that the Fresh list would show, honouring fresh_max_age and fresh_per_feed.
- search?q=X&unread=true returns only unread; omitting unread searches regardless of read state.
- search?q=X&tag=foo, &starred=true, &feed_id=, &category_id= all behave as they do on /entries.
- Controller tests cover each param against a fixture set where the query matches both in-scope and out-of-scope entries.
close_reason: GET /api/v1/search now honours unread, starred, published, feed_id, category_id, tag, view and the fresh_max_age/fresh_per_feed window via the new EntryScoping concern, shared with EntriesController#index. category_id now expands to the category subtree, matching /entries. Client doc comment in api.ts updated to say the params are honoured. Commit 5fc50be.

Note for whoever takes it: test/controllers/api/v1/search_controller_test.rb now exists with a working sign_in + create_entry + subscribe harness, so the per-param tests this ticket asks for have somewhere to go.

Filed ttrb-brv2 for the remaining copy in #headlines. Suites: rails 571/1669/0F/0E, vitest 809/46 files, playwright 260 passed 5 skipped, rubocop 200 files no offenses.

The earlier red run predated strengthening the fresh_max_age=all case, which was toothless (it asserted a total that held with view ignored) and now seeds a read decoy that Fresh must still exclude. Re-verified by checking out HEAD~1's controllers: 15 failures. The single test that passes both before and after is the deliberate control 'searches regardless of read state when unread is omitted', which is the acceptance criterion that omitting unread must not filter.

title: SearchController plucks every matching entry id and discards ts_rank relevance ordering
description:
Current behavior
app/controllers/api/v1/search_controller.rb#search_user_entries:

  entry_ids = Entry.search(params[:q]).pluck(:id)
  current_user.user_entries.where(entry_id: entry_ids)...order("entries.date_entered DESC")

Two problems in three lines.

1. Unbounded materialisation. Entry.search matches across the ENTIRE shared entries table, not just the current users subscriptions, and every matching id is pulled into Ruby memory and then shipped back to PostgreSQL as an IN list. A common word against a large corpus means a huge array and a huge query. Pagination is applied after this, so it does not help. The total count then runs a second time over the same IN list.

2. Relevance ranking is computed and thrown away. Entry.search orders by ts_rank(tsvector_combined, plainto_tsquery(...)) DESC, but pluck(:id) discards the ordering and the outer query re-sorts by entries.date_entered DESC. The ranking work is paid for and never used, and results come back chronologically rather than by relevance.

Expected behavior
Single query: join user_entries to the tsvector predicate so PostgreSQL filters and ranks in one pass over the users own rows, and decide the sort deliberately (relevance, date, or a user-facing toggle) rather than by accident.

Affected files
- app/controllers/api/v1/search_controller.rb (search_user_entries)
- app/models/entry.rb (the search scope, if the rank expression needs to be exposed for reuse)

Acceptance criteria
- No pluck of an unbounded id set; the search executes as one query against user_entries joined to entries.
- Ordering is explicit and tested: either ts_rank DESC, or date, or a documented param. Whichever is chosen, a test asserts the order.
- Total count does not re-scan an in-memory id list.
close_reason: SearchController filters and ranks in one query over user_entries joined to entries. Ordering is ts_rank DESC, date_entered DESC, user_entries.id DESC, asserted by a test seeded so relevance and date order disagree. Commit 8b0773a.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Newly live after ttrb-voe4. Entry.search(q).pluck(:id) previously always returned [] so neither problem was reachable; now it returns real ids. The scope's ts_rank ordering is confirmed correct by a new model test (EntryTest#test_search_orders_more_relevant_entries_first), so this ticket is now cleanly isolated to the controller discarding it. The new SearchController tests deliberately do NOT assert result ordering, so whichever sort this ticket picks is free to land without rewriting them.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Fixed in 8b0773a. search_user_entries is now one query: current_user.user_entries.joins(:entry) with the tsvector predicate in the WHERE, ordered ts_rank DESC, entries.date_entered DESC, user_entries.id DESC. No pluck, and the pagination count is a plain COUNT(DISTINCT user_entries.id) over the same join with no IN list and no ORDER BY (verified via rails runner against the generated SQL).

Order decision: relevance first, recency as tiebreak. Search is the one place the user has stated what they want, so the closest match belongs on top; date_entered DESC stays the default for the entry list, where the question is what is new. user_entries.id is the final tiebreak so paging cannot repeat or drop a row when two entries tie on both.

Sort controls stay hidden during a search. ttrb-qv7i hid them because the client cannot influence the server's order, and that is still true. Filed ttrb-w84a to add a sort param to the endpoint and bring them back with relevance as a search-only column.

Entry gained text_search_condition and text_search_rank as public class methods, plus a private tsquery_sql; the Entry.search scope is now composed from them, so the model test for its ordering still covers the shared expression. Also filed ttrb-wfkk: tsquery_sql still runs sanitize_sql_like on input that is not a LIKE pattern, carried forward unchanged from before the ticket.

title: Entry.search runs the query through sanitize_sql_like before plainto_tsquery (wrong sanitizer)
description:
Current behavior
app/models/entry.rb:

  sanitized = sanitize_sql_like(query)
  where("tsvector_combined @@ plainto_tsquery(english, ?)", sanitized)

sanitize_sql_like escapes LIKE metacharacters (percent, underscore, backslash) by backslash-prefixing them. It exists for LIKE and ILIKE patterns. plainto_tsquery has no LIKE semantics, so the escaping is not protective, it is corrupting: a search for a term containing an underscore or a percent sign gets a stray backslash injected into the text handed to the tokenizer.

This is not a SQL injection hole. The value is still passed as a bind parameter, and the ts_rank ordering interpolates via connection.quote. The bug is correctness and misleading intent: the name suggests the query is being made safe, which invites the next reader to trust the wrong thing.

Expected behavior
Pass the raw query text as a bind parameter to plainto_tsquery. Drop the sanitize_sql_like call. If the ordering expression cannot take a bind, keep connection.quote there but comment why.

Affected files
- app/models/entry.rb (the search scope)

Acceptance criteria
- Searching for a term containing an underscore or a percent sign returns the entries that contain it.
- A model test covers a query with LIKE metacharacters in it.
close_reason: Removed the sanitize_sql_like call and documented why the escaping was never the protection in force; model test pins the metacharacter cases. No result changes, as measured.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Re-scope after ttrb-voe4 (search now returns rows, so this is observable). The correctness half of this ticket does not hold up. Measured plainto_tsquery('english', X) with and without sanitize_sql_like for foo_bar, 50%, C_plus and back\\slash: the tsquery is IDENTICAL in every case ('foo' & 'bar', '50', 'c' & 'plus', 'back' & 'slash'). The tsvector parser already treats _, % and \\ as separators, so prefixing a backslash next to an existing separator changes nothing. The acceptance criterion 'searching for a term containing an underscore or a percent sign returns the entries that contain it' already passes. What remains is the misleading-intent half only: the name says the query is being made safe for something it is not being used for. Suggest dropping to P4 cleanup, or closing.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Downgraded P3 -> P4 on the ttrb-voe4 measurement: the correctness half of this ticket does not survive contact with the evidence. plainto_tsquery('english', X) produces an IDENTICAL tsquery with and without sanitize_sql_like for foo_bar, 50%, C_plus and back\slash ('foo' & 'bar', '50', 'c' & 'plus', 'back' & 'slash'). The parser already treats _, % and \ as separators, so the injected backslash lands beside an existing separator and changes nothing. The stated acceptance criterion passes today.

What remains is real but cosmetic: the code says sanitize_sql_like, which tells the next reader that LIKE escaping is needed here, and it is not. That is worth a comment or a deletion, not a P3 bug. Close it as won't-fix if you would rather not carry it.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 57892f7: dropped the sanitize_sql_like call in Entry.tsquery_sql and put a comment in its place recording the measurement (identical tsquery with and without it) and naming connection.quote as what actually keeps the interpolation safe. Added a model test in test/models/entry_test.rb that a query carrying LIKE metacharacters (foo_bar, 50%) still finds the entry containing them, so the escape cannot come back as a bug fix.

title: Add api.search() to lib/api.ts with typed scope params and result shape
description:
Current behavior
app/javascript/lib/api.ts has no search client. GET /api/v1/search is reachable only by hand. Nothing in app/javascript references it, so the endpoint is effectively dead code.

Expected behavior
An api.search namespace matching the style of the neighbouring api.entries / api.counters clients: build a URLSearchParams from an options object, return a typed response.

Params: q (required), plus the scoping set from the sibling bead (unread, starred, view, feed_id, category_id, tag, fresh_max_age, fresh_per_feed), plus page and per_page.

Response type mirrors what SearchController renders: { query, entries: SearchResult[], pagination: { page, per_page, total, total_pages } }, where SearchResult is { id, entry_id, feed_id, feed_title, title, link, author, published, unread, starred, snippet }. Note this is NOT the same shape as the Entry type the list already renders, so decide whether the UI reuses the entry row component or gets its own.

Affected files
- app/javascript/lib/api.ts
- app/javascript/lib/api.test.ts

Acceptance criteria
- api.search({ q, ...scope }) issues one request with only the provided params serialised.
- A blank or whitespace q does not hit the network.
- Unit test covers param serialisation and the typed response.
close_reason: api.search() added to lib/api.ts in d15ba15 with SearchParams/SearchResult/SearchResponse types and 6 unit tests. Blank q short-circuits without a fetch; scoping params not yet honoured by SearchController are documented in a comment. vitest 659/659, tsc and esbuild clean.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit d15ba15: api.search(params) added to lib/api.ts with SearchResult / SearchResponse / SearchParams types; 6 new tests in api.test.ts cover param serialisation, the full scoping set, q trimming, the typed response, and blank/whitespace q not hitting the network. Verified: vitest 659/659 pass (37 files), tsc --noEmit clean, esbuild build clean. Rails/Minitest and Playwright not run - PostgreSQL is not running in this environment. Client sends unread/starred/view/tag/fresh_max_age/fresh_per_feed but a doc comment records that SearchController ignores them until ttrb-aawe lands; ordering caveat from ttrb-soaj noted there too. No Ruby changed.

title: Search input UI in the entry list with / keybinding (Ctrl+F is already taken)
description:
Add the visible search box. This is the ctrl-f-shaped affordance Andy asked for, except the key cannot be Ctrl+F.

Keybinding constraint
keyboardShortcuts.ts:123 already binds Ctrl+F to page-down-content, paired with Ctrl+B for page-up-content. Rebinding it would break the pager. Use / to focus the search box (free: the catalog currently uses j n k J K space a f S o Enter m u s p i v r F b Escape and Shift+?).

Requirements
- / focuses the search input from anywhere except while typing in another input.
- Escape clears the query and returns to the unfiltered list. Escape is already bound to close-entry, so the search box must swallow it first while focused and non-empty.
- Debounced (roughly 250ms) server query via api.search; in-flight requests for stale queries are discarded so results cannot arrive out of order.
- Empty query returns to the normal list without a request.
- The shortcut goes in shortcutCatalog so the help dialog lists it. The catalog comment is explicit that a shortcut cannot be bound without appearing in the dialog, so add both the ShortcutId and the definition.

Affected files
- app/javascript/lib/keyboardShortcuts.ts (new ShortcutId plus definition)
- app/javascript/components/EntryList.tsx (or a new SearchBar component in components/)
- app/javascript/application.tsx (query state, wiring)
- app/javascript/components/mobile/ (decide whether mobile gets the box; file a follow-up if deferred)

Acceptance criteria
- Pressing / from the list focuses the input; typing into it does not trigger j/k/s/etc.
- Escape with text present clears the search and does not close the open entry; Escape with the box empty falls through to close-entry.
- Rapid typing produces one settled result set matching the final query.
- Vitest coverage for focus, escape precedence, debounce, and out-of-order response discard.
close_reason: Search box lives under the entry-list title, focused with / (Ctrl+F left on page-down-content). Debounced 250ms server query via api.search, sequence-guarded so stale responses cannot land; blank query returns to the unfiltered list with no request. Escape clears a non-empty box without closing the open entry and falls through to close-entry when empty. Binding registered in shortcutCatalog so the help dialog lists it. 33 new vitest tests; suite 700 green.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit 12b1752: search box in EntryList on /, debounced api.search with sequence-guarded responses.

New files: hooks/useEntrySearch.ts (query state, 250ms debounce, stale-response discard, blank-query short circuit), components/SearchBar.tsx (input, clear button, Escape split by state), components/SearchResultList.tsx (hit rows; snippet/highlighting left to ttrb-a81x).
Changed: lib/keyboardShortcuts.ts gains the focus-search ShortcutId bound to / (Ctrl+F left on page-down-content), EntryList.tsx gains an optional `search` prop object, application.tsx wires the hook, the input ref and the focus-search handler.

Scope sent is feed_id + category_id only, since SearchController ignores the rest (ttrb-aawe). Sort controls hide while a search is active because they cannot reorder server-ordered results.

Mobile uses the same EntryList, so the box appears there too; no follow-up filed for it.

Tests: 700 vitest pass (33 new across useEntrySearch, SearchBar incl. a real useKeyboardCommands harness, SearchResultList, EntryList, keyboardShortcuts). tsc --noEmit and esbuild build clean. Layout and key handling verified in Chromium against a standalone bundle with the project Tailwind CSS, light and dark. Rails/Minitest and Playwright not run: no PostgreSQL on this host.

title: Search scope controls: current list vs everything, unread vs deeper history
description:
The search box needs visible, changeable scope. Agreed model:

Default scope is the CURRENT LIST. Whatever the user is looking at (feed, category, view, tag) carries into the query, and the read-state filter of that view carries too, so searching from an unread list searches unread.

Two escapes from that default:
1. Widen to everything: search all subscribed entries regardless of the current feed / category / view.
2. Search deeper into history: include read and archived entries that the current view excludes.

Both need to be visible at a glance, because a result set that silently excludes matches is worse than no search. The scope in effect should be readable in or next to the input (for example "Fresh, unread" as a chip), and the widen control should be reachable without leaving the keyboard.

Consider also surfacing the count of matches outside the current scope, so widening is discoverable rather than something the user has to guess at ("42 more in all history").

Depends on the search endpoint accepting the scoping params and on the search input existing.

Affected files
- the SearchBar component from the sibling bead
- app/javascript/application.tsx (current view state feeds the scope)
- app/javascript/lib/api.ts (params)

Acceptance criteria
- Searching from a feed, a category, a tag, or the Fresh view returns only matches within it by default.
- The widen control returns matches from outside that scope, and the UI states which scope produced the results shown.
- The history toggle brings back read and archived matches; with it off, a read entry matching the query does not appear in an unread-scoped search.
- Scope state survives editing the query and resets on Escape.
close_reason: Two independent scope pills under the search box. Place (feed/category/tag/hide-unstarred/Starred+Published views) and history (unread pref, view fresh + its two params, view archived) each own their params outright, so a pill never describes a filter the other one already dropped. Default is the list as shown; Alt+A / Alt+H widen from inside the box; Escape and the clear button reset scope with the query, typing does not. An empty narrowed result set fetches the unscoped count and offers 'N matches in all articles'. 456eaf0.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 456eaf0: search scope controls. Two independent pills under the search box, place (feed/category/tag/starred-pref/Starred+Published views) and history (unread pref, view fresh, view archived + fresh params). Default is the list as shown; Alt+A / Alt+H widen from inside the box; Escape and the clear button reset scope with the query. Empty narrowed result set fetches the all-articles count and offers 'N matches in all articles'. New: components/SearchScopeControls.tsx. useEntrySearch now takes the whole entriesQuery (snake_case, minus sort/per_page) and exports buildSearchParams for direct param assertions.

title: Render search results with match snippets and term highlighting
description:
SearchController already returns a snippet per result: generate_snippet strips tags, finds the first occurrence of any query word, and returns roughly 200 characters of surrounding context with ellipses. Nothing renders it, and the matched terms inside it are not marked.

Requirements
- Show the snippet under the title in the search result row.
- Highlight the matched terms within both title and snippet.
- Zero-result state that names the scope that produced it, so the user knows to widen rather than concluding the article is gone.

Implementation notes
- Highlighting must not inject unescaped HTML. Split on the match and render React nodes, or mark server-side with a structure the client renders safely. Do not build a dangerouslySetInnerHTML string from user query text.
- components/HighlightedContent.tsx exists but is TTS word-timestamp highlighting, not term matching. Reuse only if the mechanism genuinely fits; otherwise leave it alone rather than generalising it.
- generate_snippet does a plain substring match while the query itself goes through plainto_tsquery stemming, so a stemmed match (running vs run) can return a snippet with no visible highlight. Decide whether to accept that or use ts_headline, which does the stemming-aware version server-side and would replace generate_snippet outright.

Affected files
- app/controllers/api/v1/search_controller.rb (generate_snippet, or a move to ts_headline)
- the search result row component

Acceptance criteria
- A result shows a snippet containing the match in context.
- Query terms are visibly marked in title and snippet, with no HTML injection from the query.
- A query with no matches renders an empty state naming the active scope.
- Stemmed-match behaviour is either handled or documented in the code.

title: Keyboard shortcuts dialog overflows short viewports: single column, no max-height, no scroll
description:
Current behavior
Pressing Shift+? opens KeyboardShortcutsDialog, which renders all 22 shortcuts from shortcutCatalog as one vertical column: DialogContent has className "sm:max-w-md" and the body is a space-y-4 stack of four sections (Navigation, Actions, View, Other), each a space-y-1 list of rows.

The container cannot cope with that height. app/javascript/components/ui/dialog.tsx:39 positions DialogContent as fixed top-[50%] translate-y-[-50%] with NO max-height and NO overflow rule. Once the content is taller than the viewport it grows off the top and bottom simultaneously and there is nothing to scroll, so the first and last shortcuts are simply unreachable. On a MacBook Air, once browser chrome is subtracted, the list is already taller than the window.

This gets worse, not better: the search bead (ttrb-qv7i) adds another catalog entry, and the catalog is designed so every new binding must appear here.

Expected behavior
The dialog fits any viewport it is opened in. Andy asked for a responsive two to three column layout.

Suggested approach
- Lay the sections out in a responsive grid: one column on narrow screens, two at md, three at lg or xl, with the section groups as grid items so a section is not split mid-list.
- Widen DialogContent past sm:max-w-md to give the columns room (for example sm:max-w-2xl lg:max-w-4xl).
- Add a belt-and-braces max-height plus overflow-y-auto on the content, so a viewport short enough to defeat even the three-column layout still scrolls rather than clipping. Consider whether that cap belongs on DialogContent itself in ui/dialog.tsx, since every other dialog in the app inherits the same clipping bug. If it is fixed there, check the other dialogs still look right.

Affected files
- app/javascript/components/KeyboardShortcutsDialog.tsx
- app/javascript/components/ui/dialog.tsx (only if the max-height fix goes in the shared primitive)

Acceptance criteria
- At a 1440x900 viewport the entire catalog is visible without scrolling.
- At a viewport short enough to still overflow, the dialog scrolls internally; no row is clipped off the top or bottom.
- Section headings stay attached to their own shortcuts across all breakpoints.
- Adding a shortcut to the catalog does not require touching the dialog layout.
close_reason: Shortcuts dialog now lays out in responsive CSS columns (1/2/3) at sm:max-w-2xl lg:max-w-4xl, and DialogContent caps at 90dvh with internal scroll for every dialog. Verified in Chromium at 1440x900 (all rows visible, no scroll) and 1440x420 (fits viewport, scrolls internally).

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit dc00895: capped DialogContent at max-h-[90dvh] overflow-y-auto in the shared primitive (tailwind-merge lets EditFeedDialog/SettingsDialog/command palette keep their own sizing), and moved KeyboardShortcutsDialog to CSS columns (columns-1 / md:columns-2 / lg:columns-3, break-inside-avoid per section) at sm:max-w-2xl lg:max-w-4xl. Verified in Chromium against a standalone render: 1440x900 gives 896x566 with all 23 rows visible and no scroll; 1440x420 stays inside the viewport and scrolls internally; 700/900/1440 wide give 1/2/3 columns; every heading sits above its own first row at all four widths. vitest 626 passed (36 files), tsc --noEmit clean, esbuild + tailwind builds clean. Rails/Minitest and Playwright E2E not run (no PostgreSQL in this environment).

title: Browse mode: focus mode + iframe as a site-by-site reader with Nibbler as a top nav bar
description:
Andy wants to enter focus mode with iframe view on and then walk the list with j/k, seeing each original website full-screen with Nibbler reduced to a nav bar at the top.

Most of this already exists and does not need building:
- i toggles iframe view (keyboardShortcuts.ts:182, handleToggleIframe).
- Shift+F toggles focus mode, which drives getSidebarWidth and getListWidth to 0px (application.tsx:805, 815), leaving the EntryContent header row as the only chrome. That header row is already the nav bar in shape.
- useContentPaging is constructed with measurable: !showIframe (application.tsx:711), so Space already skips the unreadable cross-origin scroll and advances to the next entry.
- loadEntry marks an entry read on open (application.tsx:253), so walking the list in this mode already clears unread.

Four things stop it working as a browsing loop. Each is a child bead:
1. iframe view resets to the global preference on every entry change, so j drops you back to RSS view.
2. Once the embedded page takes keyboard focus, the parent listener stops receiving keys, so j/k/i/Escape die.
3. Embed-block detection does not work, so sites that refuse framing show a blank frame rather than the existing fallback panel.
4. The header row is not yet a nav bar: no position indicator, no prev/next, and in focus mode there is no list to tell you where you are.

Sites that refuse framing (X-Frame-Options, CSP frame-ancestors) are a hard ceiling on this feature, not a bug to fix. A meaningful share of news sites cannot be embedded at all. Child 3 is about failing legibly and offering the new-tab escape, not about defeating the header.
close_reason:
All four children closed: ttrb-la5r (53c8471, sticky iframe/RSS toggle), ttrb-gmhv (5a421d5/2276445/124dd79, iframe focus guard + Restore shortcuts), ttrb-watz (e720e56/bcb4302, server-side embed policy probe replacing the unreachable onError path), ttrb-3kh4 (65ddcaa, focus-mode header carries scope + position + prev/next).

Caveat on the epic-level claim: the browsing loop itself has never been exercised end to end in a real browser against the running app, because PostgreSQL was down for this entire run so bin/e2e-server could not boot. Each child was verified with vitest plus a standalone Chromium harness. The end-to-end runs are tracked by ttrb-4tff and ttrb-l2ge; if the loop misbehaves in practice, reopen against those rather than assuming a child regressed.

title: iframe view resets to the global preference on every entry change, breaking j/k browsing
description:
Current behavior
application.tsx:183

  // Reset iframe view to default when entry changes
  useEffect(() => {
    setShowIframe(preferences.content_view_mode === "iframe")
  }, [selectedEntry?.id, preferences.content_view_mode])

The effect keys on selectedEntry?.id, so every navigation snaps showIframe back to the stored preference. Press i to see the original site, press j, and you are back in RSS view. The only way to stay in iframe view while walking the list is to change the global content_view_mode preference, which then also applies to every future session and every reading context.

That makes the intended browsing loop (focus mode plus iframe, iterate with j/k) impossible without a settings round trip.

Expected behavior
The i toggle is sticky for the session. Toggling into iframe view keeps subsequent entries in iframe view until toggled back or the page reloads. The stored preference sets the starting value, not a per-entry reset.

Design note
The existing reset is deliberate, not an accident, and there is a real case for it: someone who reads in RSS view and occasionally peeks at an original page wants the peek to be temporary. The two behaviours conflict. Options:
- Make sticky the plain behaviour and drop the reset. Simplest; the peek user presses i twice.
- Keep the reset but suppress it while focusMode is on, so the browsing loop is sticky and normal reading is not. Narrower, but couples two independent toggles and will surprise someone.
- Add a third preference value. More surface for a small problem.

First option is recommended unless Andy wants the peek behaviour preserved.

Affected files
- app/javascript/application.tsx (the reset effect, showIframe state)
- app/javascript/components/PreferencesPanel.tsx:258 (the help text says toggle with i and describes the preference; update if semantics change)

Acceptance criteria
- With iframe view toggled on, pressing j and k keeps the following entries in iframe view.
- The content_view_mode preference still determines the view on first load.
- Vitest coverage asserting showIframe survives an entry change.
close_reason: i toggle is now sticky for the session; showIframe moved to useContentViewMode with vitest coverage (53c8471)

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 53c8471: showIframe + toggle extracted to hooks/useContentViewMode.ts; the entry-keyed reset effect in application.tsx is gone. Preference still sets the starting value and still applies when changed in settings. Vitest: app/javascript/hooks/useContentViewMode.test.ts (7 cases, incl. iframe view surviving two entry changes); verified the suite fails when the reset is put back. Help text in PreferencesPanel.tsx:258 and locales/en.json updated to say the i toggle lasts the session. Took option one (drop the reset); the RSS-reader peek now costs a second i press.

title: Keyboard shortcuts stop working once the embedded iframe takes focus
description:
Current behavior
The iframe at EntryContent.tsx:330 loads third-party pages cross-origin. Keyboard commands are registered on the parent document via useKeyboardCommands. Once focus moves into the embedded document (the user clicks a link, scrolls by clicking first, or the framed page focuses something itself), keydown events are delivered to the iframe document. The parent cannot listen inside a cross-origin frame, so j, k, i, Escape and Shift+F all stop responding with no visible explanation. Clicking outside the frame is the only recovery, and in focus mode there is very little outside the frame to click.

This is the main thing that would make the browse loop feel broken rather than useful.

Expected behavior
Navigation keys keep working, or the UI makes it obvious that keyboard control has been handed to the page and how to take it back.

Approaches to evaluate
- Do not let the iframe take focus on load, and explicitly focus a parent element after each entry navigation, so the common j-j-j case never loses control.
- Detect the handoff: window blur combined with document.activeElement being the iframe is the standard way to notice focus entered a frame. On detecting it, show an affordance in the nav bar.
- Accept the handoff and make the nav bar fully clickable, so prev / next / exit are reachable with the mouse when keys are gone. This pairs with the nav bar bead and is the reliable fallback, since nothing can force keys back from a cross-origin document.

The first and third together are probably the answer. The second is a nice-to-have signal.

Affected files
- app/javascript/components/EntryContent.tsx (the iframe element, tabIndex and focus handling)
- app/javascript/application.tsx (post-navigation focus)
- app/javascript/hooks/useKeyboardCommands.ts

Acceptance criteria
- After navigating with j into an entry in iframe view, pressing j again advances without any click.
- After clicking inside the embedded page, there is a visible, clickable way to advance and to exit focus mode.
- Behaviour is verified against a real embeddable site, not only a test double, since focus semantics are browser behaviour.
close_reason: useIframeFocusGuard anchors focus in the reader's document after each entry navigation and on the first frame load, and surfaces a Restore shortcuts button when the embedded page takes the keys anyway. Verified in real Chromium against a cross-origin frame, including the counterfactual. E2E spec committed; running it against the app is ttrb-4tff (PostgreSQL down here).

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 5a421d5: useIframeFocusGuard hook + EntryContent wiring. Anchors focus on a tabIndex=-1 wrapper after each entry navigation and on the first frame load, detects the cross-origin handoff via window blur + activeElement === iframe, and renders a Restore shortcuts button in the header while it lasts. 10 hook tests + 6 EntryContent tests; full vitest suite 608 passing, tsc clean. E2E verification against a real browser frame still to come.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commits 2276445 (e2e spec) and 124dd79 (comment reword).

Real-browser verification (AC 3): PostgreSQL is down on this host, so bin/e2e-server could not boot and the committed Playwright spec has not been executed - filed as ttrb-4tff. The mechanism was instead verified directly in Chromium with a standalone harness that loaded the shipped useIframeFocusGuard into a page at https://reader.invalid embedding https://e2e.invalid (both served through page.route, so genuinely cross-origin, nothing left the machine). 11/11 checks passed:
- focus stays in the reader document after the frame loads (activeElement=DIV)
- j advances with no click in between
- clicking into the frame is detected and shows the affordance
- the keypress lands in the embedded document (input value 'j') and the reader sees nothing
- the header Next button still advances by mouse during the handoff
- Restore shortcuts clears the badge, returns focus, and j advances again

Counterfactual, same harness with the first-load reclaim disabled: a framed page that scripts its own focus takes activeElement=IFRAME and j stops advancing entirely. That is the bug as reported, reproduced and fixed. Note Chromium ignores the autofocus attribute in a cross-origin subframe but honours a scripted focus(), so the e2e fixture page uses the scripted form.

title: iframe onError never fires for X-Frame-Options or CSP refusals, so the embed-block fallback is dead code
description:
Current behavior
EntryContent.tsx has a good fallback for un-embeddable sites at line 315: a Globe icon, the message "Unable to load original page. This site may block embedding", and an Open in new tab button. It is gated on iframeError, and the only thing that sets iframeError is line 334:

  onError={() => setIframeError(true)}

Browsers do not fire an error event on an iframe element when the frame is refused by X-Frame-Options or a CSP frame-ancestors directive. The navigation is blocked at the network or commit layer and the element typically reports load, not error, with the parent unable to inspect the resulting document because it is cross-origin. So iframeError stays false and the user gets a blank white frame with no explanation instead of the fallback that was written for exactly this case.

Needs verification in the target browsers before choosing a fix. Confirm what actually fires in Chrome, Firefox and Safari for a site sending X-Frame-Options DENY. The code fact (onError is the sole trigger) is confirmed; the browser behaviour is the part to test.

This matters more than usual here because the browse-mode epic makes iframe view the primary reading surface, and a large share of news sites refuse framing.

Approaches
- Server-side probe: HEAD or GET the entry link when the feed is fetched, record whether X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors forbids embedding, and store it on the entry or feed. Then the client knows before rendering and can show the fallback immediately, or skip iframe view for that entry. Costs a request per entry and can go stale, but it is the only reliable signal.
- Client-side timeout heuristic: if no load event within N seconds, assume blocked. Cheap, and wrong often enough to annoy.
- Per-feed flag: many blocking sites block everything, so recording it per feed rather than per entry is much cheaper and nearly as accurate.

Affected files
- app/javascript/components/EntryContent.tsx (iframeError, the fallback branch)
- app/models/feed.rb or app/models/entry.rb plus a migration, if the probe result is stored
- app/jobs/update_feeds_job.rb, if the probe runs at fetch time

Acceptance criteria
- A site that refuses framing shows the existing fallback panel with the new-tab escape, not a blank frame.
- The detection mechanism is documented in the code with the browser behaviour it relies on.
- A site that embeds fine is not falsely reported as blocked.
close_reason: Fixed. The onError handler was unreachable, not merely unreliable: verified in Chromium 151 and Firefox 153 that a frame refused by X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors fires load, never error, and is opaque to the parent in exactly the way a successful cross-origin frame is. Replaced it with a server-side header read (EmbedPolicyProbe + GET /api/v1/entries/:id/embed_policy) consumed by a new useEmbedPolicy hook, so the existing fallback panel now appears for sites that refuse framing. Commits e720e56 and bcb4302. Ruby tests written but unrun (no database); follow-up in ttrb-l2ge.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Browser behaviour verified before choosing a fix, with a standalone Playwright harness (no app server): a parent page on a routed fake origin framing https://xfo.test/ (X-Frame-Options: DENY), https://xfosame.test/ (SAMEORIGIN), https://csp.test/ (frame-ancestors 'none') and an embeddable control.

Chromium 151.0.7922.34 and Firefox 153.0, identical results: the blocked frames fired 'load' and never 'error'. Every probe from the parent came back byte-identical to the embeddable control - contentDocument null, contentWindow.location/origin/history all SecurityError, contentWindow.length 0, one resource-timing entry. The refusal commits a document on the target's own origin, so it is opaque in exactly the way a successful cross-origin frame is. The only trace is a console message ('Refused to display ... X-Frame-Options'), which script cannot read. WebKit could not be launched (installed build 2287 vs the driver's expected 2336) so Safari is unverified, but the mechanism is the navigation-block path, not a vendor quirk.

Conclusion: no client-side signal exists. onError was not merely unreliable, it is unreachable, and no heuristic on the parent side can separate blocked from loaded. The issue's server-probe approach is the only one that works.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit e720e56: EmbedPolicyProbe plus GET /api/v1/entries/:id/embed_policy. HEAD with a GET fallback, frame-ancestors takes precedence over X-Frame-Options, Report-Only is ignored, ALLOW-FROM and unparseable XFO values are treated as permission (no current browser enforces them, and reporting them blocked would put the fallback in front of pages that frame fine). Definite answers cached 12h; unknowns are not cached. OFFLINE_FEED_FETCH short-circuits it so the Playwright suite stays hermetic.

Commit bcb4302: useEmbedPolicy hook, api.entries.embedPolicy, EntryContent gated on the probe instead of the dead onError, which is removed. The frame mounts without waiting and is swapped for the panel on a refusal.

Verification (PostgreSQL is not running in this session, so Minitest and Playwright could not run):
- EmbedPolicyProbe exercised end to end against a real TCPServer serving real headers, driven through 'bin/rails runner': 20/20 cases pass, covering DENY, SAMEORIGIN, lowercase, ALLOW-FROM, garbage, doubled values, frame-ancestors none/self+partner/star/absent, report-only, CSP overriding XFO, multi-policy headers, HEAD 405 falling back to GET, redirect following, HTTP 500, blank URL, connection refused and the offline switch.
- EmbedPolicyProbe.for caching verified the same way: two calls, one request; an unknown leaves nothing in the cache. Route resolution verified with recognize_path.
- vitest 640/640 (37 files), including 9 new useEmbedPolicy examples and 5 new EntryContent examples.
- tsc --noEmit clean, esbuild build clean, rubocop clean on the four Ruby files, brakeman 0 warnings.

Not run: test/services/embed_policy_probe_test.rb (20 examples, written but needs the database via test_helper's 'fixtures :all'), the Minitest suite, and the Playwright suite.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Created ttrb-l2ge for the verification that PostgreSQL being down blocked: one real run of test/services/embed_policy_probe_test.rb, the controller action end to end, and E2E coverage of the fallback panel.

title: Focus mode header needs to work as a nav bar: position in list, prev/next, and scope
description:
In focus mode the sidebar and list collapse to 0px (application.tsx:805, 815), leaving the EntryContent header row as the only Nibbler chrome. It currently carries the entry title and a set of icon buttons (star, published, open original, focus toggle). That is close to the nav bar Andy wants, but it is missing what a browsing loop needs.

Missing
- Position in the list. With the list hidden there is no way to know you are on 3 of 42, or how much is left. This is the main orientation loss in focus mode.
- Prev / next controls. Keyboard is the only way to move, which is a problem exactly when the embedded page has stolen the keys (see the sibling focus bead). Clickable prev/next is the fallback that makes the mode recoverable.
- Which list you are walking. Feed title or view name, so it is clear whether you are in Fresh, a single feed, or a tag.
- The keyboard-shortcut affordances are already there for star and published, so those need no work.

Constraint
The bar must stay short. The point of the mode is the site below it, so this is one compact row, not a toolbar that grows. Prefer a count and a feed name over labels, and keep the existing icon buttons rather than adding text.

Depends on nothing technically, but it is what makes the iframe focus-theft bead recoverable, so build it alongside.

Affected files
- app/javascript/components/EntryContent.tsx (header row)
- app/javascript/application.tsx (entry index within the loaded list, current scope name; getListTitle already computes the scope label around line 795)

Acceptance criteria
- In focus mode the bar shows the current position in the list and the name of the list being walked.
- Prev and next are clickable and move the same way j and k do.
- The bar height does not grow relative to today.
- The bar is legible at the same width in both iframe and RSS view.
close_reason: Focus-mode header now shows scope name and position (N / M) and its prev/next call the same handlers as j/k. Same 48px row, verified in Chromium at 640-1920px in both iframe and RSS view. E2E spec added but unrun (no PostgreSQL).

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 65ddcaa: header carries scope name + 1-based position (focus mode only), on the same h-12 row; prev/next rewired to handleKeyboardPrevious/handleKeyboardNext for j/k parity. 5 vitest cases in EntryContent.test.tsx, new e2e/focus-mode-nav.spec.ts (UNRUN - no PostgreSQL). Chromium harness measured barH=48px, no overflow, at 640/700/800/900/1024/1400/1920 in both iframe and RSS view.

title: Virtual folder badges (Fresh, Starred, Published) scroll out of view when categories expand
description:
Current behavior
FeedSidebar.tsx:857 opens a single ScrollArea with className "flex-1" that runs all the way to line 1232. Everything below the header is inside it: the item-list and stories virtual folders (All Feeds, Fresh, Starred, Published, Stories, rendered from getVirtualFoldersByMode at line 864), then the feed-list smart folders, then the category tree, then Tags, then Errors.

So the virtual folders are just the first rows of one long scrolling column. Expanding categories grows the content below them, the viewport scrolls, and Fresh with its badge disappears off the top. The counts Andy actually navigates by become invisible exactly when the tree is open, which is most of the time.

The sidebar header at line 752 is already shrink-0 and stays put, so the pattern for a pinned region is established in the same file.

Expected behavior
The virtual folder rows and their badges stay visible regardless of how far the category tree is expanded or scrolled.

Approaches
- Move the virtual-folder block out of the ScrollArea into its own shrink-0 section above it, so only the feed and category tree scrolls. Cleanest structurally and matches how the header already works. Watch the p-2 padding, which currently wraps the whole scrolled column and would need splitting across the two regions.
- Keep it inside the viewport and make it sticky top-0 with an opaque background. Fewer structural changes, but sticky inside a Radix ScrollArea viewport needs the background to fully cover the rows sliding under it, and the drag-and-drop DndContext wraps this region, so check that sticky positioning does not confuse drop targets.

First option is recommended.

Also check the collapsed rail variant at line 594. Its virtual folder column at line 612 is a plain flex-1 with no scroll container, so it may clip rather than scroll if the list grows. Confirm whether that path has the same or a different failure.

Affected files
- app/javascript/components/FeedSidebar.tsx (the ScrollArea at 857, the virtual folder block at 864, the collapsed rail at 594)

Acceptance criteria
- With every category expanded and the tree scrolled to the bottom, Fresh, Starred and Published and their badges are still visible.
- Drag and drop of feeds between categories still works.
- The collapsed rail is checked and either fixed or confirmed unaffected.
- Sidebar looks right at desktop, tablet and mobile widths.
close_reason: Virtual folders pinned outside the ScrollArea; badges stay visible with the tree fully expanded and scrolled to the bottom. Verified in Chromium against a git-HEAD baseline at three widths, plus drag-and-drop and background-refresh scroll preservation. Collapsed rail confirmed unaffected.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit 3b410b4: moved the item-list/stories virtual folders (All Feeds, Fresh, Starred, Published, Stories) out of the ScrollArea into a shrink-0 region between the header and the scroll viewport. Padding split: pinned block gets px-2 pt-2 pb-1 plus border-b, the scroll content keeps its p-2. Added 7 vitest cases asserting the rows render outside [data-slot=scroll-area-viewport] while the category tree renders inside it.

Browser evidence (standalone Chromium harness bundling the real FeedSidebar with the project's Tailwind CSS; Postgres is down so Rails/Minitest and Playwright E2E could not run):
- Tree scrolled to the bottom at 1440x900 (2680px of scroll). Baseline built from git HEAD: the five rows at top=-2530..-2370, off screen. Working tree: top=137..297, badges 137/22/9 intact. Same result at 820x700 and 390x640.

- ttrb-7ktq interaction: three simulated background-refresh polls replacing the feeds array left scrollTop at 900 in both baseline and fixed builds, so the pinned region does not disturb scroll restoration.
