title: Four llm_client_test.rb examples assert nothing and Minitest says so
description:
`bin/rails test` prints 'Test is missing assertions' for four examples in test/services/llm_client_test.rb: test_sends_stream:_false_in_request_body (:52), test_does_not_request_format:_json_when_format_is_nil (:85), test_sends_configured_model_in_request_body (:240) and test_can_override_model_per-instance (:248).

Each stubs a request with `.with(body: hash_including(...))` and then calls the client, relying on WebMock raising NetConnectNotAllowedError when the body does not match. That does test something, but it leaves the assertion count at zero and the intent implicit. An `assert_requested` on the stub would state the expectation and silence the warning.

Noticed while running the full suite for ttrb-l2ge; unrelated to that work.

title: e2e/iframe-keyboard-focus.spec.ts:151 asserts toBeHidden on an element clipped by an ancestor, so focus mode reads as not-entered and CI is red
description: CI run 33274819083 (push of 29fbf96 to main) failed. The test_e2e job: 226 passed, 5 skipped, 1 failed, across 3 attempts including both retries. The single failure: [chromium] > e2e/iframe-keyboard-focus.spec.ts:145:7 "focus mode can be left by mouse after the frame takes the keys" Error: expect(locator).toBeHidden() failed Locator: getByText("NibbleRSS") Expected: hidden Received: visible 14 x locator resolved to NibbleRSS Line 151, immediately after `await page.keyboard.press("Shift+F")`. THIS IS A TEST DEFECT, NOT A PRODUCT BUG. Verified by reading the source rather than inferring: - The string renders once in the app chrome, at app/javascript/components/FeedSidebar.tsx:792. - Focus mode collapses the sidebar via getSidebarWidth() returning "0px" (application.tsx:906), and the wrapper div at application.tsx:1044-1050 carries `width: getSidebarWidth()` together with `overflow: "hidden"`. So in focus mode the span is inside a zero-width, overflow-hidden ancestor: correctly invisible to a human. Playwright determines visibility from the element having a non-empty bounding box and not being visibility:hidden or display:none. It does NOT account for an ancestor clipping the element out of view. A clipped span keeps its own box, so toBeHidden never becomes true and the assertion can never pass, on any machine. It is not flaky and it is not environment-dependent. The spec was written during ttrb-gmhv (commit 2276445) and committed without ever executing, because PostgreSQL was down for that entire run so bin/e2e-server could not boot at db:prepare. ttrb-gmhv explicitly named `getByText("NibbleRSS")` as the focus-mode visibility probe most likely to need fixing on first real run. It was right. Fix options, in preference order: 1. Assert on the collapsing container instead of its descendant: give the sidebar wrapper a testid and assert its width is 0px, or assert the container is hidden. This tests what focus mode actually does. 2. `await expect(page.getByText("NibbleRSS")).not.toBeInViewport()`, which does respect clipping. Do NOT "fix" this by adding display:none to the sidebar in focus mode; the 150ms width transition at application.tsx:1048 is deliberate and display:none would kill it. Line 158 asserts the same locator toBeVisible after exiting focus mode. That direction works and should stay, though it should move to whatever handle option 1 introduces so both assertions test the same thing. Acceptance criteria: - `npm run test:e2e` passes with 0 failures. - The focus-mode assertion fails if focus mode stops collapsing the sidebar (verify by temporarily making getSidebarWidth return "240px" unconditionally and watching it go red). - No product code changes unless the counterfactual above reveals a real bug. Related: ttrb-4tff tracks running this spec generally; this is the specific defect that run surfaced. The same CI run also had 12 Ruby errors, which are a separate cause already tracked by ttrb-l2ge.
close_reason: Focus mode now asserted on the sidebar pane's own width via data-testid=sidebar-pane, instead of on text a zero-width overflow-hidden ancestor clips. Counterfactual verified red. Also removed a boot-time list reload that closed articles opened right after load, which was three more failures in the same spec. Full e2e green twice: 236 passed / 5 skipped / 0 failed. Commit 74d277c.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit 74d277c. Root cause confirmed by running the spec, not by reading it: getByText("NibbleRSS")).toBeHidden() failed identically on every attempt. Fixed with option 1 from the description - data-testid="sidebar-pane" on the wrapper at application.tsx, both directions now assert its computed width (0px entered, 240px exited, which also waits out the 150ms transition).

Counterfactual done as required: with getSidebarWidth forced to return "240px" unconditionally the new assertion fails with Expected "0px" / Received "240px". Reverted after. The old assertion failed in both worlds, so it distinguished nothing.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
The first real run of the spec found more than the one CI reported. Baseline on c3fcba6, full suite: 232 passed / 5 skipped / 4 failed. One was the toBeHidden defect; the other three were openFirstEntry timing out on the iframe with nothing selected. CI only ever showed one because retries: 2 covered the other three.

Two independent boot races were behind them.

1. The list reloaded itself once on boot for a query that had not changed. entriesQuery depended on preferences.entries_sort_config; GET /api/v1/preferences carries no such key, so the value went "date:desc" -> undefined when preferences landed while the resolved sort did not move. The reload runs loadEntries, which calls setSelectedEntry(null), closing an article opened in the first fraction of a second. Fixed in this commit by depending on the resolved sort string. Network trace: two identical GET /api/v1/entries on boot before, one after. Deliberately NOT fixed by adding entries_sort_config to the server defaults - that would always win over the legacy entries_sort_by_score fallback at application.tsx:252 and :603 and silently ignore it for users who still have it stored. Filed as ttrb-bbjz.

2. ttrb-lix7: useKeyboardCommands swaps its document keydown listener in a passive effect, so a press between paint and effect flush is handled by the previous render's closure and dropped at handleKeyboardNext's entries.length === 0 guard. Instrumented evidence: on a lost press there is no GET /api/v1/entries/<id> at all, and a second press milliseconds later works. Roughly 2 in 30. Not fixed here - it touches every shortcut in the app and a race needs a test that proves the mechanism, not one green run. openFirstEntry retries the press with a comment pointing at the ticket.

title: CI actions are on Node 20 and being force-migrated to Node 24: actions/setup-node@v4 (3 uses) and actions/upload-artifact@v4
description:
CI run 33274819083 carried this annotation on the test_e2e job:

  Node.js 20 is deprecated. The following actions target Node.js 20 but are
  being forced to run on Node.js 24: actions/setup-node@v4,
  actions/upload-artifact@v4.
  https://github.blog/changelog/2025-09-19-deprecation-of-node-20-on-github-actions-runners/

Affected lines in .github/workflows/ci.yml:
- actions/setup-node@v4 at :86, :106, :150
- actions/upload-artifact@v4 at :169

actions/checkout is already @v5 (:14, :33, :76, :103, :142) and actions/cache@v4 (:41) was not named in the annotation.

Right now this is a warning and the jobs still run, because the runner silently substitutes Node 24. That substitution is the risk, not the warning: the actions are executing on a runtime they were not tested against, and when the runners stop offering the fallback the jobs fail outright rather than warn. This is cheap to do now and becomes an outage later.

Fix: bump actions/setup-node to @v5 and actions/upload-artifact to @v5, confirm the input names did not change across the major (upload-artifact v4 to v5 is the one worth reading the changelog for), and push a branch to watch CI go green before it lands on main.

Acceptance criteria:
- No Node 20 deprecation annotation on a CI run.
- All five jobs (test, test_js, test_e2e, lint, scan_ruby) still pass.
- The Playwright failure artifact upload still produces a downloadable artifact on a deliberately failing run.

Discovered while reading CI run 33274819083 after the 29fbf96 push. Not the cause of that run failing; see ttrb-8zv5 and ttrb-l2ge for the two real failures.

- :578 "can add and remove rules"
- :605 "validation prevents empty filter creation"

These are pre-existing and predate the bdexec run that surfaced them; nothing in that run touched filters. They are `test.skip`, not `test.fixme` and not conditionally skipped, so they never run anywhere and never report as pending work. Taken together they are the entire end-to-end path for creating a filter through the UI: opening the dialog, filling it, adding and removing rules, and rejecting an empty submission. Filters can be created by a user and nothing exercises that in a browser.

The skips carry no recorded reason, so the first task is to find out why. Two likely readings, and they lead to different work:
1. They were flaky and got silenced. Then the fix is to make them deterministic, and the flake probably indicates a real race in the dialog.
2. They were written against a dialog that has since changed and never updated. Then they need rewriting against the current markup, and the coverage gap has been open for however long that is.

`git log -S "test.skip" -- e2e/filters-labels.spec.ts` and the blame on those lines should settle it.

Acceptance criteria:
- Each of the five either runs and passes, or is deleted with a written reason in the commit message. No test stays skipped without one.
- Any that are restored pass `--repeat-each=3` rather than once, since flake is a live hypothesis.
- If the investigation finds a product bug behind an original flake, file it separately rather than folding the fix in here.

Discovered while reading CI run 33274819083.

title: One entry failing 'Content can't be blank' aborts the entire feed refresh, so feed 2 has never updated
description:
Seen in production job logs on every 5-minute cycle after the 29fbf96 deploy:

  [ActiveJob] [UpdateFeedJob] Failed to update feed 2 (Braintree, MA - News Flash):
  Database error: Validation failed: Content can*t be blank

Mechanism, read from source rather than inferred:
- app/models/entry.rb:26 has `validates :content, presence: true`.
- app/services/feed_fetcher.rb:66 has a broad `rescue StandardError => e` that turns the
  ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid into a feed-level "Database error" failure.

So one item in the feed with no content aborts the whole refresh for that feed. Every other
entry in the same fetch is discarded along with it. Feed 2 fails identically on every cycle,
which means it has not ingested anything for as long as that item has been in the feed, and
it never will on its own.

Blank content is not exotic. Headline-only and link-only feeds are a normal RSS shape,
municipal news flashes especially. Treating an item with no body as invalid is the questionable
half here, not the item.

Two candidate fixes, and they are not equivalent:
1. Per-entry isolation: rescue around each entry so one bad item is skipped and counted, and
   the rest of the feed still lands. This is worth doing regardless, because ANY per-entry
   failure currently costs the whole batch.
2. Reconsider the validation: allow blank content, or synthesize it from title/summary at
   ingest. Needs a decision about what an entry with no body should render as.

Do 1 first. It is the general fix and it stops one malformed item from silently freezing a feed.
2 is a product question about what Nibbler stores for bodyless items.

Acceptance criteria:
- A feed containing one invalid item still ingests its valid items.
- The skipped item is recorded somewhere the user or the logs can see, not swallowed.
- Feed 2 ingests on the next cycle after the fix.
- A test covers a feed whose payload mixes valid and invalid items, asserting the valid ones persist.

Discovered while verifying the ttrb-k1qa deploy. Not caused by that change; it failed the same
way under the previous :async execution mode.
close_reason: Per-entry savepoint isolation so one unstorable item cannot discard the batch (d98179a), plus blank content allowed with a reader empty state for headline-only items (0d01df0). Live Braintree payload goes from 0 of 50 stored with a feed-level Database error to all 50 stored, 20 bodyless. All four suites green.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit d98179a: per-entry isolation. process_entries now writes each entry inside its own savepoint (ActiveRecord::Base.transaction(requires_new: true)), so a per-entry failure rolls back only that item. Skips are warned to the log with feed id + guid and carried on UpdateResult#skipped_entries; UpdateFeedJob appends ', N skipped' to its success line.

Trace correction: the broad rescue is at app/services/feed_updater.rb:107 (process_entries), not feed_fetcher.rb:66. feed_fetcher.rb:66 only wraps the HTTP call and never sees an ActiveRecord error. The 'Database error:' string comes from feed_updater.rb:108.

Worse than described: all entries shared ONE ActiveRecord::Base.transaction, so a raise also rolled back the feed metadata update and every previously-created entry in the same fetch.

Test confirmed RED first against original code: 12 runs, 8 failures, 2 errors, with the acceptance assertion reporting Expected :ok / Actual :error.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
PART 2 DECISION: relax the validation. validates :content, presence: true is replaced by validates :content, exclusion: { in: [nil] }.

Evidence, not judgement. Fetched the live feed and parsed it: 20 of the 50 items in Braintree, MA - News Flash carry a title and a link and no body. That is 40 percent of the feed. A rule that rejects 40 percent of a working municipal feed is describing the feed wrong, not the feed being malformed. Headline-only is the shape CivicPlus news flashes have.

Rejected the alternative of synthesizing content from title/summary: it would duplicate the title into the body (the reader already renders the title as an h1), and it would make content_hash - the update-detection hash - a function of the title, so a genuine later body edit could not be told from no change.

nil is still rejected: entries.content is NOT NULL and update_tsvector reads the value on every save, so "" is the only legal way to have no body.

RENDERING, checked before committing to it as instructed:
- Entry list row: no change needed. The server sends content_preview: null for a blank body and the row's preview block is conditional, so the snippet line collapses cleanly. No empty element.
- Reader pane: this WAS the empty pane the ticket warned about. EntryContent.tsx piped "" into dangerouslySetInnerHTML on the prose div, giving a zero-height block - a header over whitespace with no hint the article is one click away. Added an empty state: 'This item has no article text. The feed published a headline and a link only.' plus two named actions, 'Read the page here' (frames the original via onToggleIframe) and 'Open the original site'. Wording deliberately differs from the header's icon-button labels so the two do not collide as duplicate accessible names - the first draft did collide and RTL caught it with 'Found multiple elements with the role button'.

SEARCH, checked because content feeds the tsvector: no degradation, because search is already completely broken. Verified on PRE-FIX code (worktree at ed52fc2, entry WITH a full body, valid under the old validation): tsvector_combined = nil, search('Zebra') = [], 0 of 3 rows have a tsvector. Content presence was never load-bearing for the index. Root cause filed as ttrb-voe4. Distinct from ttrb-20gl (sanitize_sql_like misuse) and ttrb-clec (ts_headline snippets); neither touched.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit 0d01df0: blank content allowed + reader empty state. Closes the ticket with d98179a.

FAILS-FIRST EVIDENCE (asked for explicitly). Ran the FINAL test file against pre-d98179a code in a throwaway worktree at ed52fc2:

  FeedUpdaterTest#test_stores_the_good_items_in_a_payload_that_also_contains_an_unstorable_one:
    one bad item must not fail the whole fetch.
    Expected: :ok
      Actual: :error

  FeedUpdaterTest#test_counts_only_the_items_it_actually_stored:
    Expected: 3
      Actual: 0

  12 runs, 13 assertions, 7 failures, 3 errors, 0 skips

That is the mixed valid/invalid payload asserting the valid items persist, red before the fix. Green after.

FOUR SUITES, all on the committed tree:
  bin/rails test        537 runs, 1565 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skips  (baseline 519/1527; +18 new)
  npm run test:run      809 passed, 46 files                                      (baseline 804/46; +5 new)
  npm run test:e2e      260 passed, 5 skipped                                     (baseline unchanged)
  bundle exec rubocop   196 files, no offenses                                    (baseline 194; +2 new ruby files)
  npm run typecheck     clean

E2E note: the first E2E run overlapped a probe that briefly reverted feed_updater.rb and entry.rb on disk, so it was discarded and re-run on a stable, untouched tree. The 260/5 above is the clean run.

Also filed ttrb-voe4 (P1) for the tsvector bug found along the way.

title: Five feeds fail on every 5-minute cycle with no user-visible signal; nothing disables or surfaces a permanently broken feed
description:
Production job logs after the 29fbf96 deploy show the same five feeds failing on every single cron cycle (3 for 3 in the sampled window). Nothing in the UI says so, and nothing backs them off, so they burn a fetch attempt every five minutes indefinitely.

Diagnosed individually rather than lumped together, because the causes differ:

1. Feed 1 (BINJ) - binjonline.com: getaddrinfo Name or service not known
2. Feed 56 (flak) - flak.tedunangst.com: getaddrinfo Name or service not known
   Both confirmed dead from outside the container: `getent hosts` fails for both on iris.
   These domains do not resolve anywhere. Not a container DNS problem, genuinely gone.

3. Feed 72 (Information Is Beautiful): SSL certificate verify failed, unable to get local
   issuer certificate. NOT our CA bundle. Reproduced from iris with openssl s_client:
   "Verify return code: 21 (unable to verify the first certificate)", issuer
   "Starfield Secure Certificate Authority - G2". The site serves an incomplete chain,
   omitting the intermediate. Browsers paper over this by fetching the issuer via the AIA
   extension; Ruby OpenSSL does not. Options: fetch/pin the Starfield intermediate, or treat
   this feed as broken until the site fixes its chain.

4. Feed 44 (codename goose Blog): "Feed not found". A 404, presumably moved or withdrawn.

5. Feed 2 (Braintree, MA): filed separately, it is our own validation bug, not feed health.

The individual feeds matter less than the missing mechanism: a feed can fail forever and the
only place it shows is container logs nobody reads. There is no failure count, no last-success
timestamp surfaced, no automatic backoff, and no "this feed is broken" state in the sidebar.

Wanted:
- Persist consecutive failure count and last error per feed.
- Back off the retry interval as failures accumulate, instead of a flat 5 minutes forever.
- Surface broken state in the UI where the feed is listed, with the last error available.
- After some threshold, stop fetching and require an explicit re-enable.

Then triage the five above: 1 and 56 are almost certainly delete, 44 needs a URL check,
72 is a decision about the intermediate.

Acceptance criteria:
- A feed failing N consecutive times is visibly marked in the UI.
- Retry interval grows rather than staying flat.
- The last error is readable without shelling into a container.
- Fixing a feed URL clears the state.

Discovered while verifying the ttrb-k1qa deploy. Pre-existing; unrelated to that change.

title: Tailwind dark: variant follows the OS, not the app theme
description:
Discovered while doing ttrb-w6ob (theme registry).

application.tailwind.css never declares a custom dark variant, so Tailwind v4 compiles `dark:` utilities to `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` rather than keying them off the theme class. Verified in the built CSS:

    grep -o 'prefers-color-scheme[^}]*' app/assets/builds/application.css
    prefers-color-scheme:dark){.dark\:bg-destructive\/60{background-color:#ef444499

Effect: a user who pins Light while their OS is dark still gets the dark-variant utilities, and vice versa. Nine call sites across NibblerLogo, ui/input, ui/textarea, ui/badge, ui/context-menu and FeedOrganizer.

This gets worse with ttrb-xj40's extra palettes: a gruvbox-dark theme picked on a light OS would get none of the dark-variant styling, and NibblerLogo's `dark:bg-white` would be wrong in both directions.

Fix is a one-liner in application.tailwind.css:

    @custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *));

ThemeContext already puts the `dark` class on <html> for every theme whose registry base is dark (see app/javascript/lib/themes.ts), so the variant would immediately track the app theme for all palettes. Needs a visual pass over the nine call sites afterwards, since some of them have never actually rendered in the state their author intended.
close_reason: @custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *)) added to application.tailwind.css; built CSS now emits zero prefers-color-scheme rules and all 13 dark: rules key off the class. Four regression specs in e2e/settings.spec.ts pin a palette against the opposite emulated colorScheme in both directions and all fail without the variant. Visual pass over all nine call sites recorded in the comments. Commit 5fb9f95.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Visual check while building the new palettes (ttrb-nkhp): the most visible of the nine dark: call sites is NibblerLogo.tsx line 15 (dark:bg-white dark:p-0.5), which puts a white disc behind the logo. Pinning Gruvbox Dark on a light-preference OS drops that disc. The logo stays legible against the warm background, so this is cosmetic rather than blocking, but it is the one a user will notice first.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit 5fb9f95: added `@custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *))` to application.tailwind.css and four regression specs in e2e/settings.spec.ts that pin a palette against the opposite emulated colorScheme. Built CSS now has zero prefers-color-scheme occurrences (was 1 media block holding all 13 emitted dark: rules).

Visual pass, measured in Chromium with the OS preference set opposite to the pinned palette, before vs after:

REACHABLE AND CHANGED
- NibblerLogo.tsx:15 dark:bg-white / dark:p-0.5 - Dark or Gruvbox Dark on a light-preference OS went from transparent/0px to white/2px. The logo glyph is near-black, so without the disc it sank into the dark background; this is the change a reader sees. Reverse direction: Sepia or Light on a dark OS had a white disc on a cream/white card, now transparent.
- ui/input.tsx:11 and ui/textarea.tsx:10 dark:bg-input/30 - verified on the real <Input> in Settings > Account. Dark on a light OS: was rgba(0,0,0,0), now oklab(0.2686 .../0.3), so the field reads as a field instead of a flat black rectangle. Sepia on a dark OS: was a muddy tan wash over the cream card, now transparent.
- ui/context-menu.tsx:127 - the hovered Unsubscribe row. Dark on a light OS went 10% -> 20% destructive; Sepia on a dark OS went 20% -> 10%.
- FeedOrganizer.tsx:96 dark:text-green-400 - see the ttrb-x7fn note; the ratio roughly doubles on every light palette.

REACHABLE, VISUAL EFFECT ONLY ONCE A DESTRUCTIVE BADGE EXISTS
- ui/badge.tsx:17 dark:bg-destructive/60 and dark:focus-visible:ring-destructive/40 - correct in the probe, but no call site renders <Badge variant="destructive">, so nothing shows today.

UNREACHABLE TODAY
- ui/input.tsx:13, ui/textarea.tsx:12, ui/badge.tsx:8 dark:aria-invalid:ring-destructive/40 - nothing in app/javascript sets aria-invalid, so these three have never rendered at all. Correct under the probe (40% under a dark palette, 20% ring under a light one).

NO REGRESSION WHERE THE OS AND THE PALETTE AGREE: pixel-diffing the full reader screenshot for light-OS+Light and dark-OS+Dark gives an empty bbox, zero changed pixels.

SYSTEM SELECTION STILL FOLLOWS THE OS. ThemeContext subscribes to the media query and resolves "system" to a concrete palette before applying, so the class it writes already encodes the OS preference; keying the variant off the class does not break it. Covered by 'system follows the OS preference', which also fails without the variant.

Screenshots settled 600ms after each theme swap per ttrb-a81x.

title: iframe keeps showing the previous article's page: src is mutated in place and the frame does not renavigate
description:
Reported by Andy after ttrb-la5r landed: "i now toggles into iframe mode, which is great, and the iframe mode is kept when you go to the next article... but the iframe src does not update. you dont see the next items page."

So the sticky-iframe fix works and this is the gap it exposed: iframe view now survives navigation, which is the first time anyone walks j/k with the same iframe element on screen for more than one entry.

Confirmed from the code
- EntryContent.tsx:410-417 renders the iframe with src={entry.link} and NO key prop.
- The iframe sits inside a persistent wrapper div (the iframeFocus.anchorRef element at line 385) that does not change identity across entries.
- Therefore React reconciles the same DOM node on every entry change and mutates the src attribute in place rather than mounting a fresh element.

NOT confirmed: why the frame then fails to navigate. Do not treat the following as diagnosed.

Leading hypothesis
Mutating src on an iframe that has already committed a document does not reliably renavigate it in every browser, particularly once the embedded document has done any navigating of its own and owns history entries. The standard remedy is to force a fresh element with key={entry.id} on the iframe, which also gives the focus guard and the load handler a clean first-load per entry.

Other candidates worth eliminating before settling on that
- useEmbedPolicy (line 114) and useIframeFocusGuard (line 124) both hold per-entry state and both key off entry?.id. If either returns stale state across the swap the render could be wrong for a different reason.
- handleFrameLoad and the guards frameLoadHandled ref reset on resetKey; confirm the load event for the new page is actually firing at all. If onLoad never fires for entry 2, the frame genuinely did not navigate and the hypothesis above is right. If it DOES fire, the frame navigated and something else is showing stale content.

Reproduce first, in a real browser, and say which of those two it is before changing anything. A one-line key= fix that happens to work is not the same as knowing why.

Affected files
- app/javascript/components/EntryContent.tsx (the iframe at 410)
- app/javascript/hooks/useIframeFocusGuard.ts and useEmbedPolicy.ts (only if implicated)

Acceptance criteria
- With iframe view on, pressing j loads the next entrys page in the frame.
- Works across several consecutive navigations, not just the first.
- Still works after clicking a link inside an embedded page and then navigating, which is the case most likely to break.
- The embed-blocked fallback and the focus guard still behave correctly per entry.
- Regression coverage: the existing e2e/iframe-keyboard-focus.spec.ts is the natural home, and asserting the frame URL after navigation is the assertion that was missing.

Discovered after ttrb-la5r (sticky iframe view) and the rest of epic ttrb-a5qn closed.
close_reason:
Andy reports it no longer reproduces on the current build (2026-08-30). Closing on that, but the mechanism was NEVER IDENTIFIED, and this close should not be read as a diagnosis.

What was ruled out, with evidence:
- The title mechanism does not exist. src is not mutated in place: loadEntry sets isLoadingEntry=true, EntryContent early-returns Loading..., the whole subtree tears down and a fresh <iframe> mounts. A MutationObserver recorded unmount/remount on every navigation in BOTH engines.
- Even the fallback hypothesis is dead: measured outside the app, Chromium renavigates on an in-place src write every time, including re-setting the value the attribute already holds.
- Not reproduced in 14 scenarios across Chromium AND Firefox, including the literal reported flow (open entry, i, j), consecutive and rapid j, a 1.2s slow page, inner-link click then navigate, j-then-k back to the same entry, real cross-origin sites over the real network, and Firefox with fission.autostart and bfcache forced on. Pixels checked by screenshot, not just the frame tree. ~150 entry navigations, frame always renavigated.

Commits that landed between the report and Andy retesting, any of which may be responsible:
- ed52fc2 (ttrb-ngol) Firefox fires no window blur when focus enters a cross-origin frame, so useIframeFocusGuard never noticed the handoff and j was swallowed with no way back. Also fixed Firefox refusing to return focus to an element it holds as the remembered focused element.
- a5a2e47 (ttrb-lix7) a real ~2-in-30 dropped-keypress race affecting every shortcut in the app.
- 9eab561 (ttrb-mq4n work) key={entry.id} on the iframe, plus an E2E page that names the URL it was served for so a stale frame is distinguishable from a fresh one.

The ngol and lix7 fixes both SUPPRESS a keypress rather than advancing the header while the frame lags, so neither accounts for the reported symptom of a header that advanced. That gap is unexplained.

If this recurs: it is a returning bug, not a new one. Start from e2e/iframe-keyboard-focus.spec.ts, which now asserts the framed DOCUMENT rather than the src attribute (the old assertion could not tell a stale frame from a fresh one), and capture the Firefox build ID from about:support, whether it survives a fresh profile with extensions disabled, and whether the stale page was one visited earlier in the same session.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit 9eab561. Diagnosis first, because the ticket's stated mechanism is wrong and the reported symptom is still unexplained. NOT the mechanism. The iframe is never reconciled in place. loadEntry sets isLoadingEntry=true, EntryContent's 'if (isLoading) return
Loading...
' tears the whole subtree down, and a brand-new iframe element mounts with the new src. A MutationObserver recording every iframe mount and load shows the same shape on every navigation, in both engines: no-iframe-in-dom / mount src=.../rust-weekly/0 / load / no-iframe-in-dom / mount src=.../ruby-dispatch/0 / load Every path that changes selectedEntry.id goes through loadEntry, and React 19 resolves a keydown as discrete even from a native listener, so the loading commit is deterministic rather than a race. Nor is the browser hypothesis right. Setting src in place on a cross-origin frame renavigates in Chromium every time, including re-setting the value the attribute already holds after the embedded page navigated itself (measured directly, without the app: /a -> /b -> inner click -> re-set /b pulls it back -> /c). Not reproduced, in 14 scenarios: preference-boot and i-toggle flows; two and three consecutive j presses; a 1.2s slow page; a link clicked inside the frame then Next; inner click then k then j back to the same entry; rapid j j j; real cross-origin sites behind a redirect; real sites written straight into the seeded entries so the src attribute is the real URL with nothing intercepted; Chromium and Firefox; Firefox again with fission.autostart and bfcache forced on; pixels checked by screenshot, not just the frame tree. One caution for whoever picks this up: an early run DID show the frame stuck on the previous site across two steps. That was my own harness - a hash mapping entry URLs onto a site list collided, serving two entries the same page. With an explicit mapping it was clean. It looked exactly like the reported bug. What landed - The embedded test page now names the URL it was served for. Every entry previously got a byte-identical document, so a frame that never renavigated was indistinguishable from one that did, and the src attribute was the only thing left to assert - and React sets that from entry.link either way. This is the assertion the ticket said was missing. - Two examples compare the rendered document against the attribute: 'each j puts the next entry's page in the frame, not just in its src' (two consecutive steps) and 'coming back to an entry reloads its page, not the one the frame wandered to' (inner link, Previous, Next). - Teeth verified by mutation: with the frame frozen on the first entry's document while the attribute tracks the entry, both new examples fail and the pre-existing 'j keeps advancing once the framed page has loaded' still passes. That asymmetry is the gap that was open. - key={entry.id} on the iframe. It changes nothing today and the comment says so; it removes the dependency on the loading flash, which is ttrb-li2x. Fold li2x into this if you agree that covers it. - A firefox project scoped to the three browse-mode specs. Found on the way: ttrb-ngol, a real Firefox-only defect. Firefox fires no window blur when focus moves into a cross-origin frame, so useIframeFocusGuard never sees the handoff, 'Restore shortcuts' never appears, and j is swallowed with no way back. Chromium logs 'window blur: activeElement=IFRAME' on the same click; Firefox logs no event at all while still setting document.activeElement to the iframe. Four examples fixme'd under Firefox against it. That is the serious browse-mode bug in this area, and it is not this one. Verification: rails 519 runs / 1527 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors; vitest 793 passed / 45 files; playwright 256 passed / 9 skipped across both projects (chromium 243+5, firefox 13+4); rubocop 194 files no offenses; tsc clean. iframe spec at --repeat-each=6: chromium 42/42, firefox 18 passed / 24 skipped. Leaving this open. I cannot close a P1 I could not reproduce, and the symptom Andy describes - header advancing while the frame keeps the previous article's rendered page - is not accounted for by anything above.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Correction from ttrb-ngol, not a reproduction. That ticket's notes recorded that with focus in the frame under Firefox a keypress 'reaches neither document'. It does reach the framed document: instrumenting the embedded page's own keydown listener shows page.keyboard.press('j') logged inside the frame in both engines, with the parent's keydown log empty. What differs is only which element inside the frame Playwright's click leaves focused (the input under Chromium, the body under Firefox), so Chromium types a character and Firefox does not. Nothing found that explains a header advancing while the frame holds the previous article's rendered page. Across roughly 150 entry navigations in both engines while fixing ngol, the frame always renavigated and expectFrameShowsItsSrc always held. The two ngol defects (no handoff event in Firefox, and anchor.focus() being a no-op while the anchor is the remembered focused element) both leave focus in the frame, which suppresses j entirely rather than advancing the header, so neither is the mq4n mechanism.

title: useKeyboardCommands swaps its keydown listener in a passive effect, so the first keypress after a render is handled by the previous render's closure and dropped
close_reason: Stable keydown listener reading commands from a commit-phase ref (a5a2e47); e2e retry removed, 140/140 at --repeat-each=10 in chromium and firefox against 4/70 failures on the old code

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit a5a2e47. Registered the keydown listener once in a useLayoutEffect with [] deps; the handler closes over nothing and reads commands/enabled from a ref synced in a useLayoutEffect.

Why layout effects and not the render-phase ref write the description suggested: layout effects run inside the commit phase, in the same uninterrupted synchronous block that mutates the DOM and strictly before the browser may paint it. So the invariant is 'if the screen shows render N, the ref holds render N', with no window at all rather than a smaller one. A render-phase write also closes the window but leaves the ref describing state from a render React may abandon (discarded transition, offscreen prerender). Note the description's warning that 'updating the ref in an effect would reintroduce the same post-paint window' is true of useEffect only, not useLayoutEffect.

This is a class fix, not a narrowed window: the listener identity never changes for the component's lifetime, so there is no stale-closure listener for a press to land on at any timing.

Behaviour change worth knowing: enabled:false now leaves the listener attached and returns from it immediately, instead of detaching. Nothing observable hung on its presence, and not touching registration is what keeps the identity stable.

Tests (app/javascript/hooks/useKeyboardCommands.test.tsx, renamed from .ts for JSX): exactly one addEventListener and zero removeEventListener across five re-renders with fresh command arrays; the function object captured at mount dispatching to the newest handlers; and a keydown fired from a parent layout effect, which by React's bottom-up layout order runs after the subtree committed and before any passive effect anywhere. All three fail against the old implementation.

Removed the openFirstEntry retry in e2e/iframe-keyboard-focus.spec.ts. Control run to show the retry-less spec can actually see the bug: old hook, chromium, --repeat-each=10 gave 4 failures in 70 (5.7%, matching the ~2 in 30 reported here). New hook, --repeat-each=10 across chromium and firefox: 140/140.

Filed ttrb-fuky for FeedOrganizer, ScoreButtons and SidebarDrawer, which have the same listener shape.

title: GET /api/v1/preferences omits entries_sort_config, tts_playback_speed and the digest_* keys, and PATCH silently drops them
description:
Found while fixing ttrb-8zv5.

app/javascript/contexts/PreferencesContext.tsx declares defaults for entries_sort_config, tts_playback_speed, digest_enable, digest_preferred_time, digest_catchup and digest_min_score. app/controllers/api/v1/preferences_controller.rb lists none of them in either default_preferences or allowed_preference_keys.

Two consequences.

1. Writes are silently dropped. application.tsx:756 calls updatePreference("entries_sort_config", sortString) and AudioPlayerContext.tsx:475 calls updatePreference("tts_playback_speed", ...). params.permit filters both out, the controller saves nothing and returns 200 with the unchanged set, so the reader keeps the optimistic value for the session and loses it on reload. A user reordering the entry list or changing TTS speed does not get that back next visit. PreferencesPanel.tsx writes the digest_* keys the same way; SendDigestsJob reads digest_preferred_time straight out of user_preferences, so that feature is reading a row nothing can write through this endpoint.

2. Reads flip on boot. The client default is a string, the API response has no key, so the value goes from e.g. "date:desc" to undefined the moment preferences land. That was rebuilding the reader's entriesQuery for a query that had not changed and reloading the list, which clears the selection - see ttrb-8zv5, where it closed an article opened in the first moments after boot. Worked around there by depending on the resolved sort string instead of the raw preference; the underlying contract mismatch is still here.

Careful with the obvious fix: adding "entries_sort_config" => "date:desc" to default_preferences is NOT safe on its own. application.tsx:252 and :603 both read entries_sort_config first and fall back to the legacy entries_sort_by_score only when it is blank. A server-supplied default would always win and would silently ignore entries_sort_by_score = "true" for users who still have it stored. Any fix has to keep that fallback reachable - e.g. add the key to allowed_preference_keys so it can be written, and leave it absent from default_preferences until the legacy preference is migrated out.

Acceptance: PATCH /api/v1/preferences persists each of these keys and GET returns them; a controller test covers the round trip; users with entries_sort_by_score = "true" and no entries_sort_config still get score sorting.
close_reason: PATCH/GET now round-trip entries_sort_config, tts_playback_speed and the four digest_* keys. entries_sort_config is writable but has no server default, preserving the legacy entries_sort_by_score fallback without a migration. Covered by 14 new controller tests in 4f2e890.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 4f2e890. Added the six missing keys to allowed_preference_keys; gave five of them server defaults (tts_playback_speed 1, digest_enable false, digest_preferred_time 08:00, digest_catchup false, digest_min_score 0) and deliberately left entries_sort_config without one so the legacy entries_sort_by_score fallback at application.tsx:242/:617 stays reachable. No migration: existing entries_sort_by_score users are untouched and keep score sorting until they pick a sort. Client side, dropped the matching "date:desc" claim from PreferencesContext defaults and marked the field optional in the api.ts Preferences interface, so pre-load and post-load agree; the ttrb-8zv5 fix (query depends on the resolved sort string) is unchanged and still correct. New test/controllers/api/v1/preferences_controller_test.rb, 14 tests, 10 of which failed before the change; they assert re-GET rather than the PATCH status, plus two drift guards. Filed ttrb-nhp6 (digest_enable is stored but SendDigestsJob still gates on users.email_digest, which nothing writes) and ttrb-qmwo (language picker only writes localStorage).

title: Browse-mode iframe correctness depends on the Loading flash unmounting the frame, an accident nothing tests or documents
description:
Discovered while investigating ttrb-mq4n, and true whether or not that bug reproduces. Walking j/k in iframe view currently shows the correct page for each entry, but not for the reason anyone designed. Proven with a MutationObserver recording every iframe element mount and every load event during Playwright runs against bin/e2e-server: no-iframe-in-dom mount src=https://e2e.invalid/rust-weekly/0 load attr=https://e2e.invalid/rust-weekly/0 no-iframe-in-dom mount src=https://e2e.invalid/ruby-dispatch/0 load attr=https://e2e.invalid/ruby-dispatch/0 The frame is fully unmounted and remounted on every entry change. The mechanism is incidental: application.tsx loadEntry() sets isLoadingEntry = true, and EntryContent has an early `if (isLoading) return
Loading...
` that tears down the entire iframe subtree. A brand-new
close_reason:
Folded into ttrb-mq4n commit 9eab561, which did all three wanted items.

1. key={entry.id} on the iframe at EntryContent.tsx, with a comment stating it is a no-op today and exists to remove the dependency on the Loading flash.
2. The dependency is now named in code rather than being an undocumented accident.
3. A test with teeth: the embedded E2E page now names the URL it was served for, so a stale frame is distinguishable from a fresh one. Previously every entry got a byte-identical document and the only thing left to assert was the src attribute, which React sets from entry.link whether or not the frame navigated. Two new examples compare the RENDERED DOCUMENT against the attribute.

Teeth verified by mutation rather than asserted: against a frame frozen on the first entry document while the attribute tracks the entry, both new examples fail while the pre-existing "j keeps advancing" example still passes. That asymmetry is exactly the gap this ticket was about.

Suite after: e2e 256 passed / 9 skipped (chromium 243+5, firefox 13+4), Ruby 519 runs / 0 failures, vitest 793, rubocop 194 clean.

title: useIframeFocusGuard detects the keyboard handoff only in Chromium: Firefox fires no window blur, so Restore shortcuts never appears and j/k die silently
description:
Reported behaviour
Browse mode's escape hatch does not exist in Firefox. Once an embedded page takes keyboard focus, no 'Restore shortcuts' button appears and j/k stop working with nothing on screen to say why or offer a way back.

Mechanism, measured rather than assumed
useIframeFocusGuard detects the handoff by watching for the parent window to blur while document.activeElement is the iframe (hooks/useIframeFocusGuard.ts:75-100). The same click into a cross-origin frame, instrumented identically in both browsers:

  Chromium: 'window blur: activeElement=IFRAME hasFocus=true'  -> button appears, j lands in the embedded field
  Firefox:  no event at all - no blur, no focusin              -> no button, j is swallowed entirely

Firefox does set document.activeElement to the IFRAME element (confirmed by reading it directly after the click), it simply never fires an event to say so: the parent window is still focused, so it does not blur, and focusin does not fire for focus crossing into a subframe. The guard's syncHandoff is therefore never called, keyboardHandedOff stays false, and the fallback the whole feature depends on is unreachable.

Follow-on measurement: with focus in the frame under Firefox, pressing j twice left the selected entry, the src attribute and the frame document all unchanged. The keypress reaches neither document in the Playwright harness. Either way the reader is stuck with no affordance.

This is ttrb-gmhv's fix being Chromium-specific, not a regression from it.

Evidence
- Four examples in e2e/iframe-keyboard-focus.spec.ts fail under Firefox and pass under Chromium: 'clicking into the frame hands the keys over and says so', 'the header still advances by mouse while the frame holds the keys', 'restoring shortcuts brings j back', 'focus mode can be left by mouse after the frame takes the keys'. They are marked test.fixme for Firefox and reference this issue.
- The other three examples in that file, including the two ttrb-mq4n added, pass in both browsers.

Likely fix
No event exists to hang this on in Firefox, so an event-only design cannot work. Poll document.activeElement while the frame is up (a short interval, only while showIframe is on and the frame is mounted), or combine the existing blur listener with a poll so Chromium keeps its immediate response and Firefox gets a slightly delayed but correct one. Measure the polling cost before settling on an interval, and keep the existing blur path rather than replacing it.

Acceptance criteria
- Clicking into an embedded page shows 'Restore shortcuts' in Firefox as it does in Chromium.
- Clicking it returns focus to the reader and j/k work again, in both browsers.
- The four fixme markers in e2e/iframe-keyboard-focus.spec.ts are removed and the examples pass under both projects.
- Whatever polling is added stops when no frame is on screen.

Found while diagnosing ttrb-mq4n; not the bug that ticket describes.
close_reason: Handoff detection is now a 100ms poll of document.activeElement, the one signal both engines produce; event listeners kept for latency only. Also fixed reclaimKeyboard, which Firefox ignored when the anchor was already the document's remembered focused element: it releases the frame first now. Four Firefox fixmes removed, 24/24 per engine at --repeat-each=6. Commit ed52fc2.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit ed52fc2. Detection is now a 100ms poll of document.activeElement, the one signal both engines produce (measured: Firefox fires no blur/focusout/focusin/iframe-focus on the way in, and hasFocus/visibilityState do not separate the states in either engine). Event listeners kept for latency only. Second defect found and fixed in the same hook: with focus in the frame and the anchor still the document's remembered focused element, Firefox treats anchor.focus() as a no-op, so reclaimKeyboard now releases the frame first. That was stuck on 3 of 20 first loads before, 0 of 30 after. Four fixmes removed, 24/24 per engine at --repeat-each=6.

title: Playwright suite runs Chromium only for everything except the browse-mode specs
description:
playwright.config.ts now declares two projects: chromium runs everything, firefox runs only the three browse-mode specs (iframe-keyboard-focus, embed-block-fallback, focus-mode-nav).

That scope was deliberate rather than complete. Browse mode is the one feature whose correctness is browser behaviour rather than application logic - cross-origin framing, focus crossing a document boundary, what a frame does when its src changes - and Chromium and Firefox genuinely disagree there, so it is the part that earns a second browser first. The rest of the suite has never been run under Firefox and its state is unknown.

Work
- Run the full suite under Firefox and see what falls out.
- Fix or triage each failure. Expect a mix of real cross-browser bugs and selector or timing assumptions that only hold in Chromium.
- Widen the firefox project's testMatch, or drop it entirely so the project runs everything.

Worth doing before widening: ttrb-ngol, since the known Firefox defect it covers will account for some of the failures in any spec that touches the embedded-page keyboard handoff.

Not urgent. Filed so the narrow scope is a recorded decision rather than an oversight.

title: Subscribe bookmarklet button is dead: React 19 replaces the javascript: href with a throwing stub
description:
Reported by Andy: dragging the "Subscribe to NibbleRSS" button to the bookmarks bar produces a bookmark whose URL is

  javascript:throw new Error(*React has blocked a javascript: URL as a security precaution.*)

Confirmed, not inferred. React 19.2.8 (package.json:41 declares ^19.2.3) sanitizes href at render. The substitution is visible in the shipped bundle at app/assets/builds/application.js:3817:

  isJavaScriptProtocol.test("" + url)
    ? "javascript:throw new Error(*React has blocked a javascript: URL as a security precaution.*)"
    : url

So app/javascript/components/ToolsPanel.tsx:73 passing href={minifiedBookmarklet} can never work on this React. The drag-to-bookmarks-bar path, which is the primary affordance and the one the card text tells you to use, is dead. It is not degraded, it produces a bookmark that throws when clicked.

What still works: the copy-to-clipboard path at ToolsPanel.tsx:88-96. That is an <Input value={minifiedBookmarklet}> plus navigator.clipboard.writeText, neither of which goes through href sanitization. Anyone who copied the code rather than dragging the button has a working bookmarklet, which is probably why this survived.

Fix: React only sanitizes hrefs it sets through props, so set the attribute imperatively after mount:

  <a ref={(el) => el?.setAttribute("href", minifiedBookmarklet)} ...>

That keeps the element draggable and keeps the real code in the bookmark. Confirm in a real browser that the resulting bookmark URL is the bookmarklet and not the stub — a unit test asserting the ref ran is not the same check, since the whole bug is what the DOM attribute ends up holding.

Consider also whether the anchor should stop being an anchor. onClick already calls preventDefault, so it is a drag source and nothing else; the accessibility story of a link that refuses to navigate is poor either way.

Acceptance criteria:
- Dragging the button to the bookmarks bar yields a bookmark whose URL starts with javascript:(function(){ and contains no "React has blocked".
- Clicking that bookmark on a page with a feed link opens <origin>?subscribe=<encoded feed url>.
- The copy path keeps working unchanged.
- A test that fails if the href reverts to the sanitized stub. Assert on the rendered DOM attribute, not on the prop.

Two adjacent problems found while reading the file, NOT part of this ticket and not yet filed:
1. baseUrl is window.location.origin captured at render (ToolsPanel.tsx:12), so a bookmarklet grabbed from localhost:3000 permanently targets localhost.
2. Multiple-feed selection uses window.prompt (line 30), which is blocked in some contexts and poor everywhere. Since ?subscribe= already exists, the bookmarklet could hand all candidates to Nibbler and let it render the choice.
Ask Andy before doing either; he has seen both and has not asked for them.
close_reason: Bookmarklet href set imperatively via ref callback + setAttribute so React 19 cannot substitute its throwing stub. Verified in real Chromium: dragged href is javascript:(function(){..., clicking it opens <origin>?subscribe=<encoded feed url>. New ToolsPanel.test.tsx asserts on the DOM attribute and fails against the old code. Commit ad7b46b.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit ad7b46b: anchor href set via ref callback + setAttribute instead of the href prop. Test asserts on the rendered DOM attribute and was confirmed failing (6 of 7) against the pre-fix component, where the attribute held javascript:throw new Error('React has blocked...') while the Input held the real code. Real-Chromium harness against a built bundle: attribute is javascript:(function(){..., no React stub, and clicking a bookmark made from it on a page with an RSS link opened <origin>?subscribe=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Ffeed.xml. Copy path untouched and covered. vitest 802/46, typecheck clean, build clean.

title: Entry#update_tsvector always assigns nil, so full-text search never matches any entry
description:
app/models/entry.rb:47 builds the tsvector with:

  SELECT to_tsvector('english', ?) || to_tsvector('english', ?)

then reads the result as .first["to_tsvector"]. PostgreSQL names the result
column of a || expression '?column?', not 'to_tsvector', so the lookup returns
nil and the before_save assigns nil to tsvector_combined on every save.

Verified empirically (RAILS_ENV=test rails runner):
  row={"?column?" => "'bodi':3 'headlin':1 'probe':2 'text':4"}
  keys=["?column?"]
  row['to_tsvector']=nil

Consequence: entries created through FeedUpdater have tsvector_combined NULL,
so Entry.search (which matches tsvector_combined @@ plainto_tsquery) returns
nothing for them. There is no database trigger and the column is not GENERATED
(pg_trigger empty, attgenerated = ''), so the Rails callback is the only writer.
Confirmed the same for entries WITH a body, so this is independent of the blank
content change in ttrb-rz4v.

Fix options:
1. Read the right key: alias the expression, SELECT ... AS tsvector_combined.
2. Better: make tsvector_combined a GENERATED ALWAYS column, or a DB trigger, so
   it cannot drift from title/content and does not cost a round trip per save.
   Needs a migration.

A backfill is needed for existing rows either way.

Discovered while working ttrb-rz4v (per-entry isolation in FeedUpdater). Not
caused by it; left alone there to keep that change scoped.
close_reason: tsvector_combined is now a GENERATED ALWAYS ... STORED column computed by PostgreSQL from title and content; the before_save that assigned nil is gone. The migration's table rewrite backfills every existing row (7.7s at 8271 rows, other columns byte-identical). Tests go through a real save and a real Entry.search and fail 8/16 at the model, 4/6 over HTTP against the previous code. rake search:status reports index coverage. Commit 367159e.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit 367159e. Chose the GENERATED ALWAYS ... STORED column over fixing the string key, because the callback could silently skip and a generated column cannot. Backfill is the migration's table rewrite: 7.7s at 8271 rows / 8.6KB bodies, md5 over all 16 other columns byte-identical before and after. Verified the fix empirically: 0 -> 8271 indexed, GIN Bitmap Index Scan in the plan, HTML attribute noise (href, tracker host) absent from the index. Deploy order safe both ways (Rails' attributes_for_create/attributes_for_update filter virtual columns, so the old callback's assignment is dropped rather than raising). Tests fail 8/16 at the model and 4/6 over HTTP against the previous code.

title: Let search results be re-sorted, and un-hide the sort controls during a search
description:
Discovered during ttrb-soaj.

ttrb-soaj changed the search endpoint to return ts_rank relevance DESC, with date_entered DESC and user_entries.id DESC as tiebreaks. That is a deliberate order now rather than the accidental date order the endpoint used to return, but the client still cannot influence it, so EntryList.tsx:381 keeps hiding the sort controls while searchActive is true (the guard added by ttrb-qv7i, commit 12b1752).

To bring them back, SearchController#index needs to accept a sort selection the way EntriesController#apply_sorting does, with relevance as an additional sortable column that only search offers. Then EntryList can drop the !searchActive guard on the sort controls and pass the selection through useEntrySearch to api.search.

Acceptance criteria
- SearchController accepts a sort param; relevance is the default, date is selectable.
- Ordering is still deterministic: whatever the primary sort, user_entries.id remains the final tiebreak so paging cannot repeat or drop a row.
- EntryList shows the sort controls during a search, with relevance as a column the entry list itself does not offer.
- A controller test asserts each ordering with entries seeded so the orderings disagree.

title: Entry search runs sanitize_sql_like on plainto_tsquery input, mangling queries with _ or %
description:
Discovered during ttrb-soaj; carried forward unchanged rather than fixed, to keep that ticket's diff to the ordering defect.

app/models/entry.rb#tsquery_sql:

  plainto_tsquery('english', #{connection.quote(sanitize_sql_like(query.to_s))})

sanitize_sql_like escapes the LIKE metacharacters _ and % with a backslash. Nothing here is a LIKE pattern. The value goes to plainto_tsquery as ordinary text, so a query for web_dev is handed to the parser as web\_dev and a query containing % gains a backslash it never had. Injection safety comes from connection.quote, not from this call, so removing it costs nothing.

The same expression predates the ticket; ttrb-soaj only moved it into a private class method.

Acceptance criteria
- sanitize_sql_like is gone from the tsquery path; connection.quote stays.
- A model test searches for a term containing an underscore and finds the entry containing it.
close_reason:
Duplicate of ttrb-20gl, which covers exactly this (sanitize_sql_like applied to input that is not a LIKE pattern, before plainto_tsquery) and already carries the measurement.

Merging rather than keeping both: ttrb-voe4 measured plainto_tsquery('english', X) with and without the sanitizer for foo_bar, 50%, C_plus and back\\slash. The resulting tsquery is IDENTICAL in every case ('foo' & 'bar', '50', 'c' & 'plus', 'back' & 'slash'), because the tsquery parser already treats _, % and \\ as separators. So the observation here is right — web_dev does arrive as web\\_dev — but it changes no result. Consistent with, not contradicting, this report.

ttrb-20gl was downgraded to P4 on that evidence and is the single place to track the remaining cosmetic issue: the call misleads the next reader into thinking LIKE escaping is required here. Injection safety comes from connection.quote, as noted in both tickets.

title: Route EntriesController#headlines through EntryScoping instead of its own copy of the filter block
description:
Discovered during ttrb-aawe. ttrb-aawe extracted the entry-list scoping params (unread/starred/published/feed_id/category_id/tag/view + fresh window) into app/controllers/concerns/entry_scoping.rb and routed EntriesController#index and SearchController#index through it. #headlines still carries a hand-rolled copy of the same block (app/controllers/api/v1/entries_controller.rb), so it is now the one remaining site that can drift.

It was left alone deliberately: #headlines builds its relation with an explicit select() column list and a count("user_entries.id"), its category branch omits the joins(:feed) that #index needs because feeds is already joined, and it writes the filters as raw where() rather than model scopes. Converting it is behaviour-preserving on paper but wants its own test pass, which was out of scope for ttrb-aawe.

Acceptance: #headlines calls apply_entry_scoping, the select list and count("user_entries.id") still work, and the existing headlines controller tests pass unchanged.

title: E2E coverage for article search: / opens the box, scope pills narrow and widen, results replace the list
description:
The whole search feature (ttrb-tydj: api.search, useEntrySearch, SearchBar, SearchScopeControls, SearchResultList, the / binding) landed with vitest coverage only. e2e/ has no search spec, so nothing exercises the box against a real Rails server and a real PostgreSQL full-text index.

Worth covering:
- / focuses the box from the list, and a typed query replaces the entry list with hits.
- A search launched from inside a feed returns only that feed's matches; pressing the place pill (or Alt+A) brings in matches from other feeds.
- A read article matching the query is absent from an unread-scoped search and present once the history pill (or Alt+H) is pressed.
- From Fresh, the search honours the toolbar's time and per-feed selectors.
- Escape clears the box and puts the scope back; the entry list returns.

Discovered during ttrb-prmg.

title: Three more keydown listeners are swapped in passive effects and can drop a press: FeedOrganizer, ScoreButtons, SidebarDrawer
description:
Same class as ttrb-lix7, found while fixing it. Each builds a keydown handler that closes over state and swaps it into the document from a useEffect, so between the paint of render N and the flush of render N's effects the live listener is still N-1's closure and a press in that window runs against stale state.

- app/javascript/components/FeedOrganizer.tsx:312, deps [selectedId, editingId, sortableIds, showQuickMove]
- app/javascript/components/ScoreButtons.tsx:58-63, deps [keyboardEnabled, handleKeyDown]
- app/javascript/components/mobile/SidebarDrawer.tsx:31-34, deps [handleKeyDown] over [isOpen, layout]

Lower priority than ttrb-lix7 was: none of these guards a list that populates asynchronously the way handleKeyboardNext does, so the stale closure usually differs from the fresh one only in ways the user cannot see. FeedOrganizer is the likeliest to bite, since sortableIds changes as feeds load and arrow navigation reads it.

Fix is the shape landed in a5a2e47: register once in a useLayoutEffect with [] deps and read the state out of a ref synced in a useLayoutEffect. app/javascript/hooks/useKeyboardCommands.ts carries the reasoning.

Checked and already correct: CommandPalette.useCommandPalette and MoveFeedDialog.useMoveFeedDialog both register once with [] and use functional setState.
close_reason: FeedOrganizer and ScoreButtons moved to the ttrb-lix7 listener shape (dae12e2), with five lifecycle tests confirmed failing against the pre-fix code. SidebarDrawer judged unreachable and left alone; reasoning in the comment. Filed ttrb-qlpd for its conditional-hook violation.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
Commit dae12e2: FeedOrganizer and ScoreButtons converted to the ttrb-lix7 shape - one listener registered at mount whose identity never changes, handler reading the current render out of a ref, both effects useLayoutEffect. Five new vitest tests, all confirmed failing against the pre-fix code by stashing only the two component files.

SidebarDrawer deliberately left alone. Its handler reads only isOpen; the drawer's sole opener is a tap on the mobile header button (application.tsx:1185 onShowSidebar={layout.goToSidebar}), there is no keyboard path to open it, and it renders only under 640px. Entering the window means pressing Escape on a hardware keyboard within a frame of a tap that starts a 200ms open transition. The other direction (stale isOpen=true just after close) makes the handler call goToList() when already on list, which only pushes a redundant paneHistory entry. Not worth the churn, and adding two more hooks there would deepen ttrb-qlpd.

Correction to this ticket's premise: ScoreButtons does sit behind an async populate. onScoreChange in application.tsx:1250 is (score) => selectedEntry && handleSetScore(selectedEntry.id, score), a fresh arrow over the current selection, and loadEntry (application.tsx:349) awaits the network before setSelectedEntry, so the next entry's score paints when the response lands. EntryContent has no key, so ScoreButtons stays mounted across that change. A digit pressed in the window ran the previous render's closure - previous score for the score===0 guard, previous onScoreChange for the target - and scored the entry the reader had just left. That is a wrong write, not a dropped press, which makes it the more serious of the three rather than the least.

Filed ttrb-qlpd for the conditional-hook violation in SidebarDrawer found while judging it. Also noted there: the project has no eslint config at all, so react-hooks lint rules are not enforced.

Baselines held: bin/rails test 593 runs / 1835 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors / 0 skips; npm run test:run 900 passed / 51 files (was 895, +5 new); npm run test:e2e 274 passed / 5 skipped; bundle exec rubocop 202 files / no offenses.

title: Send daily digest toggle writes digest_enable, but SendDigestsJob gates on users.email_digest, which no endpoint sets
description:
Found while fixing ttrb-bbjz.

PreferencesPanel.tsx:488 toggles the digest_enable user preference. As of 4f2e890 that value now persists, but nothing on the server reads it: grep for digest_enable across app/ lib/ finds only the client. SendDigestsJob:31 selects users with `.where(email_digest: true)` -- the boolean column on users (db/schema.rb:364, default false) -- and no controller in app/controllers/api/v1/ permits or assigns email_digest.

So a user turning 'Send daily digest' on in the settings panel still receives nothing, and a user turning it off still receives digests if email_digest happens to be true. The toggle and the gate are two unconnected pieces of state.

Pick one. Either the job reads the digest_enable preference (consistent with digest_preferred_time, digest_catchup and digest_min_score, which are all preferences), or the preferences controller writes users.email_digest when digest_enable changes and GET reports the column rather than a preference row. The first is the smaller change and matches the other three digest keys.

Whichever way, existing users with email_digest = true and no digest_enable row must keep receiving digests -- the API default for digest_enable is currently 'false'.

Acceptance: enabling the toggle causes SendDigestsJob to select the user; disabling it stops selection; a job test covers both; users already opted in via email_digest are not silently unsubscribed.
close_reason: SendDigestsJob now gates on the digest_enable preference instead of the unwritten users.email_digest column, so the 'Send daily digest' switch works in both directions. Idempotent backfill migration keeps existing opted-in users subscribed. Six new tests, two of them driving the switch through the API and then running the job. 593 runs / 1835 assertions / 0 failures.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit fe24937: SendDigestsJob selects on the digest_enable preference; migration 20260830023650 backfills email_digest=true users into it (idempotent, no writes to users). Follow-up ttrb-iosi files the column drop for a later deploy.

title: Language picker never stores user_language, so the settings dropdown reverts to Browser default
description:
Found while fixing ttrb-bbjz. Same shape as ttrb-g18k (theme), different key.

user_language is permitted and defaulted by PreferencesController, and PreferencesPanel.tsx:194 renders the Select from `preferences.user_language || "auto"`. But choosing an actual language calls I18nContext#setLanguage (PreferencesPanel.tsx:199), which only does `localStorage.setItem("nibbler-language", language)` (I18nContext.tsx:40). updatePreference("user_language", ...) is called in exactly one branch: the 'Browser default' one, which writes "".

Consequences: the server row stays "" forever, the dropdown shows 'Browser default' again the next time the panel opens even though the UI is in Spanish, and the choice does not follow the user to another browser or device. It also means a server-side default of "" is the only value that key will ever hold.

Fix: have setLanguage (or its caller) write the preference as well as localStorage, and seed i18n from preferences.user_language once preferences load, keeping localStorage as the pre-load hint so the first paint is not in the wrong language.

Acceptance: picking a language stores it in user_preferences; reopening the panel shows that language selected; a fresh browser with the same account starts in that language.
close_reason: Language picker writes user_language on both branches; server preference is the source of truth with localStorage as a first-paint cache, adopted once for readers who only have the cache. Commit e15eaad.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text: Commit e15eaad: both branches of the picker now write user_language and set the language; PreferencesContext applies the server value on load and adopts a cache-only language once. No migration -- there is no server-side language column, the only prior copy is each reader's localStorage. Catching test app/javascript/components/PreferencesPanel.language.test.tsx drives the real Select against real i18next and asserts rendered output; 4/4 fail against the previous code. E2E 'the chosen language survives a reload on an empty cache' fails at the pick, before the reload.

title: Drop the now-unread users.email_digest column in a follow-up deploy
description:
SendDigestsJob no longer reads users.email_digest as of ttrb-nhp6; the digest_enable preference is the only source of truth, and migration 20260830023650 backfilled the column's opted-in users into it.

The column is left in place deliberately: the switch-away and the cleanup must not ship in the same deploy, so that a rollback of the job code still has the column to select on.

Once the digest_enable change has been running in production long enough to trust, remove the column (and the two references left in test/fixtures-adjacent setup, if any remain). Check first that no user has email_digest = true without a matching digest_enable = 'true' preference row -- if any do, the backfill did not run and dropping the column loses their opt-in.

title: Shift+J / Shift+K do not change category: the handlers jump within the loaded entry list instead, and silently no-op in most views
description:
Reported by Andy: "shift-j shift-k are not working to change categories".

The keybinding is fine. The handlers do something other than what the shortcut is named.

Binding is correct
keyboardShortcuts.ts:95 and :102 bind { key: "J", modifiers: { shift: true } } and { key: "K", modifiers: { shift: true } }. useKeyboardCommands matches on event.key === command.key plus an exact modifier comparison, and event.key for Shift+j is "J", so the match succeeds and there is no collision with the plain j and k bindings, which carry no shift and are compared strictly. The handlers ARE being called.

What the handlers actually do
application.tsx:681 handleKeyboardNextCategory scans the CURRENTLY LOADED entries array for the next entry whose feed has a different category_id, then opens that entry. handleKeyboardPreviousCategory at :696 does the mirror. Neither touches the sidebar selection, selectedCategoryId, or the loaded list. Nothing changes category in the navigation sense.

Why it appears dead
1. In any view already scoped to one category (a single feed, a category, or a tag whose entries share a category) every entry has the same category_id, the loop finds nothing, and the handler falls out of the bottom. The code even says so: "No different category found - stay at current position". No toast, no flash, no feedback of any kind, which is why it reads as the key not working rather than as a no-op.
2. getCategoryForEntry returns feed?.category_id ?? null by looking the entry up in `feeds`. If feeds has not loaded, or an entry references a feed missing from that array, every entry resolves to null, every comparison is equal, and the handler no-ops for a second reason.
3. In All Feeds the list is date-sorted with categories interleaved, so "next entry with a different category" is usually just the next entry. The action is real but indistinguishable from j.

The help dialog reinforces the wrong expectation: the description is "Next category" / "Previous category", which reads as moving the sidebar selection, not as jumping within a list.

Expected behavior, and the decision to make
Andys words were "change categories", which points at moving the navigation selection: Shift+J selects the next category in the sidebar and loads its entries, Shift+K the previous. That is the reading to build unless Andy says otherwise. The alternative, keeping the jump-within-list behaviour but fixing the silence and the label, is a smaller change but does not match what he asked for.

If the sidebar-selection reading is taken, decide:
- Order. Categories are a tree (Category#self_and_descendant_ids is used for filtering); next means next in the sidebars rendered order, including nesting, not next by id.
- Whether it walks only expanded categories or all of them.
- Whether it wraps at the ends, and what happens from a virtual folder (All, Fresh, Starred) where no category is selected.
- Whether the boundary flash used elsewhere (animate-boundary-flash) is the right feedback when there is nowhere to go.

Affected files
- app/javascript/application.tsx (handleKeyboardNextCategory :681, handleKeyboardPreviousCategory :696, getCategoryForEntry)
- app/javascript/lib/keyboardShortcuts.ts (descriptions at :97 and :104)
- app/javascript/components/FeedSidebar.tsx (if selection moves, the sidebar needs to scroll the newly selected category into view)

Acceptance criteria
- Shift+J and Shift+K do what the help dialog says they do.
- From a single-feed or single-category view the keys have a visible effect, or a visible reason why they cannot.
- No silent no-op path remains.
- Behaviour is defined and tested for the ends of the list and for a virtual folder with no category selected.
- Vitest coverage for the handler, since neither handler has any today.

title: text-destructive is unreadable on the stock Dark palette (1.98:1) and under AA on Light (3.76:1)
description:
Found by the theme colour audit (ttrb-x7fn), measured in Chromium with canvas-resolved sRGB and the WCAG formula.

--color-destructive is painted as a foreground in 29 places (text-destructive: error strings in LoginPage, StoriesPanel, SearchResultList, AccountPanel, OpmlPanel, SubscribeFeedDialog, FollowStoryDialog, AudioPanel, EditFeedDialog, plus AlertCircle icons in QueuePanel, EntryList and FeedOrganizer). Contrast against --color-background:

  Light          3.76:1   FAIL (needs 4.5 for normal text)
  Dark           1.98:1   FAIL, effectively unreadable
  Gruvbox Dark   4.59:1   pass
  Gruvbox Light  7.48:1   pass
  Sepia          6.36:1   pass

The two failures are the two palettes inherited from shadcn, where --destructive is designed as a *fill* (bg-destructive with destructive-foreground on top) and was never intended as a text colour. Dark's hsl(0 62.8% 30.6%) = rgb(127,29,29) is a dark red for a button, which is why white-on-it measures a healthy 10.02:1 while the same colour as text on the near-black page measures 1.98.

The three hand-authored palettes already solved this. Gruvbox Dark's block carries the comment 'Lighter than gruvbox's neutral red so text-destructive clears AA (4.6:1)' and pairs it with a dark --color-destructive-foreground. Applying the same treatment to Light and Dark is the obvious fix and is why this is filed rather than done: it flips the destructive Button from dark-red-with-white-text to light-red-with-dark-text on the stock palettes, which is a visible change to a control that appears in delete confirmations throughout the app. That is a design call, not a token nudge.

Alternatives worth weighing:
- Add a separate --color-destructive-text token for the 29 foreground call sites and leave --color-destructive as the fill. Keeps every button identical; costs a token and 29 edits.
- Accept the Button change and match Gruvbox Dark. Smallest diff, no new token.

Also in scope: components/ui/badge.tsx's destructive variant. Its text-white was changed to text-destructive-foreground in ttrb-x7fn (it measured 3.19:1 on Gruvbox Dark's light red), but on Light the pairing is still ~3.76:1 because destructive-foreground is near-white there. The variant is currently unused, so nothing renders it today.

Guard: e2e/settings.spec.ts asserts 4.5:1 for foreground, muted-foreground, success and warning across all five palettes. --color-destructive is deliberately excluded there, with a comment pointing here. Add it to CONTRAST_PAIRS as part of closing this.

comments.author: Andy Nutter-Upham
comments.text:
DECISION (Andy, 2026-08-30): take the separate-token option. Add --color-destructive-text for the 30 foreground call sites and leave --color-destructive as the fill, so every destructive Button keeps exactly its current appearance on all five palettes.

Implementation notes for whoever picks this up:
- The new token needs a value in all five palette blocks, not just the two failing ones. The three hand-authored palettes already clear AA as text, so their destructive-text can equal their existing destructive; Light and Dark need lighter values reaching 4.5:1 against --color-background.
- 30 call sites, enumerated in the description. Menu items (EntryList.tsx:318, FeedSidebar.tsx:1003/1096/1146/1445) use text-destructive twice each via focus:/hover: variants — both halves move.
- ContextMenuItem variant="destructive" (FeedSidebar.tsx:1465) and Button variant="destructive" (FeedSidebar.tsx:1035, EditFeedDialog.tsx:656) are FILLS and must NOT change.
- badge.tsx's destructive variant: x7fn already moved its text-white to text-destructive-foreground. It is a fill, so it stays on the fill token and is out of scope for this change. It renders nowhere today.
- Closing this requires adding the new token to CONTRAST_PAIRS in e2e/settings.spec.ts across all five palettes and removing the exclusion comment that points here.

title: CI does not install Firefox, so every firefox-project E2E test errors: ci.yml installs chromium only
description:
main is RED because of this, and it was introduced by this session.

.github/workflows/ci.yml:159 runs:

  npx playwright install --with-deps chromium

Commit 9eab561 (ttrb-mq4n work) added a `firefox` project to playwright.config.ts so a Firefox-only bug could be covered. The binary is never installed on the runner, so every test in that project errors:

  Error: browserType.launch: Executable doesn t exist at
  /home/runner/.cache/ms-playwright/firefox-1538/firefox/firefox
