Observed on CI run 33281382078 (push of 9eab561): scan_ruby, test, test_js and lint all PASS; test_e2e is the only failing job, and every failure is this one cause. Run 33291841698 (push of a19e02f) was in progress at filing time and will fail identically.

Locally the suite is green (274 passed / 5 skipped) because this machine has the Firefox binary from `npx playwright install firefox`, run during ttrb-ngol. That divergence is why it was not caught before the push: local green and CI red have different browser inventories.

Fix, one line:

  npx playwright install --with-deps chromium firefox

Weigh the cost before widening further: Firefox currently runs only the three browse-mode specs (playwright.config.ts scopes it), so the added CI time is small. ttrb-6yuw covers widening Firefox to the whole suite and should NOT be folded in here — this ticket is only about making the browsers that are already configured actually available.

Acceptance criteria:
- A CI run on main is green.
- The firefox project runs on CI rather than erroring, and its test count in the CI log matches what the same command produces locally.
- No change to playwright.config.ts scoping.

Also worth doing while in this file: the step is named "Install Playwright browser", singular. Make it plural so the next person does not read the name and assume one browser is intended.

Related: ttrb-oprt (P2) also edits ci.yml, to move actions/setup-node@v4 and actions/upload-artifact@v4 off deprecated Node 20. Doing both in one commit is reasonable and saves a CI cycle, but this one is the blocker and should not wait for that decision.

title: Mark-read does not reach search results: useEntrySearch owns its result rows and exposes no way to update them
description:
Reported by Andy: "I would like the mark read to affect the filtered list when using the search feature."

Current behavior
useEntrySearch holds its own result state (results: SearchResult[], hooks line 173) and its return object (line 294) exposes results read-only. There is no setter, no per-row update, no invalidate. Nothing outside the hook can change a result row.

Every read-state mutation in application.tsx writes to the OTHER list. handleToggleRead (line 460), the star, published and score handlers (479, 494, 510), mark-all-read (567) and loadEntry auto-mark-on-open (357) all call setEntries(...) and none of them touch entrySearch.results.

So while a search is active:
- Marking an article read leaves its search row still showing unread.
- The row stays in the result set even when it no longer matches the search scope.
- Opening a result is enough to cause it: loadEntry marks read on open, so the inconsistency appears without the reader taking any deliberate action.

Why the scope part matters here specifically
entriesQuery sets unread: true whenever the entries_hide_read preference is on (application.tsx:256), and searchListScope is built from entriesQuery, so the search inherits unread: true. The search then genuinely IS an unread-only query, and a row that has just been marked read no longer satisfies the filter the pill on screen is claiming. That is the "filtered list" Andy means.

Two halves, one certain and one to decide

Certain, do this regardless: the row must reflect its own state. Marking read, starred, or published while a search is active has to update the corresponding SearchResult. Note SearchResult is NOT the Entry shape the list uses; it carries id (the user_entry id), entry_id, unread, starred and snippet, so the update maps by id rather than reusing the Entry updater wholesale. The hook needs to expose a targeted updater rather than having application.tsx reach into its state.

To decide: whether a row that stops matching the scope is REMOVED from the results, or stays put with its state updated. Arguments both ways:
- Remove. It is what "affect the filtered list" asks for literally, and it keeps the result set honest against the scope pill beside it.
- Keep. It matches what the main list already does: handleToggleRead maps over entries and updates in place; read articles only disappear from the main list on the next load, they are not yanked out from under the reader. Removing rows only in search would make search behave unlike the list it inherited its scope from, and an article vanishing the instant you open it is disorienting.

Recommendation: update in place, and reconcile on the next search request, matching the main list. If Andy wants rows removed, that is a deliberate divergence from list behaviour and should be applied to both or neither.

Affected files
- app/javascript/hooks/useEntrySearch.ts (expose a per-row updater)
- app/javascript/application.tsx (the five mutation handlers plus loadEntry)
- app/javascript/components/EntryList.tsx (if removal is chosen)

Acceptance criteria
- With a search active, marking an article read updates its row immediately.
- The same holds for starred and published.
- Opening a search result, which auto-marks read, leaves the row consistent.
- Mark-all-read while a search is active does not leave stale unread rows.
- Whichever removal behaviour is chosen is the same in search and in the main list, or the difference is documented in the code with its reason.
- Vitest coverage for the updater and for the mark-read-while-searching path.

title: SidebarDrawer calls useCallback and two useEffects after an early return on layout.isMobile
description:
app/javascript/components/mobile/SidebarDrawer.tsx:15-17 returns <>{children}</> when !layout.isMobile, before useCallback (line 22) and the two useEffects (31, 36). A mounted instance that saw isMobile flip would go from 1 hook to 4 and React would throw 'Rendered more hooks than during the previous render'.

Latent rather than live: application.tsx:1061 renders SidebarDrawer only inside the layout.isMobile ternary, and the other branch is a plain div, so crossing the 640px breakpoint changes the element type and unmounts the component instead of re-rendering it. It is the only call site (grep for SidebarDrawer). Any second call site that renders it unconditionally would crash on a resize across the breakpoint.

Fix is to move the early return below the hooks. Noticed while judging SidebarDrawer for ttrb-fuky and deliberately not folded into that commit, since it is a separate defect from the listener race.

The project has no eslint config at all (no .eslintrc*, no eslint.config.*, no lint script in package.json), so react-hooks/rules-of-hooks is not enforced anywhere. That is the reason this survived, and probably worth its own ticket.

title: Support -term negative search by swapping plainto_tsquery for websearch_to_tsquery
description:
Andy: "I would like the search feature to accept -<term> to indicate negative searches, that is dont show me entries with <term> in it."

PostgreSQL already does this. Verified on the dev database (PostgreSQL 15.8, so websearch_to_tsquery has been available since 11):

  select websearch_to_tsquery(%english%, %climate -oil%)::text
  => %climat% & !%oil%

Current behavior
Entry.tsquery_sql (app/models/entry.rb:109) builds plainto_tsquery(%english%, <quoted query>). plainto_tsquery deliberately ignores all operators: it tokenises the input and ANDs every lexeme. A leading hyphen is discarded as a separator, so searching "climate -oil" today returns articles about climate AND oil, the exact opposite of the intent.

The change
Swap the one function in tsquery_sql. It is the single place the query text becomes a tsquery, and all three consumers go through it: text_search_condition (line 81), text_search_rank (line 85) and text_search_headline (line 100). So negation reaches the WHERE clause, the relevance ordering and the snippet highlighting in one edit, consistently. connection.quote stays exactly as it is; it is what keeps this safe, per the comment already at line 103.

Things that arrive with the swap, whether or not they were asked for
websearch_to_tsquery is a whole mini-syntax, not just negation. It also accepts "quoted phrases" for adjacency and the bare word or for alternation. Those become live features the moment this lands. Decide whether to document them or suppress them; documenting is cheaper than pretending they are not there, since a reader who types a quoted phrase will get phrase behaviour either way.

Plain multi-word queries are unaffected: websearch_to_tsquery ANDs bare terms exactly as plainto_tsquery does, so existing searches keep their current results.

Guard needed: the pure-negative query
"-oil" alone produces !%oil%, which matches every article that does not mention oil. That is a legitimate tsquery but the GIN index (entries_tsvector_combined_idx) cannot serve a pure negation, so it degrades to a scan of the shared entries table, and the result set is "almost everything" in any case. Require at least one positive term, and say so in the UI rather than running it. Check what websearch_to_tsquery returns for a query that is nothing but negations before deciding how to detect this.

UI
The syntax is invisible unless the search box says it exists. A hint in the placeholder or an affordance beside the input is part of this bead, not a follow-up; a search feature with an undiscoverable operator is a search feature without the operator.

Affected files
- app/models/entry.rb (tsquery_sql, and the surrounding comments, which currently reason explicitly about plainto_tsquery behaviour and would go stale)
- the search box component (placeholder or syntax hint)
- test/models/entry_test.rb

Acceptance criteria
- "climate -oil" returns articles matching climate and not matching oil.
- Stemming still applies on both sides: -studies excludes an article that says study.
- Negated terms are not marked in the ts_headline snippet.
- Existing plain multi-word searches return the same results as before the swap.
- A query with no positive term is rejected with a message, not executed.
- The syntax is discoverable from the search UI.
- Model tests cover negation, a quoted phrase, or, and the pure-negative rejection.
